Termination. This Agreement may be terminated as follows:

Material Breach. This Agreement (in its entirety) may be terminated by either Party (the “Nonbreaching Party”) upon written notice thereof to the other Party (the “Breaching Party”) in the event of a material breach of this Agreement by the Breaching Party which is not cured within sixty (60) days after the receipt by the Breaching Party of written notice from the Nonbreaching Party, specifying in reasonable detail the nature of such breach. If such breach is not cured within such cure period, this Agreement shall terminate as set forth in the Nonbreaching Party’s notice of breach and in accordance with the terms of this Article; provided, however, that this Agreement shall not be terminated prior to the end of such cure period.

Insolvency. This Agreement may be terminated by either Party upon sixty (60) days’ prior written notice to the other Party at any time during this Agreement if the other Party: (a) files in any court pursuant to any statute a petition in bankruptcy or insolvency or for reorganization or for an arrangement or for the appointment of a receiver or trustee of the other Party, or of its assets; (b) proposes a written agreement of composition for extension of its debts; (c) is served with an involuntary petition against it, filed in any insolvency proceeding, and such petition shall not be dismissed within sixty (60) days after filing thereof; or (d) makes an assignment for the benefit of its creditors. The Party affected shall immediately notify the other Party in writing of the occurrence of any of the foregoing events.

playbookClauses.text: Dispute Resolution. Subject to Section 12.5.4 below, any dispute between the Parties arising out of, related to or in connection with this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively by invoking the following dispute resolution procedures:

The Parties agree to make a diligent, good faith effort to resolve all disputes amicably if at all possible. To this end, authorized representatives of each Party shall meet within fifteen (15) days after receipt of written notice by either Party at a mutually agreeable time and place to discuss possible resolution of the dispute.

In the event that the Parties are unable to resolve the dispute within fifteen (15) days after their meeting, then either Party may invoke non-binding mediation under the International Institute for Conflict Prevention & Resolution (“CPR”) Mediation Procedure then in effect . Unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties, the Parties will select a single mediator from the CPR Panels of Distinguished Neutrals. The mediation proceeding shall be conducted in New York, New York, or such other location as may be agreed in writing by the Parties. The Parties shall (a) share equally the fees and expenses of the mediator; and (b) bear their own attorneys’ fees and associated costs and expenses. At the request of either Party, the mediator shall enter an appropriate protective order to maintain the confidentiality of information produced or exchanged in the course of the mediation proceedings. The Parties shall use their best efforts to complete the mediation procedure provided for in this Section 12.5 within no more than sixty (60) days.

After (i) completion of the process described in Section 12.5.1 and Section 12.5.2 above or (ii) the non-cooperation of either Party in the completion of the stated procedure, then either Party (in the case of clause (i)) or the cooperating Party (in the case of clause (ii)) may initiate an action in court against the other, but such action may only be brought in a court having jurisdiction pursuant to Section 12.6 of this Agreement. All applicable statutes of limitation and defenses based upon the passage of time shall be tolled while the process described in Section 12.5.1 and Section 12.5.2 above is pending. The Parties shall take such action, if any, required to effectuate such tolling.

Nothing in this Section 12.5 shall be construed to prevent either Party from seeking injunctive relief against the other Party from any judicial or administrative authority of competent jurisdiction to enjoin such other Party from breaching any provision of this Agreement pending the resolution of a dispute as hereinbefore provided.

Venue. All disputes arising out of this Agreement (and all amendments and attachments hereto) shall be exclusively resolved in a court of competent jurisdiction in the State of New York. Each Party expressly consents to the jurisdiction of the state or federal courts in the State of New York and waives any objections or right as to forum non conveniens, lack of personal jurisdiction or similar grounds. Each Party hereby irrevocably and unconditionally waives all right to trial by jury in any action (whether based on contract, tort or otherwise) arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or its performance under or the enforcement of this Agreement.

GLOBAL ANTI-BRIBERY POLICY
Our Anti-Bribery Commitment

Colgate’s commitment to dealing legally and ethically applies worldwide. We comply with all applicable anti-bribery laws, including but not limited to the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (“FCPA”), everywhere we do business, and we expect the same of the third parties with whom we work. While the FCPA prohibits, among other things, bribery of foreign government officials and entities, other anti-bribery laws, like the UK Bribery Act, prohibit commercial bribery between private individuals and entities.

Colgate people and any third parties acting on our behalf or in connection with our business are prohibited from giving or offering anything of value directly or indirectly to any government official or entity, or to any private individual or entity, in order to improperly obtain or retain any business advantage or to improperly affect any act or decision.

This prohibition includes any facilitating, expediting or “grease” payments made to government officials, either directly or indirectly, in order to expedite any official service or function (for example, small payments made to an official to move Colgate’s application to the front of the line or to shorten the time frame in which services or other actions are provided). Any official fees supported by government-issued receipts do not qualify as improper payments.
Maintaining Accurate Books and Records

No payment by or on behalf of the Company shall be approved or made if any part of the payment is to be used for an unlawful or improper purpose, or for any purpose other than that described by valid documents supporting the payment. No false or misleading entries should be made in any books or financial records of the Company for any reason.

Any expenses that an employee or third party incurs on Colgate’s behalf or in connection with our business shall not be reimbursable unless they are lawful and supported by detailed documentation including, for example, valid invoices or receipts.
Expenditures Related to Government Officials

No funds may be provided to or spent on behalf of a government official or entity, directly or indirectly, without advance written approval from Colgate’s Global Legal Organization. This includes any payments, gifts, donations, entertainment, travel, meals, or other items of value. (For additional information, please review the Global Policy on Expenditures Related to Government Officials & Governments.) Advance approval is not required for official fees supported by government-issued receipts (e.g., permit or license fees).

Please note that the term “government official” is widely defined and may include individuals who are employed by any public or state-affiliated institution or organization or who act in an official capacity in any way, whether full-time, part-time or unpaid. Government officials can be found in every branch and level of government and public life and may include anyone from low-level customs employees, to employees of state-owned media outlets, to high-ranking lawmakers, as well as researchers, professors, teachers, dentists, veterinarians, or other professionals and Key Thought Leaders. If you are in doubt as to whether an individual could be considered a government official, you should contact the Global Legal Organization.
Commercial Bribery

In addition to prohibiting bribery of government officials, Colgate also prohibits its employees and third parties from engaging in bribery of private parties. You should not seek to improperly influence the judgment or conduct of any party with whom you might be conducting Company business by offering or providing any payments, gifts or other benefits, or by any other unlawful inducement.
Our Expectations

Colgate’s reputation depends on the conduct of our employees as well as the conduct of those with whom we do business. It is our goal to ensure that Colgate People and the third parties with whom we work reflect the same high ethical standards and demonstrate a commitment to compliance with all applicable laws. We further expect our third parties to ensure that their employees and subcontractors understand and comply with this Anti-Bribery Policy.

Failure to comply with this Anti-Bribery Policy or any applicable anti-bribery laws, including but not limited to the FCPA, may result in civil or criminal penalties, as well as termination of the employment or business relationship.
Any questions regarding this policy may be directed to our Global Compliance Legal Specialist: Legal_Compliance@colpal.com

clauses.text: Research Project Managers. Each Party hereby appoints the Research Project manager for such Party set forth in Exhibit B (each, a “Research Project Manager”) to act as the primary contact for such Party in connection with matters related to the Research Project. Either Party may replace its Research Project Manager at any time by providing written notice to the other Party. Researcher’s Research Project Manager shall keep Colgate’s Research Project Manager apprised of the status of the Research Project and of the various Research Steps at all times. The Research Project Managers will meet at least [●], or more frequently as agreed by the Research Project Managers, and such meetings may be held by videoconference or telephone conference.

Compliance with Policies While On-Site. While at the offices or facilities of Colgate and its Affiliates, Researcher and its Representatives shall comply with all applicable policies and procedures of Colgate (including security policies and procedures) as provided to Researcher and its Representatives in writing or explained in a formal course on security.

clauses.text: Fees. In consideration of Researcher’s performance of the Research Project, Colgate shall pay to Researcher the fees as set forth in the Project Description (the “Fees”). Researcher agrees to establish an account with Colgate’s electronic invoicing provider for the submission and payment of all invoices. After the Fees have become due, as set forth in the Project Description, Researcher shall submit an invoice electronically. All undisputed Fees shall be payable by Colgate within ninety (90) days after Colgate’s receipt of an acceptable invoice for such Fees from Researcher; provided that Researcher may only issue such an invoice after such Fees have become due pursuant to the Project Description. All payments will be made by Colgate to Researcher via a wire transfer. Any sales, use, excise, value-added or other taxes or duties and penalties and interest relating thereto shall be the sole responsibility of Researcher.

No Other Costs. Except as otherwise set forth in the Project Description, all direct and indirect costs and expenses (including any travel costs, legal and other advisory fees and other Third-Party costs) in connection with this Agreement incurred by Researcher or its Representatives shall be borne solely by Researcher, and Colgate shall have no obligation to reimburse Researcher for any such costs or expenses.

Researcher shall maintain complete and accurate records of, and supporting documentation for, all Fees billable to and payments made by Colgate hereunder in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. Researcher shall provide Colgate with reasonable documentation and other information for each invoice as may be reasonably requested by Colgate.

Colgate or its Representatives may audit the books and records of Researcher to verify Fees paid or payable in accordance with this Agreement. Colgate’s right to audit Researcher’s books and records for any calendar year shall expire twelve (12) months after the end of such calendar year. [Colgate shall pay the costs of the auditors conducting such audit, unless the results of an audit reveal an overpayment of Fees of five percent (5%) or more, in which case, Researcher shall pay the costs of the auditors conducting such audit and Colgate’s out-of-pocket costs of conducting such audit. If the audit concludes that an overpayment has occurred during the audited period, such payment shall be remitted by Researcher to Colgate within thirty (30) days after the date such auditor’s written report identifying the overpayment is delivered to Researcher, together with interest of two percent (2%) per month from the date of overpayment (or the maximum amount of interest permitted by applicable law if lower).

Ownership of Deliverables and Data. All Deliverables (including data, information and work in progress resulting from the conduct of the Research Project) shall be the exclusive property of Colgate, shall be considered Colgate Confidential Information and shall be subject to Colgate’s exclusive use, commercial or otherwise. Researcher hereby assigns, and shall cause its Affiliates and its and their Representatives and subcontractors to assign, to Colgate the entire right, title and interest in and to all Deliverables.

Background IP. All Background IP shall be and remain exclusively the property of the Party that made or acquired such Background IP. Except as set forth in Article 7, neither Party has any right or license to any of the other Party’s Background IP.

clauses.text: Research Project IP.

Ownership. Colgate shall exclusively own all right, title and interest in and to all Research Project IP. Researcher hereby assigns, and shall cause its Affiliates and its and their Representatives and subcontractors to assign, to Colgate the entire right, title and interest in and to all Research Project IP. If Researcher is not permitted by applicable Law to assign any Research Project IP to Colgate, Researcher hereby grants Colgate a perpetual, irrevocable, exclusive (even as to Researcher), world-wide, royalty-free, freely-assignable license in all fields to such Research Project IP (including the right to sell and grant sublicenses (through multiple tiers) to such Research Project IP) and agrees not to bring any action, claim or proceeding against Colgate or any of its sublicensees or assignees for its use or exploitation of such Research Project IP. Colgate shall have the exclusive right to prepare and file applications for, prosecute, maintain, defend and assert, at its own costs, the Research Project IP. Researcher shall reasonably assist and cooperate with Colgate at Colgate’s expense in perfecting, maintaining and defending the rights granted to Colgate in this Section 5.3.1, including the provision of any requested documentation necessary for prosecution or maintenance of patents claiming such Research Project IP, and the execution of any required documents therefor. Unless obligated by applicable Law, Researcher shall not file any patent applications claiming, or amend any patent applications to claim, any Research Project IP. If despite the foregoing, Researcher files any patent applications claiming, or amends any patent applications to claim, any Research Project IP, Researcher agrees to assign such patent applications to Colgate.

Disclosure. Upon delivery of any Deliverable, Researcher shall provide to Colgate a written report detailing any Research Project IP developed in connection with or embodied in the Deliverable. Researcher shall include in its written report a reasonable level of detail regarding the applicable Research Project IP and shall provide such additional information on the Research Project IP as is reasonably requested by Colgate.

Enforcement. Colgate shall have the exclusive right to bring and control any claim, action or proceeding related to the infringement, misappropriation or other violation of any Research Project IP, and shall retain all damages, recoveries and other amounts awarded in connection therewith. Researcher shall reasonably assist and cooperate with Colgate in bringing a claim, action or proceeding pursuant to this Section 5.3.3, at Colgate’s expense, including the provision or execution of any requested documentation. Researcher acknowledges that it may be a necessary party to any claim, action or proceeding brought by Colgate arising from enforcement of any Research Project IP and, if necessary, Researcher shall participate in such claim, action or proceeding, at Colgate’s request.

clauses.text: Use of Names and Trademarks. Neither Party nor its Affiliates shall make any oral or written statement or perform any act indicating that the other Party or its Affiliates endorses or approves, or has endorsed or approved, such Party or its products or services. Nothing contained in this Agreement will be construed as conferring any right to use in advertising, publicity or other promotional activities any name, trade name, trademark, service mark or other designation of a Party (including any contraction, abbreviation or simulation of any of the foregoing) without the prior written approval of such Party.

Publications. Any proposed electronic, oral, or written disclosure, including, but not limited to, abstracts, manuscripts, presentations and publications, by Researcher referring to the Research Project (“Publications”) shall be submitted by Researcher to Colgate for review and approval ninety (90) days prior to submission for publication. No Publication shall be undertaken without such approval. Colgate may withhold approval at Colgate’s sole discretion. It is understood and agreed that all Publications which Researcher publishes with Colgate’s permission based on information obtained from the Research Project may, at Colgate’s sole discretion, carry a statement that the Research Project was supported by Colgate-Palmolive Company.

License to Researcher Background IP and Confidential Information. Researcher, on behalf of itself and its Affiliates, grants to Colgate and Colgate’s Affiliates a non-exclusive, royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide license to practice and otherwise fully exploit all Researcher Background IP and Researcher Confidential Information, including to manufacture, have manufactured, use, import, sell or offer for sale any product or service or practice any method, in any and all fields to the extent incorporated into, or otherwise necessary or useful to exploit, any Research Project IP or Deliverable. For the avoidance of doubt, expiration or termination of this Agreement shall not terminate or limit Colgate’s rights under this Section 7.1.

clauses.text: Indemnification Claims. Colgate agrees to give Researcher prompt written notice of any matter upon which any indemnified Person intends to base a claim for indemnification (an “Indemnity Claim”) under this Article 9, provided, however, that any delay in providing or failure to provide such notice shall not relieve Researcher of any of its obligations hereunder except to the extent that Researcher is materially prejudiced by such failure. Researcher shall have the right to participate jointly with the indemnified Person in the indemnified Person’s defense, settlement or other disposition of any Indemnity Claim. With respect to any Indemnity Claim relating solely to the payment of money damages which could not result in the indemnified Person becoming subject to injunctive or other equitable relief or otherwise adversely affect the business of the indemnified Person in any manner, and as to which Researcher shall have acknowledged in writing the obligation to indemnify the indemnified Person hereunder, Researcher shall have the sole right to defend, settle or otherwise dispose of such Indemnity Claim, on such terms as Researcher, in its sole discretion, shall deem appropriate; provided that Researcher shall provide reasonable evidence of its ability to pay any damages claimed and with respect to any such settlement shall have obtained the written release of the indemnified Person from the Indemnity Claim. Researcher shall obtain the written consent of the indemnified Person, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, prior to ceasing to defend, settling or otherwise disposing of any Indemnity Claim if as a result thereof the indemnified Person would become subject to injunctive or other equitable relief or the business of the indemnified Person would be adversely affected in any manner.

Obligations of Confidentiality. The Receiving Party shall (a) maintain any Confidential Information in confidence; (b) take all necessary and reasonable precautions to prevent Confidential Information from being disclosed to any unauthorized third party, which shall include open artificial intelligence platforms (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini), and (c) use Confidential Information exclusively for performing any task or obligations described in the Project Description or otherwise in accordance with any licenses granted hereunder, as applicable. The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to its Representatives and permitted subcontractors, each with a need to know such Confidential Information in order to perform any task or obligations described in the Project Description or otherwise in accordance with any licenses granted hereunder; provided that (i) the Receiving Party advises its Representatives and permitted subcontractors of the confidential nature thereof and (ii) such Representatives and permitted subcontractors are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as stringent as those set forth herein (for subcontractors, the confidentiality terms must be approved in writing by Colgate, as set forth in Section 2.4). The Receiving Party shall be liable to the Disclosing Party for any failure by any of its Representatives or permitted subcontractors to comply with this Article 10 with respect to the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information in the same manner as the Receiving Party is obligated to treat such Confidential Information under the terms of this Agreement.
Exclusions. Confidential Information shall not include information that the Receiving Party demonstrates:
is in the public domain as of the Effective Date, or subsequently enters the public domain through no fault or act of the Receiving Party;

is known to the Receiving Party prior to disclosure from the Disclosing Party[; provided that such information was not acquired from the Disclosing Party under one of the Prior Non-Disclosure Agreements if such information is still to be treated as confidential under such Prior Non-Disclosure Agreement;]
that the Receiving Party received from any third party not under any obligation to the Disclosing Party to keep such information confidential; and
was independently developed by the Receiving Party without reliance upon or use of the Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party.

In the event that the Receiving Party receives a subpoena or other government process that purports to require the production of any Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party for use in an action or proceeding or for any purpose other than for performing any task or obligations described in the Project Description or in connection with any licenses granted hereunder, the Receiving Party shall (a) promptly inform the party or entity issuing such subpoena or other government process of the existence of this Agreement, (b) promptly inform the Disclosing Party of the receipt of such subpoena or other government process and (c) not oppose any effort by the Disclosing Party to quash any such subpoena or other government process. In the event that (x) the Disclosing Party fails to intervene to quash such subpoena or other government process after being given notice and a reasonable opportunity to do so or (y) such intervention fails or is denied by a court of competent jurisdiction, such Confidential Information may be produced but limited to what is strictly necessary, notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary.

In the event that the Receiving Party believes it is required by applicable Law or stock exchange rules to disclose any part of the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information, the Receiving Party shall: (a) promptly advise the Disclosing Party of each such requirement in writing and identify the documents so required thereby, so that the Disclosing Party may seek an appropriate protective order or other remedy or waive compliance by the Receiving Party with the provisions of this Agreement; and (b) consult with the Disclosing Party on the advisability of taking legally available steps to resist or narrow the scope of such requirement. If, in the absence of such a protective order or such a waiver by the Disclosing Party of the provisions of this Agreement, the Receiving Party is nonetheless required by mandatory applicable Law to disclose any part of the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information, the Receiving Party may disclose such Confidential Information without liability under this Agreement, except that the Receiving Party shall furnish only that portion of the Confidential Information which is legally required.

In the event that any Confidential Information is produced or disclosed pursuant to this Section 10.3.3, such Confidential Information shall not lose its confidential status through such use, and the Receiving Party shall take all reasonable and necessary steps to protect the confidentiality of such Confidential Information during such use.

Terms of Agreement. Subject to Section 10.2 and Section 10.3, neither Party shall, without the prior written consent of the other Party, disclose in any manner to any Third Party the existence and the terms and conditions of this Agreement.

Trade Secrets. No Disclosing Party shall disclose any “trade secrets” to the Receiving Party pursuant to this Agreement, unless: (a) such Confidential Information is clearly marked as a “trade secret” of the Disclosing Party and (b) the Receiving Party has separately agreed in writing to the receipt of such “trade secret.” In connection with the disclosure of any “trade secret,” the Disclosing Party may also condition such disclosure on additional confidentiality obligations and disclosure limitations that must be agreed upon in writing by the Parties, such as limitation of disclosure to a defined group of individual Representatives of the Receiving Party.

clauses.text: Survival. The mutual obligations of confidentiality and non-use under this Article 10 shall survive the expiration and earlier termination of this Agreement for a period of [two (2) years] after its expiration or earlier termination.

Term. This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and, unless terminated earlier pursuant to this Article, shall continue in force and effect until the [earlier/later] of [●]or completion by both Parties of all tasks and obligations set forth the Project Description (the “Term”).
Termination. This Agreement may be terminated as follows:

Material Breach. This Agreement (in its entirety) may be terminated by either Party (the “Nonbreaching Party”) upon written notice thereof to the other Party (the “Breaching Party”) in the event of a material breach of this Agreement by the Breaching Party which is not cured within sixty (60) days after the receipt by the Breaching Party of written notice from the Nonbreaching Party, specifying in reasonable detail the nature of such breach. If such breach is not cured within such cure period, this Agreement shall terminate as set forth in the Nonbreaching Party’s notice of breach and in accordance with the terms of this Article; provided, however, that this Agreement shall not be terminated prior to the end of such cure period.

Insolvency. This Agreement may be terminated by either Party upon sixty (60) days’ prior written notice to the other Party at any time during this Agreement if the other Party: (a) files in any court pursuant to any statute a petition in bankruptcy or insolvency or for reorganization or for an arrangement or for the appointment of a receiver or trustee of the other Party, or of its assets; (b) proposes a written agreement of composition for extension of its debts; (c) is served with an involuntary petition against it, filed in any insolvency proceeding, and such petition shall not be dismissed within sixty (60) days after filing thereof; or (d) makes an assignment for the benefit of its creditors. The Party affected shall immediately notify the other Party in writing of the occurrence of any of the foregoing events.

For Convenience. This Agreement may be terminated by Colgate for any or no reason by providing Researcher with written notice at least thirty (30) days prior to the desired effective date of termination. If Colgate elects to terminate this Agreement pursuant to this Section 11.2.3, Researcher shall be entitled to receive Fees for the Research Steps performed until the termination date of this Agreement but Colgate shall have no other liability to Researcher as a result of such termination of this Agreement.

Consequences of Termination. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement:

each Party shall either (at the sole discretion of such Party) deliver to the other Party or destroy all Confidential Information and original technical data and technology supplied by the other Party pursuant to this Agreement to such Party; provided, however, that each Party may retain an archival copy or other appropriate record (including electronic backup copies created in the ordinary course) of any such Confidential Information. Such copies and records may be used exclusively for internal recordkeeping and administrative purposes, to assure compliance with any applicable Governmental Authority requirements and for dispute resolution purposes;

Researcher shall, in accordance with such Colgate’s instructions, deliver to Colgate: (i) all materials, products or equipment of Colgate previously provided to Researcher in connection with the Research Project, including the Materials pursuant to this Agreement; and (ii) all Deliverables (including Deliverables in progress) developed under this Agreement; and

All Fees advanced by Colgate to Researcher and not earned by Researcher under this Agreement shall be reimbursed by Researcher to Colgate within sixty (60) days after the effective date of termination.

Survival. All provisions under this Agreement which by their terms survive, or by their nature should survive, expiration or any earlier termination of this Agreement shall survive any such expiration or termination, including Article 1, Section 4.3, Article 5, Article 6, Section 7.1, Section 8.7, Article 9, Article 10, Section 11.4, this Section 11.5 and Article 12.

Force Majeure. No liability shall result to Colgate or Researcher from any delay in performance or from non-performance caused by acts of God, fire, flood, explosion, war, action or request of governmental authority, or any other unforeseeable circumstances of a similar nature beyond the reasonable control of the Party affected; provided that the delayed or nonperforming Party (i) promptly notifies the other Party of the existence of such cause and its probable duration and (ii) makes all reasonable efforts to prevent, limit and remove the effects of such cause (“Force Majeure”). [In the event of a Force Majeure that continues for thirty (30) days or more, Colgate may terminate this Agreement immediately upon notice as per Section 12.2 to Researcher.]

Notices. The Parties shall deliver all notices, claims, demands, consents, approvals and other communications under this Agreement (each, a “Notice”) in writing and in English, referring to this Agreement and addressed to the other Party at its address below or to the last address the receiving Party provided to the other Party in compliance with this section. The Parties shall deliver any Notice by personal delivery, reputable overnight courier (all fees prepaid), certified or registered mail (postage prepaid, return receipt requested) or by email. clauses.text: Dispute Resolution. Subject to Section 12.5.4 below, any dispute between the Parties arising out of, related to or in connection with this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively by invoking the following dispute resolution procedures:

The Parties agree to make a diligent, good faith effort to resolve all disputes amicably if at all possible. To this end, authorized representatives of each Party shall meet within fifteen (15) days after receipt of written notice by either Party at a mutually agreeable time and place to discuss possible resolution of the dispute.

In the event that the Parties are unable to resolve the dispute within fifteen (15) days after their meeting, then either Party may invoke non-binding mediation under the International Institute for Conflict Prevention & Resolution (“CPR”) Mediation Procedure then in effect . Unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties, the Parties will select a single mediator from the CPR Panels of Distinguished Neutrals. The mediation proceeding shall be conducted in New York, New York, or such other location as may be agreed in writing by the Parties. The Parties shall (a) share equally the fees and expenses of the mediator; and (b) bear their own attorneys’ fees and associated costs and expenses. At the request of either Party, the mediator shall enter an appropriate protective order to maintain the confidentiality of information produced or exchanged in the course of the mediation proceedings. The Parties shall use their best efforts to complete the mediation procedure provided for in this Section 12.5 within no more than sixty (60) days.

After (i) completion of the process described in Section 12.5.1 and Section 12.5.2 above or (ii) the non-cooperation of either Party in the completion of the stated procedure, then either Party (in the case of clause (i)) or the cooperating Party (in the case of clause (ii)) may initiate an action in court against the other, but such action may only be brought in a court having jurisdiction pursuant to Section 12.6 of this Agreement. All applicable statutes of limitation and defenses based upon the passage of time shall be tolled while the process described in Section 12.5.1 and Section 12.5.2 above is pending. The Parties shall take such action, if any, required to effectuate such tolling.

Nothing in this Section 12.5 shall be construed to prevent either Party from seeking injunctive relief against the other Party from any judicial or administrative authority of competent jurisdiction to enjoin such other Party from breaching any provision of this Agreement pending the resolution of a dispute as hereinbefore provided.

GLOBAL ANTI-BRIBERY POLICY
Our Anti-Bribery Commitment

Colgate’s commitment to dealing legally and ethically applies worldwide. We comply with all applicable anti-bribery laws, including but not limited to the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (“FCPA”), everywhere we do business, and we expect the same of the third parties with whom we work. While the FCPA prohibits, among other things, bribery of foreign government officials and entities, other anti-bribery laws, like the UK Bribery Act, prohibit commercial bribery between private individuals and entities.

Colgate people and any third parties acting on our behalf or in connection with our business are prohibited from giving or offering anything of value directly or indirectly to any government official or entity, or to any private individual or entity, in order to improperly obtain or retain any business advantage or to improperly affect any act or decision.

This prohibition includes any facilitating, expediting or “grease” payments made to government officials, either directly or indirectly, in order to expedite any official service or function (for example, small payments made to an official to move Colgate’s application to the front of the line or to shorten the time frame in which services or other actions are provided). Any official fees supported by government-issued receipts do not qualify as improper payments.
Maintaining Accurate Books and Records

No payment by or on behalf of the Company shall be approved or made if any part of the payment is to be used for an unlawful or improper purpose, or for any purpose other than that described by valid documents supporting the payment. No false or misleading entries should be made in any books or financial records of the Company for any reason.

Any expenses that an employee or third party incurs on Colgate’s behalf or in connection with our business shall not be reimbursable unless they are lawful and supported by detailed documentation including, for example, valid invoices or receipts.
Expenditures Related to Government Officials

No funds may be provided to or spent on behalf of a government official or entity, directly or indirectly, without advance written approval from Colgate’s Global Legal Organization. This includes any payments, gifts, donations, entertainment, travel, meals, or other items of value. (For additional information, please review the Global Policy on Expenditures Related to Government Officials & Governments.) Advance approval is not required for official fees supported by government-issued receipts (e.g., permit or license fees).

Please note that the term “government official” is widely defined and may include individuals who are employed by any public or state-affiliated institution or organization or who act in an official capacity in any way, whether full-time, part-time or unpaid. Government officials can be found in every branch and level of government and public life and may include anyone from low-level customs employees, to employees of state-owned media outlets, to high-ranking lawmakers, as well as researchers, professors, teachers, dentists, veterinarians, or other professionals and Key Thought Leaders. If you are in doubt as to whether an individual could be considered a government official, you should contact the Global Legal Organization.
Commercial Bribery

In addition to prohibiting bribery of government officials, Colgate also prohibits its employees and third parties from engaging in bribery of private parties. You should not seek to improperly influence the judgment or conduct of any party with whom you might be conducting Company business by offering or providing any payments, gifts or other benefits, or by any other unlawful inducement.
Our Expectations

Colgate’s reputation depends on the conduct of our employees as well as the conduct of those with whom we do business. It is our goal to ensure that Colgate People and the third parties with whom we work reflect the same high ethical standards and demonstrate a commitment to compliance with all applicable laws. We further expect our third parties to ensure that their employees and subcontractors understand and comply with this Anti-Bribery Policy.

Failure to comply with this Anti-Bribery Policy or any applicable anti-bribery laws, including but not limited to the FCPA, may result in civil or criminal penalties, as well as termination of the employment or business relationship.
Any questions regarding this policy may be directed to our Global Compliance Legal Specialist: Legal_Compliance@colpal.com

articleGuidance.DEFINITIONS: Colgate’s primary watchouts center on protecting the integrity of its proprietary assets and managing administrative risks. A critical concern is the definition of Background IP, which includes intellectual property developed independently; Colgate must ensure the Researcher does not use this clause to inappropriately claim discoveries made during the project as pre-existing work. While the agreement wisely excludes Research Project IP from the definition of Researcher Confidential Information to safeguard Colgate's ownership rights , a significant operational risk exists regarding oral disclosures, which must be summarized in writing within 15 days to maintain confidential status. Furthermore, Colgate must ensure that any Prior Non-Disclosure Agreements are explicitly identified to avoid protection gaps for information shared during preliminary discussions. Finally, because Materials, Deliverables, and the existence and terms of the Agreement itself are all defined as Colgate Confidential Information, Colgate must maintain strict oversight of Exhibit A to ensure all provided items and project outputs are captured under these restrictive definitions.
articleGuidance.MANAGEMENT OF THE RESEARCH PROJECT: Management of the Research Project: establishes a critical oversight structure by mandating the appointment of Research Project Managers to act as the primary leads for both parties. Colgate’s protection in this section stems from the Researcher’s obligation to provide continuous status updates and participate in mandatory progress meetings to ensure the Research Steps are being followed. To maximize effectiveness, Colgate should ensure the meeting frequency is sufficient for active oversight and that all internal safety and security policies are provided to the Researcher in writing before any on-site visits occur. One watchout hereis preventing "scope creep" during informal management updates, as any actual changes to the agreement must still be formally documented and signed.
articleGuidance.FEES: establishes a controlled financial framework that prioritizes transparency and performance-based compensation. Colgate’s primary protections include a standard 90-day payment window—though payments may be negotiated within a net 45-90 range —the exclusion of any costs not pre-approved in Exhibit A , and robust Audit Rights that allow Colgate or its representatives to audit the books and records of the Researcher (the third party) to verify fees. To maximize security, Colgate must ensure that Exhibit A ties all payments to the formal acceptance of specific Milestones or Deliverables.
articleGuidance.INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY:
- Colgate must retain exclusive ownership of all Deliverables and raw Data generated during the Research Project.
- Background IP must remain the exclusive property of the originating Party, with no implied licenses granted to the other Party.
- Colgate requires exclusive ownership of all Research Project IP developed solely by Colgate or through its funding.
- We can agree to a license to any IP developed by researcher or University but if its a non-commercial license or non-exclusive, this must be approved by the requester after informing them of the risks.
- If forced to accept a non-exclusive or non-commercial license, Colgate must secure a formal option to negotiate an exclusive commercial arrangement with the option beginning when the IP is disclosed and we are formally notified that the option period has begun.
- Jointly developed Research Project IP should be jointly owned, provided ideally Colgate retains the exclusive right to control enforcement and commercialization.
- The counterparty must provide timely written disclosure of all Research Project IP developed in connection with any Deliverable.
- Colgate must maintain the exclusive right to initiate and control all legal proceedings regarding the infringement or misappropriation of Research Project IP.
- Neither Party may use the other Party’s name or trademarks for marketing or endorsement purposes without prior written consent.
articleGuidance.PUBLICATIONS: establishes a safeguard for Colgate’s proprietary interests by requiring a 45–90 day prior review and approval for most disclosures. For university researchers, the requirement shifts to a 30-45-day review-and-comment model where Colgate identifies and redacts its Confidential Information and reserves the right to delay publication for an additional 30–45 days for patent filings. While Colgate may not have editorial control over academic works, it must strictly enforce the removal of confidential information and ensure the researcher provides sufficient time for review and IP protection. Also crucially, this clause should never be made mutual. Colgate will not accept a where it has to send a publication for review to researcher.
articleGuidance.LICENSES: serves to guarantee Colgate’s \"freedom to operate\" by securing a worldwide, royalty-free license to any of the Researcher's Background IP necessary to exploit the project Deliverables. Colgate’s primary watchout is ensuring that its use of research results is never blocked by the Researcher's pre-existing patents; if a license is refused, the Researcher must formally warrant that no such Background IP will be embedded in the final outputs. While Colgate may grant a temporary license to the Researcher for project execution and educational rights, all commercial and use rights granted to Colgate must be perpetual and irrevocable to prevent future legal or financial obstacles. As a crucial extension of the IP strategy, if Colgate does not own the Research Project IP outright, it must secure a formal Option Right to negotiate an exclusive or commercial license. This is particularly critical when dealing with University partners, where securing automatic commercial rights is often a major hurdle. To ensure the timeline is manageable, the Option Period should only begin once the Researcher formally notifies Colgate in writing that all relevant IP has been fully disclosed and the window is officially open. This prevents the Researcher from prematurely starting the clock on Colgate's decision-making process before all technical details are available for review. Colgate should not provide a license to its background IP unless its solely for the conduct of the Research.

HOWEVER, may also need to be increased if research being conducted carries a higher degree of risk. Discuss with CP Risk Management to determine an appropriate level of coverage if unsure.

playbookClauses.text: This SERVICES AGREEMENT is entered into as of the date of the last signature below (the “Effective Date”) by and between Colgate-Palmolive Company, a Delaware corporation, having its principal offices at 300 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10022 (“Colgate”), and [●], a [●] organized under the laws of [●], having its principal offices at [●] (“Provider”). Colgate and Provider are sometimes hereinafter referred to collectively as the “Parties” and individually as a “Party.”
WHEREAS, Colgate desires to have Provider carry out services for Colgate or its Affiliates, as more specifically set forth in Exhibit A to this Agreement; and
WHEREAS, Colgate and Provider desire to enter into this Agreement to govern the provision and receipt of such services.
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the premises and the undertakings of the Parties hereinafter set forth, the Parties agree as follows:

“Affiliate” means, with respect to a Person, an individual, trust, business trust, joint venture, partnership, corporation, association or any other entity which (directly or indirectly) is controlled by, controls, or is under common control with a Person. For purposes of this definition, the term “control” (including, with correlative meanings, the term “controlled by” and “under common control with”) as used with respect to any Person, shall mean the possession (directly or indirectly) of power to direct or cause the direction of the management or policies of such Person.
“Agreement” means this Services Agreement and all Exhibits hereto, as the same may be amended or modified from time to time in accordance with the terms hereof.

“Background IP” means Intellectual Property under the control of a Party that was developed or acquired by the Party prior to the Effective Date or independently and outside the activities contemplated by this Agreement without reference to or use of the other Party’s Confidential Information or Background IP. For purposes of this definition, a Party “controls” Intellectual Property if it owns or otherwise has the right to license or sublicense such Intellectual Property.
“Breaching Party” is defined in Section 9.2.1.
“Claims” is defined in Section 7.1.
“Colgate” is defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Colgate Confidential Information” means (a) any information or data, whether technical or nontechnical, whether written (including graphic or electronic) and marked confidential or oral, disclosed by Colgate or its Affiliates or on Colgate’s behalf to Provider, either directly or indirectly, on or after the Effective Date [or previously under a Prior Non-Disclosure Agreement], and (b) the existence and terms of this Agreement. If Colgate Confidential Information is disclosed orally, Colgate shall provide a summary and confirm the confidential nature of such information in writing within fifteen (15) days after such oral disclosure. For the avoidance of doubt, Colgate Confidential Information shall include Foreground IP, Materials, Deliverables and [●].
“Confidential Information” means Colgate Confidential Information or Provider Confidential Information, as the context requires.
“Deliverables” is defined in Section 2.1.
“Disclosing Party” means the Party disclosing Confidential Information.
“Effective Date” is defined in the preamble to this Agreement.
“Fees” is defined in Section 3.1.
“Force Majeure” is defined in Section 10.1.

[“Foreground IP” means Intellectual Property that is created by the Representatives of either or both Parties while performing or receiving the Services under this Agreement, including, but not limited to, any Intellectual Property in the Deliverables.]

“Governmental Authority” means any legislative, executive or judicial unit of any governmental or quasi-governmental authority or instrumentality (multi-national, national, federal, state, provincial, local or foreign, international or domestic), or any department, agency, board, bureau, commission, official or other regulatory, administrative or judicial authority thereof, including any administrative or regulatory agency or commission, and any court or arbitration tribunal, in each instance having jurisdiction over the subject matter before it.
“Indemnity Claim” is defined in Section 7.2.

“Intellectual Property” means all discoveries, inventions, improvements, developments, procedures, processes, formulations, know-how, trade secrets, formulae, trademarks, service marks, trade dress, designs, logos, packaging, proprietary information, technical information, techniques, works of authorship, drawings, models, manuals and systems, whether or not patentable or copyrightable or otherwise registerable, and all rights and applications or registrations derived or derivable therefrom.

“Law” means all supranational, international, national, state and local laws, statutes, regulations, rules, codes or ordinances enacted, adopted, issued or promulgated by any Governmental Authority or common law.
“Materials” is defined in Section 2.4.
“Nonbreaching Party” is defined in Section 9.2.1.
"Notice” is defined in Section 10.2.
“Party” and “Parties” are defined in the preamble to this Agreement.
“Person” means any natural person, corporation, limited liability company, trust, joint venture, association, company, partnership or other entity.
“Prior Non-Disclosure Agreements” mean [●].
“Provider” is defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Provider Confidential Information” means (a) any information or data, whether technical or nontechnical, whether written (including graphic or electronic) and marked confidential or oral, disclosed by Provider or its Affiliates or on Provider’s behalf to Colgate, either directly or indirectly, on or after the Effective Date[or previously under a Prior Non-Disclosure Agreement], excluding all Colgate Confidential information, and (b) the existence and terms of this Agreement; provided that Provider Confidential Information shall not include any Foreground IP. If Provider Confidential Information is disclosed orally, Provider shall provide a summary and confirm the confidential nature of such information in writing within fifteen (15) days after such oral disclosure.
“Receiving Party” means the Party receiving Confidential Information.
“Representatives” means, for a Party, its directors, officers, employees, advisors or agents and the directors, officers, employees, advisors or agents of its Affiliates.
“Service Exhibit” is defined in Section 2.1.
“Services” is defined in Section 2.2.
“Term” is defined in Section 9.1.
“Third Party” means any entity other than Provider or Colgate or an Affiliate of either Party.

Service Exhibit. Exhibit A hereto (the “Service Exhibit”) sets forth the services and other activities to be conducted by Provider. The Service Exhibit identifies: (a) a description of the services to be provided by Provider; (b) the schedule under which such services are to be performed; (c) the deliverables to be provided by Provider to Colgate (the “Deliverables”); (d) each Party’s primary contact for performance and receipt of the services; and (e) the Fees (as defined below).

Performance of Services. Provider shall, and shall cause its Representatives and permitted subcontractors to, perform all of the services set forth in the Service Exhibit (including the delivery of the Deliverables), together with any services not specifically described in the Service Exhibit but which are inherent in or a necessary part of the services described in the Service Exhibit, or are reasonably required for proper performance of such services (collectively, the “Services”). Provider shall be responsible for acquiring all necessary equipment, materials and tools necessary to perform the Services other than the Materials, if any. [All Deliverables delivered by Provider are subject to Colgate’s acceptance, and Provider shall re-perform and re-deliver any Deliverable that is not accepted by Colgate. No payment under this Agreement by Colgate shall be evidence of the performance of Provider or the acceptance of any Deliverable.]

Removal of Personnel. Provider shall maintain staffing levels and continuity of personnel consistent with its obligation to perform the Services. [Provider shall not remove or redeploy personnel performing the Services without the prior written permission of Colgate.] If any Representatives performing the Services are unacceptable to Colgate for any reason, Colgate reserves the right to notify Provider in which case Provider shall immediately remove such Representatives from performing the Services hereunder and, if requested by Colgate, provide a qualified replacement. If Provider provides replacement Representatives for any reason, Provider shall not charge Colgate for the number of hours required to train the replacement until such Representatives are familiar with the particular Services, so that such replacement Representatives are capable of performing the Services in accordance with this Agreement.

playbookClauses.text: Materials. Colgate will provide the materials identified in the Service Exhibit, if any (the “Materials”), to Provider for the performance of the Services. Provider shall not use the Materials other than for the performance of the Services and expressly agrees not to analyze, attempt to identify, modify or otherwise reverse engineer the Materials to determine their composition. Upon the completion of the Services, Provider shall return all unused Materials to Colgate, unless otherwise instructed by Colgate in writing. The Materials are Confidential Information of Colgate.

Subcontractors. Provider may not subcontract or engage any Third Party to perform any of the Services unless: (a) Colgate provides written approval in advance; and (b) such Third Party enters into an agreement having commercial, Intellectual Property and confidentiality terms that are approved in writing by Colgate. No such subcontracting shall relieve Provider of its obligations under this Agreement and Provider shall be responsible for the actions and inactions of all of its permitted subcontractors as if such actions and inactions were committed by Provider.

playbookClauses.text: Compliance with Policies While On-Site. While at the offices or facilities of Colgate and its Affiliates, Provider and its Representatives shall comply with all applicable policies and procedures of Colgate (including security policies and procedures) as provided to Provider and its Representatives in writing or explained in a formal course on security.

Conflicts. During the Term and for one (1) year thereafter, Provider shall not undertake to perform any services or other work that may be adverse to or conflict with Services being provided to Colgate, including similar work for any of Colgate’s direct competitors in competing categories, without the prior written consent of Colgate.

Fees. In consideration of Provider’s performance of the Services, Colgate shall pay to Provider the fees as set forth in the Service Exhibit (the “Fees”). Provider agrees to establish an account with Colgate’s electronic invoicing provider for the submission and payment of all invoices. After the Fees have become due, as set forth in the Service Exhibit, Provider shall submit an invoice electronically. All undisputed Fees shall be payable by Colgate within forty-five (45) days after receipt of an acceptable invoice for such Fees from Provider; provided that Provider may only issue such an invoice after such Fees have become due pursuant to the Service Exhibit. All payments will be made by Colgate to Provider via a wire transfer. Any sales, use, excise, value-added or other taxes or duties and penalties and interest relating thereto shall be the sole responsibility of Provider.

No Other Costs. Except as otherwise set forth in the Service Exhibit, all direct and indirect costs and expenses (including any travel costs, legal and other advisory fees and other Third-Party costs) in connection with this Agreement incurred by Provider or its Representatives shall be borne solely by Provider, and Colgate shall have no obligation to reimburse Provider for any such costs or expenses. In case the Service Exhibit sets forth that specific expenses or costs are to be reimbursed by Colgate, such expenses or costs must be supported by detailed documentation including, for example, valid invoices or receipts.
Audit.

playbookClauses.text: Provider shall maintain complete and accurate records of, and supporting documentation for, all Fees billable to and payments made by Colgate hereunder in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. Provider shall provide Colgate with reasonable documentation and other information for each invoice as may be reasonably requested by Colgate.

Colgate or its Representatives may audit the books and records of Provider to verify Fees paid or payable in accordance with this Agreement. Colgate’s right to audit Provider’s books and records for any calendar year shall expire twelve (12) months after the end of such calendar year. [Colgate shall pay the costs of the auditors conducting such audit, unless the results of an audit reveal an overpayment of Fees of five percent (5%) or more, in which case, Provider shall pay the costs of the auditors conducting such audit and Colgate’s out-of-pocket costs of conducting such audit. If the audit concludes that an overpayment has occurred during the audited period, such payment shall be remitted by Provider to Colgate within thirty (30) days after the date such auditor’s written report identifying the overpayment is delivered to Provider, together with interest of two percent (2%) per month from the date of overpayment (or the maximum amount of interest permitted by applicable Law if lower).]

Ownership of Deliverables and Data. All Deliverables (including data, information and work in progress resulting from the conduct of the Services) shall be the exclusive property of Colgate, shall be considered Confidential Information of Colgate and shall be subject to Colgate’s exclusive use, commercial or otherwise. Provider hereby assigns, and shall cause its Affiliates and its and their Representatives and subcontractors to assign, to Colgate the entire right, title and interest in and to all Deliverables.

Work for Hire. Provider expressly acknowledges that all copyrightable works contained in the Deliverables provided under this Agreement or any SOW are being specially ordered and commissioned by Colgate. Provider agrees that all copyrightable works contained in the Deliverables are provided as a work made for hire and will be Colgate’s sole and exclusive property, and Colgate shall be the sole owner of the entire right, title and interest in and to all copyrightable works contained in the Deliverables.

playbookClauses.text: Background IP. All Background IP shall be and remain exclusively the property of the Party that made or acquired such Background IP. Except as set forth in Article 5, neither Party has any right or license to any of the other Party’s Background IP.
Foreground IP.

Ownership. Colgate shall exclusively own all right, title and interest in and to all Foreground IP. Provider hereby assigns, and shall cause its Affiliates and its and their Representatives and subcontractors to assign, to Colgate the entire right, title and interest in and to all Foreground IP. If Provider is not permitted by applicable Law to assign any Foreground IP to Colgate, Provider hereby grants Colgate a perpetual, irrevocable, exclusive (even as to Provider), world-wide, royalty-free, freely-assignable license in all fields to such Foreground IP (including the right to sell and grant sublicenses (through multiple tiers) to such Foreground IP) and agrees not to bring any action, claim or proceeding against Colgate or any of its sublicensees or assignees for its use or exploitation of such Foreground IP. Colgate shall have the exclusive right to prepare and file applications for, prosecute, maintain, defend and assert, at its own costs, the Foreground IP. Provider shall reasonably assist and cooperate with Colgate at Colgate’s expense in perfecting, maintaining and defending the rights granted to Colgate in this Section 4.4.1, including the provision of any requested documentation necessary for prosecution or maintenance of patents claiming such Foreground IP, and the execution of any required documents therefor. Unless obligated by applicable Law, Provider shall not file any patent applications claiming, or amend any patent applications to claim, any Foreground IP. If despite the foregoing, Provider files any patent applications claiming, or amends any patent applications to claim, any Foreground IP, Provider agrees to assign such patent applications to Colgate.

Disclosure. Upon delivery of any Deliverable, Provider shall provide to Colgate a written report detailing any Foreground IP developed in connection with or embodied in the Deliverable. Provider shall include in its written report a reasonable level of detail regarding the applicable Foreground IP and shall provide such additional information on the Foreground IP as is reasonably requested by Colgate.

playbookClauses.text: Enforcement. Colgate shall have the exclusive right to bring and control any claim, action or proceeding related to the infringement, misappropriation or other violation of any Foreground IP, and shall retain all damages, recoveries and other amounts awarded in connection therewith. Provider shall reasonably assist and cooperate with Colgate in bringing a claim, action or proceeding pursuant to this Section 4.4.3, at Colgate’s expense, including the provision or execution of any requested documentation. Provider acknowledges that it may be a necessary party to any claim, action or proceeding brought by Colgate arising from enforcement of any Foreground IP and, if necessary, Provider shall participate in such claim, action or proceeding, at Colgate’s request.
Notice of Infringement. Provider shall promptly notify Colgate of its knowledge of any infringement or potential infringement of the Foreground IP by any Third Party.

Validity and Enforceability. Provider agrees not to contest the validity or enforceability of any Foreground IP, or assist any other entity in attacking the validity or enforceability of the Foreground IP.

Use of Names and Trademarks. Neither Party nor its Affiliates shall make any oral or written statement or perform any act indicating that the other Party or its Affiliates endorses or approves, or has endorsed or approved, such Party or its products or services. Nothing contained in this Agreement will be construed as conferring any right to use in advertising, publicity or other promotional activities any name, trade name, trademark, service mark or other designation of a Party (including any contraction, abbreviation or simulation of any of the foregoing) without the prior written approval of such Party.

License to Provider Background IP and Confidential Information. To the extent Provider Background IP is incorporated into, or otherwise necessary or useful to exploit, any Foreground IP or Deliverable, Provider, on behalf of itself and its Affiliates, grants to Colgate and Colgate’s Affiliates a sub-licensable, non-exclusive, royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide license to practice and otherwise fully exploit all Provider Background IP, including to use and/or import any product or service or practice any method, in any and all fields. For the avoidance of doubt, expiration or termination of this Agreement shall not terminate or limit Colgate’s rights under this Section 5.1.

playbookClauses.text: Indemnification Claims. Colgate agrees to give Provider prompt written notice of any matter upon which any indemnified Person intends to base a claim for indemnification (an “Indemnity Claim”) under this Article 7, provided, however, that any delay in providing or failure to provide such notice shall not relieve Provider of any of its obligations hereunder except to the extent that Provider is materially prejudiced by such failure. Provider shall have the right to participate jointly with the indemnified Person in the indemnified Person’s defense, settlement or other disposition of any Indemnity Claim. With respect to any Indemnity Claim relating solely to the payment of money damages which could not result in the indemnified Person becoming subject to injunctive or other equitable relief or otherwise adversely affect the business of the indemnified Person in any manner, and as to which Provider shall have acknowledged in writing the obligation to indemnify the indemnified Person hereunder, Provider shall have the sole right to defend, settle or otherwise dispose of such Indemnity Claim, on such terms as Provider, in its sole discretion, shall deem appropriate; provided that Provider shall provide reasonable evidence of its ability to pay any damages claimed and with respect to any such settlement shall have obtained the written release of the indemnified Person from the Indemnity Claim. Provider shall obtain the written consent of the indemnified Person, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, prior to ceasing to defend, settling or otherwise disposing of any Indemnity Claim if as a result thereof the indemnified Person would become subject to injunctive or other equitable relief or the business of the indemnified Person would be adversely affected in any manner.

Obligations of Confidentiality. The Receiving Party shall (a) maintain any Confidential Information in confidence; (b) take all necessary and reasonable precautions to prevent Confidential Information from being disclosed to any unauthorized Third Party, and (c) use Confidential Information exclusively for performing or receiving the Services, as applicable. The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to its Representatives and permitted subcontractors, each with a need to know such Confidential Information in order to perform their duties in carrying out and receiving the Services; provided that (i) the Receiving Party advises its Representatives and permitted subcontractors of the confidential nature thereof and (ii) such Representatives and permitted subcontractors are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as stringent as those set forth herein (for subcontractors, the confidentiality terms must be approved in writing by Colgate, as set forth in Section 2.5). The Receiving Party shall be liable to the Disclosing Party for any failure by any of its Representatives or permitted subcontractors to comply with this Article 8 with respect to the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information.
Exclusions. Confidential Information shall not include information that the Receiving Party demonstrates:
is in the public domain as of the Effective Date or subsequently enters the public domain through no fault or act of the Receiving Party;

is known to the Receiving Party prior to disclosure from the Disclosing Party[; provided that such information was not acquired from the Disclosing Party under one of the Prior Non-Disclosure Agreements if such information is still to be treated as confidential under such Prior Non-Disclosure Agreement;]
that the Receiving Party received from any Third Party not under any obligation to the Disclosing Party to keep such information confidential; or
was independently developed by the Receiving Party without reliance upon or use of the Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party.
Compelled and Mandatory Disclosures.

In the event that the Receiving Party receives a subpoena or other government process that purports to require the production of any Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party for use in an action or proceeding or for any purpose other than for performing or receiving the Services, the Receiving Party shall (a) promptly inform the party or entity issuing such subpoena or other government process of the existence of this Agreement, (b) promptly inform the Disclosing Party of the receipt of such subpoena or other government process and (c) not oppose any effort by the Disclosing Party to quash any such subpoena or other government process. In the event that (x) the Disclosing Party fails to intervene to quash such subpoena or other government process after being given notice and a reasonable opportunity to do so or (y) such intervention fails or is denied by a court of competent jurisdiction, such Confidential Information may be produced but limited to what is strictly necessary, notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary.

In the event that the Receiving Party believes it is required by applicable Law or stock exchange rules to disclose any part of the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information, the Receiving Party shall: (a) promptly advise the Disclosing Party of each such requirement in writing and identify the documents so required thereby, so that the Disclosing Party may seek an appropriate protective order or other remedy or waive compliance by the Receiving Party with the provisions of this Agreement; and (b) consult with the Disclosing Party on the advisability of taking legally available steps to resist or narrow the scope of such requirement. Termination. This Agreement may be terminated as follows:

Material Breach. This Agreement may be terminated by either Party (the “Nonbreaching Party”) upon written notice thereof to the other Party (the “Breaching Party”) in the event of a material breach of this Agreement by the Breaching Party which is not cured within sixty (60) days after the receipt by the Breaching Party of written notice from the Nonbreaching Party, specifying in reasonable detail the nature of such breach. If such breach is not cured within such cure period, this Agreement shall terminate as set forth in the Nonbreaching Party’s notice of breach and in accordance with the terms of this Article; provided, however, that this Agreement shall not be terminated prior to the end of such cure period.

Insolvency. This Agreement may be terminated by either Party upon sixty (60) days’ prior written notice to the other Party at any time during this Agreement if the other Party: (a) files in any court pursuant to any statute a petition in bankruptcy or insolvency or for reorganization or for an arrangement or for the appointment of a receiver or trustee of the other Party, or of its assets; (b) proposes a written agreement of composition for extension of its debts; (c) is served with an involuntary petition against it, filed in any insolvency proceeding, and such petition shall not be dismissed within sixty (60) days after filing thereof; or (d) makes an assignment for the benefit of its creditors. Provider shall, in accordance with such Colgate’s instructions, deliver to Colgate: (i) all materials, products or equipment of Colgate previously provided to Provider in connection with the Services, including the Materials; and (ii) all Deliverables (including Deliverables in progress); and

Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of State of New York, without giving effect to any choice of law or conflicts of law rules or provisions.

Dispute Resolution. Subject to Section 10.5.4 below, any dispute between the Parties arising out of, related to or in connection with this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively by invoking the following dispute resolution procedure:

The Parties agree to make a diligent, good faith effort to resolve all disputes amicably if at all possible. To this end, authorized representatives of each Party shall meet within fifteen (15) days after receipt of written notice by either Party at a mutually agreeable time and place to discuss possible resolution of the dispute.

In the event that the Parties are unable to resolve the dispute within fifteen (15) days after their meeting, then either Party may invoke non-binding mediation under the International Institute for Conflict Prevention & Resolution (“CPR”) Mediation Procedure then in effect . Unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties, the Parties will select a single mediator from the CPR Panels of Distinguished Neutrals. The mediation proceeding shall be conducted in New York, New York, or such other location as may be agreed in writing by the Parties. The Parties shall (a) share equally the fees and expenses of the mediator; and (b) bear their own attorneys’ fees and associated costs and expenses. At the request of either Party, the mediator shall enter an appropriate protective order to maintain the confidentiality of information produced or exchanged in the course of the mediation proceedings. The Parties shall use their best efforts to complete the mediation procedure provided for in this Article 10.5 within no more than sixty (60) days.

After (i) completion of the process described in Section 10.5.1 and Section 10.5.2 above or (ii) the non-cooperation of either Party in the completion of the stated procedure, then either Party (in the case of clause (i)) or the cooperating Party (in the case of clause (ii)) may initiate an action in court against the other, but such action may only be brought in a court having jurisdiction pursuant to Article 10.6 of this Agreement. All applicable statutes of limitation and defenses based upon the passage of time shall be tolled while the process described in Section 10.5.1 and Section 10.5.2 above is pending. The Parties shall take such action, if any, required to effectuate such tolling.

Nothing in this Article 10.5 shall be construed to prevent either Party from seeking injunctive relief against the other Party from any judicial or administrative authority of competent jurisdiction to enjoin such other Party from breaching any provision of this Agreement pending the resolution of a dispute as hereinbefore provided.

Venue. All disputes arising out of this Agreement (and all amendments and attachments hereto) shall be exclusively resolved in a court of competent jurisdiction in the State of New York. Each Party expressly consents to the jurisdiction of the state or federal courts in the State of New York and waives any objections or right as to forum non conveniens, lack of personal jurisdiction or similar grounds. Each Party hereby irrevocably and unconditionally waives all right to trial by jury in any action (whether based on contract, tort or otherwise) arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or its performance under or the enforcement of this Agreement.

Assignment. This Agreement or any of the Parties’ rights and obligations can only be assigned, transferred or delegated (collectively “to assign” or “assignment”) with the other Party’s express prior written consent; provided that Provider’s consent is not necessary if Colgate assigns to any of its Affiliates. When duly assigned, this Agreement shall be binding on each Party’s successors and assigns.
Time of the Essence. Time is of the essence in the performance of this Agreement.

Counterparts. This Agreement may have multiple signature pages signed separately in different locations which, when together, shall be considered one and the same Agreement as of the date the last Party signed, and shall become a binding Agreement when the signed signature pages have been delivered to the other Party. Each Party is permitted to deliver this Agreement to the other Party by sending a copy of their signed signature pages via facsimile or as an attachment in portable document format (PDF) or other email attachment format, e-signature, to an email addressed to the other Party.

The Parties hereto agree that they have [been represented] by counsel during the negotiation and execution of this Agreement and, therefore, waive the application of any Law (including any rule of construction) providing that ambiguities in an agreement or other document will be construed against the Party drafting such agreement or document. Whenever the context hereof shall so require, the singular shall include the plural, the male gender shall include the female gender and neuter, and vice versa. Whenever the words “include,” “includes” or “including” are used in this Agreement, they shall be deemed to be followed by the words “without limitation” whether or not such words actually appear thereafter. Whenever the word “or” is used in this Agreement, it shall not be deemed to be exclusive. Headings in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement or of any provision herein. This Agreement has been fully negotiated by the Parties and shall not be construed by any Governmental Authority against either Party by virtue of the fact that such Party was the drafting party.
Waiver. The waiver by any Party hereto of a breach of any provision of this Agreement shall not operate or be construed as a waiver of any subsequent breach.

Severability. In addition, the affected portion of this Agreement will remain in effect in all circumstances other than the circumstances that caused the court or arbiter to find that part to be illegal, invalid or unenforceable.
