GLOBAL ANTI-BRIBERY POLICY
Our Anti-Bribery Commitment

Colgate’s commitment to dealing legally and ethically applies worldwide. We comply with all applicable anti-bribery laws, including but not limited to the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (“FCPA”), everywhere we do business, and we expect the same of the third parties with whom we work. While the FCPA prohibits, among other things, bribery of foreign government officials and entities, other anti-bribery laws, like the UK Bribery Act, prohibit commercial bribery between private individuals and entities.

Colgate people and any third parties acting on our behalf or in connection with our business are prohibited from giving or offering anything of value directly or indirectly to any government official or entity, or to any private individual or entity, in order to improperly obtain or retain any business advantage or to improperly affect any act or decision.

This prohibition includes any facilitating, expediting or “grease” payments made to government officials, either directly or indirectly, in order to expedite any official service or function (for example, small payments made to an official to move Colgate’s application to the front of the line or to shorten the time frame in which services or other actions are provided). Any official fees supported by government-issued receipts do not qualify as improper payments.
Maintaining Accurate Books and Records

No payment by or on behalf of the Company shall be approved or made if any part of the payment is to be used for an unlawful or improper purpose, or for any purpose other than that described by valid documents supporting the payment. No false or misleading entries should be made in any books or financial records of the Company for any reason.

Any expenses that an employee or third party incurs on Colgate’s behalf or in connection with our business shall not be reimbursable unless they are lawful and supported by detailed documentation including, for example, valid invoices or receipts.
Expenditures Related to Government Officials

No funds may be provided to or spent on behalf of a government official or entity, directly or indirectly, without advance written approval from Colgate’s Global Legal Organization. This includes any payments, gifts, donations, entertainment, travel, meals, or other items of value. (For additional information, please review the Global Policy on Expenditures Related to Government Officials & Governments.) Advance approval is not required for official fees supported by government-issued receipts (e.g., permit or license fees).

Please note that the term “government official” is widely defined and may include individuals who are employed by any public or state-affiliated institution or organization or who act in an official capacity in any way, whether full-time, part-time or unpaid. Government officials can be found in every branch and level of government and public life and may include anyone from low-level customs employees, to employees of state-owned media outlets, to high-ranking lawmakers, as well as researchers, professors, teachers, dentists, veterinarians, or other professionals and Key Thought Leaders. If you are in doubt as to whether an individual could be considered a government official, you should contact the Global Legal Organization.
Commercial Bribery

In addition to prohibiting bribery of government officials, Colgate also prohibits its employees and third parties from engaging in bribery of private parties. You should not seek to improperly influence the judgment or conduct of any party with whom you might be conducting Company business by offering or providing any payments, gifts or other benefits, or by any other unlawful inducement.
Our Expectations

Colgate’s reputation depends on the conduct of our employees as well as the conduct of those with whom we do business. It is our goal to ensure that Colgate People and the third parties with whom we work reflect the same high ethical standards and demonstrate a commitment to compliance with all applicable laws. We further expect our third parties to ensure that their employees and subcontractors understand and comply with this Anti-Bribery Policy.

Failure to comply with this Anti-Bribery Policy or any applicable anti-bribery laws, including but not limited to the FCPA, may result in civil or criminal penalties, as well as termination of the employment or business relationship.
Any questions regarding this policy may be directed to our Global Compliance Legal Specialist: Legal_Complinace@colpal.com

Dispute Resolution. Subject to Section 10.5.4 below, any dispute between the Parties arising out of, related to or in connection with this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively by invoking the following dispute resolution procedure:

The Parties agree to make a diligent, good faith effort to resolve all disputes amicably if at all possible. To this end, authorized representatives of each Party shall meet within fifteen (15) days after receipt of written notice by either Party at a mutually agreeable time and place to discuss possible resolution of the dispute.

In the event that the Parties are unable to resolve the dispute within fifteen (15) days after their meeting, then either Party may invoke non-binding mediation under the International Institute for Conflict Prevention & Resolution (“CPR”) Mediation Procedure then in effect . Unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties, the Parties will select a single mediator from the CPR Panels of Distinguished Neutrals. The mediation proceeding shall be conducted in New York, New York, or such other location as may be agreed in writing by the Parties. The Parties shall (a) share equally the fees and expenses of the mediator; and (b) bear their own attorneys’ fees and associated costs and expenses. At the request of either Party, the mediator shall enter an appropriate protective order to maintain the confidentiality of information produced or exchanged in the course of the mediation proceedings. The Parties shall use their best efforts to complete the mediation procedure provided for in this Article 10.5 within no more than sixty (60) days.

After (i) completion of the process described in Section 10.5.1 and Section 10.5.2 above or (ii) the non-cooperation of either Party in the completion of the stated procedure, then either Party (in the case of clause (i)) or the cooperating Party (in the case of clause (ii)) may initiate an action in court against the other, but such action may only be brought in a court having jurisdiction pursuant to Article 10.6 of this Agreement. GLOBAL ANTI-BRIBERY POLICY
Our Anti-Bribery Commitment

Colgate’s commitment to dealing legally and ethically applies worldwide. We comply with all applicable anti-bribery laws, including but not limited to the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (“FCPA”), everywhere we do business, and we expect the same of the third parties with whom we work. While the FCPA prohibits, among other things, bribery of foreign government officials and entities, other anti-bribery laws, like the UK Bribery Act, prohibit commercial bribery between private individuals and entities.

Colgate people and any third parties acting on our behalf or in connection with our business are prohibited from giving or offering anything of value directly or indirectly to any government official or entity, or to any private individual or entity, in order to improperly obtain or retain any business advantage or to improperly affect any act or decision.

This prohibition includes any facilitating, expediting or “grease” payments made to government officials, either directly or indirectly, in order to expedite any official service or function (for example, small payments made to an official to move Colgate’s application to the front of the line or to shorten the time frame in which services or other actions are provided). Any official fees supported by government-issued receipts do not qualify as improper payments.
Maintaining Accurate Books and Records

No payment by or on behalf of the Company shall be approved or made if any part of the payment is to be used for an unlawful or improper purpose, or for any purpose other than that described by valid documents supporting the payment. No false or misleading entries should be made in any books or financial records of the Company for any reason.

Any expenses that an employee or third party incurs on Colgate’s behalf or in connection with our business shall not be reimbursable unless they are lawful and supported by detailed documentation including, for example, valid invoices or receipts.
Expenditures Related to Government Officials

No funds may be provided to or spent on behalf of a government official or entity, directly or indirectly, without advance written approval from Colgate’s Global Legal Organization. This includes any payments, gifts, donations, entertainment, travel, meals, or other items of value. (For additional information, please review the Global Policy on Expenditures Related to Government Officials & Governments.) Advance approval is not required for official fees supported by government-issued receipts (e.g., permit or license fees).

Please note that the term “government official” is widely defined and may include individuals who are employed by any public or state-affiliated institution or organization or who act in an official capacity in any way, whether full-time, part-time or unpaid. Government officials can be found in every branch and level of government and public life and may include anyone from low-level customs employees, to employees of state-owned media outlets, to high-ranking lawmakers, as well as researchers, professors, teachers, dentists, veterinarians, or other professionals and Key Thought Leaders. If you are in doubt as to whether an individual could be considered a government official, you should contact the Global Legal Organization.
Commercial Bribery

In addition to prohibiting bribery of government officials, Colgate also prohibits its employees and third parties from engaging in bribery of private parties. You should not seek to improperly influence the judgment or conduct of any party with whom you might be conducting Company business by offering or providing any payments, gifts or other benefits, or by any other unlawful inducement.
Our Expectations

Colgate’s reputation depends on the conduct of our employees as well as the conduct of those with whom we do business. It is our goal to ensure that Colgate People and the third parties with whom we work reflect the same high ethical standards and demonstrate a commitment to compliance with all applicable laws. We further expect our third parties to ensure that their employees and subcontractors understand and comply with this Anti-Bribery Policy.

Failure to comply with this Anti-Bribery Policy or any applicable anti-bribery laws, including but not limited to the FCPA, may result in civil or criminal penalties, as well as termination of the employment or business relationship.
Any questions regarding this policy may be directed to our Global Compliance Legal Specialist: Legal_Complinace@colpal.com

MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT
THIS MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”), is entered into as of the date of the last signature below (the “Effective Date”), by and between Colgate-Palmolive Company, a Delaware corporation (“Colgate”), with offices at 300 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10022, and [Third Party Ful legal En]*, a [State of Incorporation] [Type of Company] (“Company”), with offices at [Principal Address].  Colgate and Company are referred to herein collectively as the “Parties” and individually as a “Party.” In consideration of the promises and of the mutual agreements and covenants hereinafter set forth and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, and intending to be legally bound, the Parties agree as follows:
Objective.	Each Party may receive or have access to certain Confidential Information (as defined below) of the other Party in connection with the exploration of a business relationship between the Parties involving [Description of purpose] (“Purpose”).
Definitions.
Definition of Confidential Information.  “Confidential Information” of a Disclosing Party shall mean (a) any information or data, whether technical or nontechnical, whether written (including graphic or electronic) and marked confidential or oral, disclosed by such Party or on such Party’s behalf to the Receiving Party, either directly or indirectly, on or after the Effective Date, and (b) the existence and terms of this Agreement and the fact that discussions or negotiations are taking place between the Parties concerning a possible business relationship. If Confidential Information is disclosed orally, the Disclosing Party shall provide a summary and confirm the confidential nature of such information in writing within 15 days after such oral disclosure. 
Confidential Information shall not include information that the Receiving Party demonstrates (a) is publicly available as of the Effective Date or subsequently becomes publicly available through no fault or act of the Receiving Party, (b) is known to the Receiving Party prior to disclosure from the Disclosing Party, (c)  that the Receiving Party received from any third party not under any obligation to the Disclosing Party to keep such information confidential or (d) was independently developed by the Receiving Party without reliance upon or use of the Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party. 
Definition of Affiliates.  “Affiliate” shall mean an individual, trust, business trust, joint venture, partnership, corporation, association or any other entity which (directly or indirectly) is controlled by, controls, or is under common control with a Party.  For purposes of this definition, the term “control” (including, with correlative meanings, the term “controlled by” and “under common control with”) as used with respect to any Party, shall mean the possession (directly or indirectly) of power to direct or cause the direction of the management or policies of such Party.
Definition of Disclosing Party and Receiving Party.	The Party disclosing such Confidential Information shall be deemed the “Disclosing Party” and the Party receiving such Confidential Information shall be deemed the “Receiving Party.”
Confidentiality. 
Obligation of Confidentiality.  The Receiving Party shall (a) maintain any Confidential Information in confidence, (b) take all necessary and reasonable precautions to prevent Confidential Information from being disclosed to any unauthorized third party, which shall include open artificial intelligence platforms (e.g., ChatGPT), and (c) use Confidential Information exclusively for the Purpose.  The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to its directors, officers, employees, advisors or agents and the directors, officers, employees, advisors or agents of its Affiliates (collectively, “Representatives”), each with a need to know such Confidential Information in order to achieve the Purpose; provided that (i) the Receiving Party advises its Representatives of the confidential nature thereof and (ii) such Representatives are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as stringent as those set forth herein.  The Receiving Party shall be liable to the Disclosing Party for any failure by any of its Representatives to treat any Confidential Information in the same manner as the Receiving Party is obligated to treat such Confidential Information under the terms of this Agreement.
Trade Secrets.  No Disclosing Party shall disclose any “trade secrets” to the Receiving Party pursuant to this Agreement. For purposes of this Agreement “trade secrets” shall have the meaning ascribed to them in the Defend Trade Secrets Act of 2016.
Compelled Disclosures.  In the event that the Receiving Party receives a subpoena or other government process that purports to require the production of any Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party for use in an action or proceeding or for any purpose other than for the Purpose, the Receiving Party shall (a) promptly inform the party or entity issuing such subpoena or other government process of the existence of this Agreement, (b) promptly inform the Disclosing Party of the receipt of such subpoena or other government process and (c) not oppose any effort by the Disclosing Party to quash any such subpoena or other government process.  In the event that (x) the Disclosing Party fails to intervene to quash such subpoena or other government process after being given notice and a reasonable opportunity to do so or (y) such intervention fails or is denied by a court of competent jurisdiction, such Confidential Information may be produced but limited to what is strictly necessary, notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary.  In the event that any Confidential Information is ordered produced in an action or proceeding, such Confidential Information shall not lose its confidential status through such use, and the Receiving Party shall take all reasonable and necessary steps to protect the confidentiality of such Confidential Information during such use.
Residual Information.  Notwithstanding the confidentiality obligations contained in this Section, the Receiving Party may, during and after the term hereof, use in its business any Residual Information. “Residual Information" means information of a general nature, such as general knowledge, professional skills, know-how, work experience or techniques, that would be retained in the unaided memory of an ordinary person skilled in the art, not intent on appropriating the proprietary information of the Disclosing Party, as a result of such person’s access to, use, review, evaluation, or testing of the Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party. Memory shall be considered unaided if the person has not intentionally memorized the information contained within the Confidential Information for the purpose of retaining and subsequently using or disclosing same.   Nothing in this Section, however, shall be deemed to grant to the Receiving Party a license under the Disclosing Party’s patents or other intellectual property rights.
Return of Confidential Information.  At the written request of the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party shall promptly return or destroy (at the sole discretion of the Receiving Party) all Confidential Information in its or its Representatives’ possession, respectively, and shall confirm such return or destruction; provided, however, that the Receiving Party may retain an archival copy or other appropriate record (including electronic backup copies created in the ordinary course) of any such Confidential Information.  Such copies and records may be used exclusively for internal recordkeeping and administrative purposes, to assure compliance with any applicable governmental requirements and for dispute resolution purposes.
Right to Disclose Information.  The Disclosing Party hereby represents and warrants that (a) its entry into this Agreement does not violate or constitute a breach of any agreement to which it is otherwise bound, (b) it has the right to disclose to the Receiving Party any Confidential Information disclosed by such Disclosing Party or on such Party’s behalf and (c) to the best of its knowledge, such disclosure does not violate or constitute a breach of any agreement or understanding, written or oral, to which such Party is bound.
Ownership. All Confidential Information disclosed by the Disclosing Party or on its behalf to the Receiving Party or its Representatives pursuant to this Agreement shall be and remain the property of the Disclosing Party.  All data, information, analysis and reports (“Data and Reports”) about Confidential Information that is created or generated by a Receiving Party shall be owned and controlled exclusively by such Receiving Party (which includes without limitation the right to file patent applications on any inventions conceived by such Receiving Party that result from its proper use of Confidential Information hereunder), subject only to its duty hereunder to maintain the confidentiality of any Confidential Information contained in such Data and Reports.
Absence of License. Except for the purpose of fulfilling obligations under this Agreement, nothing in this Agreement, by implication or otherwise, conveys to the Receiving Party any right or license with respect to any intellectual property or Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party.  No right is granted by this Agreement to the Receiving Party to use any registered or unregistered trademark, service mark or trade name of the Disclosing Party.
No Commitments.  Nothing in this Agreement nor in any previous or contemporaneous communications or understandings, whether oral or written, shall be deemed to provide any commitment of any kind or intent by either Party to enter into any further agreement with the other Party or to disclose any Confidential Information hereunder, and neither Party has acted or shall act in reliance on any potential further agreement.  Each Party agrees that neither the holding of discussions between them nor the furnishing of any Confidential Information hereunder shall be construed as an obligation on the part of either Party to refrain from engaging at any time in any business similar or dissimilar to the business matters discussed by the Parties.
Disclaimer.  Neither Party makes any representation or warranty, express or implied, as to the accuracy or completeness of any Confidential Information provided hereunder, all of which shall be provided “as is”.
Limitations of Liability.  TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW, EXCLUDING GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFULL MISCONDUCT, AND/OR FRAUD, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY HAVE ANY LIABILITY TO THE OTHER PARTY, ANY OF THE OTHER PARTY’S AFFILIATES OR ANY THIRD PARTY ARISING OUT OF, RELATED TO OR IN CONNECTION WITH THIS AGREEMENT, REGARDLESS OF THE FORM OF THE ACTION, WHETHER IN CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), PRODUCT LIABILITY OR OTHERWISE:
FOR INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, INDIRECT, SPECIAL, PUNITIVE OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES OR LIABILITIES OF ANY KIND OR FOR LOSS OF REVENUE OR PROFITS OR LOSS OF BUSINESS; OR
IN AN AGGREGATE AMOUNT IN EXCESS OF $[Liability Cap Amount].
Governing Law.  This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of State of New York, without giving effect to any choice of law or conflicts of law rules or provisions.  
Dispute Resolution.  Subject to Section 10.4 below, any dispute between the Parties arising out of, related to or in connection with this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively by invoking the following dispute resolution procedure:
The Parties agree to make a diligent, good faith effort to resolve all disputes amicably if at all possible. To this end, authorized representatives of each Party shall meet within fifteen (15) days after receipt of written notice by either Party at a mutually agreeable time and place to discuss possible resolution of the dispute.
In the event that the Parties are unable to resolve the dispute within fifteen (15) days after their meeting, then either Party may invoke non-binding mediation under the International Institute for Conflict Prevention & Resolution (“CPR”) Mediation Procedure then in effect. Unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties, the Parties will select a single mediator from the CPR Panels of Distinguished Neutrals. The mediation proceeding shall be conducted in New York, New York, or such other location as may be agreed in writing by the Parties. The Parties shall (a) share equally the fees and expenses of the mediator; and (b) bear their own attorneys’ fees and associated costs and expenses. At the request of either Party, the mediator shall enter an appropriate protective order to maintain the confidentiality of information produced or exchanged in the course of the mediation proceedings. The Parties shall use their best efforts to complete the mediation procedure provided for in this Section 10 within no more than sixty (60) days.
After (i) completion of the process described in Section 10.1 and Section 10.2 above or (ii) the non-cooperation of either Party in the completion of the stated procedure, then either Party (in the case of clause (i)) or the cooperating Party (in the case of clause (ii)) may initiate an action in court against the other, but such action may only be brought in a court having jurisdiction pursuant to Section 11 of this Agreement. All applicable statutes of limitation and defenses based upon the passage of time shall be tolled while the process described in Section 10.1 and Section 10.2 above is pending. The Parties shall take such action, if any, required to effectuate such tolling.
Nothing in this Section 10 shall be construed to prevent either Party from seeking injunctive relief against the other Party from any judicial or administrative authority of competent jurisdiction to enjoin such other Party from breaching any provision of this Agreement pending the resolution of a dispute as hereinbefore provided.
Venue.  All disputes arising out of this Agreement (and all amendments and attachments hereto) shall be exclusively resolved in a court of competent jurisdiction in New York County in the State of New York. Each Party expressly consents to the jurisdiction of the state or federal courts in New York County in the State of New York and waives any objections or right as to forum non conveniens, lack of personal jurisdiction or similar grounds. EACH PARTY HEREBY IRREVOCABLY AND UNCONDITIONALLY WAIVES ALL RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION (WHETHER BASED ON CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE) ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, OR THE PERFORMANCE UNDER OR ENFORCEMENT OF THIS AGREEMENT.
Compliance with Laws.  In connection with its performance of this Agreement, Company shall comply with all applicable laws, rules, regulations and treaties, including but not limited to all applicable anti-corruption, competition, environmental, labor, product and ingredient laws, rules, regulations and treaties.  Failure to comply with applicable laws may be deemed a material breach of this Agreement.
Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any of the Parties’ rights or obligations hereunder may be assigned, transferred or delegated (collectively “to assign” or “assignment”) without the prior written consent of the other Party; provided, however, that Colgate may assign this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations hereunder to any of its Affiliates without obtaining the Company’s prior written consent.   This Agreement shall be binding on, and inure to the benefit of, each Party’s successors and permitted assigns. 
Entire Agreement; Amendment.  This Agreement supersedes all previous and contemporaneous communications and understandings, whether oral or written, and constitutes the sole and entire agreement between the Parties pertaining to the Confidential Information.  No modification, deletion, addition or waiver of the terms of this Agreement shall be binding on either Party unless made in writing and signed by a duly authorized representative of each Party.
Term; Termination.  
The term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and continue in effect for two (2) years.
This Agreement may be terminated by either Party for any or no reason by providing the other Party with written notice at least thirty (30) days prior to the desired effective date of termination.  
Survival.  The obligations of confidentiality and non-use set forth herein shall apply during the term of this Agreement and survive for a period of three (3) years after the expiration or termination of this Agreement pursuant to Section 15.  All other provisions which by their nature should survive the termination of this Agreement shall survive any such termination.
Headings; Construction.  Headings in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall ot affect the interpretation of this Agreement or of any provision herein.  This Agreement shall be construed without regard to any presumption or other rule requiring construction hereof against the Party causing this Agreement to be drafted.
Non-Waiver.  Failure of either Party to exercise any of its rights under this Agreement upon any occasion shall not waive such Party’s right to exercise any such right on another occasion.
Severability.  If any portion of this Agreement is to any extent determined to be illegal, invalid or unenforceable by a court or arbiter of competent jurisdiction, the remainder of this Agreement will not be affected and will remain valid and enforceable.  In addition, the affected portion of this Agreement will remain in effect in all circumstances other than the circumstances that caused the court or arbiter to find that part to be illegal, invalid or unenforceable.
Notices.  Each Party shall deliver all notices required pursuant to Sections 10 and 15 under this Agreement (each, a “Notice”) in writing and in English, referring to this Agreement and addressed to the other Party at its address below or to the last address the receiving Party provided to the other Party in compliance with this Section. The Parties shall deliver any Notice by personal delivery, reputable overnight courier (all fees prepaid), or certified or registered mail (postage prepaid, return receipt requested). MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

THIS MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT is entered into as of the date of the last signature below (the “Effective Date”) by and between Colgate-Palmolive Company, a Delaware corporation, having its principal offices at 300 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10022 (“Colgate”), and [●], a [●] organized under the laws of [●], having its principal offices at [●] (“Provider”).  Colgate and Provider are sometimes hereinafter referred to collectively as the “Parties” and individually as a “Party.”

RECITALS

WHEREAS, Colgate desires to have Provider carry out services for Colgate or its Affiliates, as more specifically set forth in one or more Statements of Work to this Agreement; and

WHEREAS, Colgate and Provider desire to enter into this Agreement to govern the provision and receipt of such services.

AGREEMENT

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the premises and the undertakings of the Parties hereinafter set forth, the Parties agree as follows:

DEFINITIONS

“Affiliate” means, with respect to a Person, an individual, trust, business trust, joint venture, partnership, corporation, association or any other entity which (directly or indirectly) is controlled by, controls, or is under common control with a Person.  For purposes of this definition, the term “control” (including, with correlative meanings, the term “controlled by” and “under common control with”) as used with respect to any Person, shall mean the possession (directly or indirectly) of power to direct or cause the direction of the management or policies of such Person.

“Agreement” means this Master Services Agreement and all Exhibits hereto and the SOWs executed by the Parties hereunder which in accordance with their terms constitute a part of this Agreement, as the same may be amended or modified from time to time in accordance with the terms hereof.

“Background IP” means Intellectual Property under the control of a Party that was developed or acquired by the Party prior to the Effective Date or independently and outside the activities contemplated by this Agreement without reference to or use of the other Party’s Confidential Information or Background IP. For purposes of this definition, a Party “controls” Intellectual Property if it owns or otherwise has the right to license or sublicense such Intellectual Property.

“Breaching Party” is defined in Section 9.2.1.

“Claims” is defined in Section 7.1.

“Colgate” is defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Colgate Confidential Information” means (a) any information or data, whether technical or nontechnical, whether written (including graphic or electronic) and marked confidential or oral, disclosed by Colgate or its Affiliates or on Colgate’s behalf to Provider, either directly or indirectly, on or after the Effective Date [or previously under a Prior Non-Disclosure Agreement], and (b) the existence and terms of this Agreement. If Colgate Confidential Information is disclosed orally, Colgate shall provide a summary and confirm the confidential nature of such information in writing within fifteen (15) days after such oral disclosure.  For the avoidance of doubt, Colgate Confidential Information shall include Foreground IP, Materials, Deliverables and [●].

“Confidential Information” means Colgate Confidential Information or Provider Confidential Information, as the context requires.

“Deliverables” is defined in Section 2.1.

“Disclosing Party” means the Party disclosing Confidential Information.

“Effective Date” is defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Fees” is defined in Section 3.1.

“Force Majeure” is defined in Section 10.1.

[“Foreground IP” means Intellectual Property that is created by the Representatives of either or both Parties while performing or receiving the Services under this Agreement, including, but not limited to, any Intellectual Property in the Deliverables.]

“Governmental Authority” means any legislative, executive or judicial unit of any governmental or quasi-governmental authority or instrumentality (multi-national, national, federal, state, provincial, local or foreign, international or domestic), or any department, agency, board, bureau, commission, official or other regulatory, administrative or judicial authority thereof, including any administrative or regulatory agency or commission, and any court or arbitration tribunal, in each instance having jurisdiction over the subject matter before it.

“Indemnity Claim” is defined in Section 7.2.

“Intellectual Property” means all discoveries, inventions, improvements, developments, procedures, processes, formulations, know-how, trade secrets, formulae, trademarks, service marks, trade dress, designs, logos, packaging, proprietary information, technical information, techniques, works of authorship, drawings, models, manuals and systems, whether or not patentable or copyrightable or otherwise registerable, and all rights and applications or registrations derived or derivable therefrom.

“Law” means all supranational, international, national, state and local laws, statutes, regulations, rules, codes or ordinances enacted, adopted, issued or promulgated by any Governmental Authority or common law. 

“Materials” is defined in Section 2.4.

“Nonbreaching Party” is defined in Section 9.2.1.

“Notice” is defined in Section 10.2.

“Party” and “Parties” are defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Person” means any natural person, corporation, limited liability company, trust, joint venture, association, company, partnership or other entity.

“Prior Non-Disclosure Agreements” mean [●].

“Provider” is defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Provider Confidential Information” means (a) any information or data, whether technical or nontechnical, whether written (including graphic or electronic) and marked confidential or oral, disclosed by Provider or its Affiliates or on Provider’s behalf to Colgate, either directly or indirectly, on or after the Effective Date[or previously under a Prior Non-Disclosure Agreement], excluding all Colgate Confidential information, and (b) the existence and terms of this Agreement; provided that Provider Confidential Information shall not include any Foreground IP.  If Provider Confidential Information is disclosed orally, Provider shall provide a summary and confirm the confidential nature of such information in writing within fifteen (15) days after such oral disclosure.

“Receiving Party” means the Party receiving Confidential Information.

“Representatives” means, for a Party, its directors, officers, employees, advisors or agents and the directors, officers, employees, advisors or agents of its Affiliates.

“Services” is defined in Section 2.2.

“Statement of Work” and “SOW” are defined in Section 2.1.

“Term” is defined in Section 9.1.

“Third Party” means any entity other than Provider or Colgate or an Affiliate of either Party.

GENERAL OBLIGATIONS

Execution of Statements of Work.  The parties may enter into one or more statements of work setting forth the services and other activities to be conducted by Provider (each, a “Statement of Work” or “SOW”).  Each SOW shall be generally in the form of Exhibit A and shall identify: (a) a description of the services to be provided by Provider; (b) the schedule under which such services are to be performed; (c) the deliverables to be provided by Provider to Colgate (the “Deliverables”); (d) each Party’s primary contact for performance and receipt of the Services; and (e) the Fees (as defined below).  Each SOW shall be signed by authorized representatives of both Parties.  Unless otherwise agreed by the Parties in writing, all SOWs that are entered into under this Agreement shall be governed by the terms of this Agreement and are hereby made part of and incorporated into this Agreement.  In the event of a conflict between this Agreement and a SOW, the terms of this Agreement shall prevail, unless the SOW expressly references the specific provision in this Agreement to be modified by the SOW.  Each SOW may only be modified by the written agreement of both Parties.  [The initial SOW is set forth on Exhibit B]. 

Performance of Services.  Provider shall, and shall cause its Representatives and permitted subcontractors to, perform all of the services set forth in any SOW (including the delivery of the Deliverables), together with any services not specifically described in such SOW but which are inherent in or a necessary part of the services described in such SOW, or are reasonably required for proper performance of such services (collectively, the “Services”).  Provider shall be responsible for acquiring all necessary equipment, materials and tools necessary to perform the Services other than the Materials, if any.  [All Deliverables delivered by Provider are subject to Colgate’s acceptance, and Provider shall re-perform and re-deliver any Deliverable that is not accepted by Colgate.  No payment under this Agreement by Colgate shall be evidence of the performance of Provider or the acceptance of any Deliverable.]

Removal of Personnel.  Provider shall maintain staffing levels and continuity of personnel consistent with its obligation to perform the Services.  [Provider shall not remove or redeploy personnel performing the Services without the prior written permission of Colgate.]  If any Representatives performing the Services are unacceptable to Colgate for any reason, Colgate reserves the right to notify Provider in which case Provider shall immediately remove such Representatives from performing the Services hereunder and, if requested by Colgate, provide a qualified replacement.  If Provider provides replacement Representatives for any reason, Provider shall not charge Colgate for the number of hours required to train the replacement until such Representatives are familiar with the particular Services, so that such replacement Representatives are capable of performing the Services in accordance with this Agreement.

Materials.  Colgate will provide the materials identified in a SOW, if any (the “Materials”), to Provider for the performance of the Services.  Provider shall not use the Materials other than for the performance of the Services and expressly agrees not to analyze, attempt to identify, modify or otherwise reverse engineer the Materials to determine their composition.  Upon the completion of the Services, Provider shall return all unused Materials to Colgate, unless otherwise instructed by Colgate in writing.  The Materials are Confidential Information of Colgate.

Subcontractors.  Provider may not subcontract or engage any Third Party to perform any of the Services unless: (a) Colgate provides written approval in advance; and (b) such Third Party enters into an agreement having commercial, Intellectual Property and confidentiality terms that are approved in writing by Colgate.  No such subcontracting shall relieve Provider of its obligations under this Agreement and Provider shall be responsible for the actions and inactions of all of its permitted subcontractors as if such actions and inactions were committed by Provider.

Compliance with Policies While On-Site.  While at the offices or facilities of Colgate and its Affiliates, Provider and its Representatives shall comply with all applicable policies and procedures of Colgate (including security policies and procedures) as provided to Provider and its Representatives in writing or explained in a formal course on security.

Conflicts.  During the Term and for one (1) year thereafter, Provider shall not undertake to perform any services or other work that may be adverse to or conflict with Services being provided to Colgate, including similar work for any of Colgate’s direct competitors in competing categories, without the prior written consent of Colgate.

FEES

Fees.  In consideration of Provider’s performance of the Services pursuant to a SOW, Colgate shall pay to Provider the fees as set forth in such SOW (the “Fees”).  Provider agrees to establish an account with Colgate’s electronic invoicing provider for the submission and payment of all invoices.  After the Fees have become due, as set forth in the SOW, Provider shall submit an invoice electronically.   All undisputed Fees shall be payable by Colgate within ninety (90) days after Colgate’s receipt of an acceptable invoice for such Fees from Provider; provided that Provider may only issue such an invoice after such Fees have become due pursuant to the SOW.  All payments will be made by Colgate to Provider via a wire transfer.  Any sales, use, excise, value-added or other taxes or duties and penalties and interest relating thereto shall be the sole responsibility of Provider.

No Other Costs.  Except as otherwise set forth in a SOW, all direct and indirect costs and expenses (including any travel costs, legal and other advisory fees and other Third-Party costs) in connection with this Agreement incurred by Provider or its Representatives shall be borne solely by Provider, and Colgate shall have no obligation to reimburse Provider for any such costs or expenses. In case a SOW sets forth that specific expenses or costs are to be reimbursed by Colgate, such expenses or costs must be supported by detailed documentation including, for example, valid invoices or receipts.

Audit.

Provider shall maintain complete and accurate records of, and supporting documentation for, all Fees billable to and payments made by Colgate hereunder in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.  Provider shall provide Colgate with reasonable documentation and other information for each invoice as may be reasonably requested by Colgate.

Colgate or its Representatives may audit the books and records of Provider to verify Fees paid or payable in accordance with this Agreement.  Colgate’s right to audit Provider’s books and records for any calendar year shall expire twelve (12) months after the end of such calendar year.  [Colgate shall pay the costs of the auditors conducting such audit, unless the results of an audit reveal an overpayment of Fees of five percent (5%) or more, in which case, Provider shall pay the costs of the auditors conducting such audit and Colgate’s out-of-pocket costs of conducting such audit.  If the audit concludes that an overpayment has occurred during the audited period, such payment shall be remitted by Provider to Colgate within thirty (30) days after the date such auditor’s written report identifying the overpayment is delivered to Provider, together with interest of two percent (2%) per month from the date of overpayment (or the maximum amount of interest permitted by applicable Law if lower).]

While  the  FCPA  prohibits,  among  other  things,  bribery  of  foreign  government officials and entities, other anti-bribery laws, like the UK Bribery Act, prohibit commercial bribery between private individuals and entities.





Colgate people and any third parties acting on our behalf or in connection with our business are prohibited from giving or offering anything of value directly or indirectly to any government official or entity, or to any private individual or entity, in order to improperly obtain or retain any business advantage or to improperly affect any act or decision.





This prohibition includes any facilitating, expediting or “grease” payments made to government officials, either directly or indirectly, in order to expedite any official service or function (for example, small payments made to an official to move Colgate’s application to the front of the line or to shorten the time frame in which services or other actions are provided).  Any official fees supported by government-issued receipts do not qualify as improper payments.



Maintaining Accurate Books and Records



No payment by or on behalf of the Company shall be approved or made if any part of the payment is to be used for an unlawful or improper purpose, or for any purpose other than that described by valid documents supporting the payment.  No false or misleading entries should be made in any books or financial records of the Company for any reason.



Any expenses that an employee or third party incurs on Colgate’s behalf or in connection with our business shall not be reimbursable unless they are lawful and supported by detailed documentation including, for example, valid invoices or receipts.





Expenditures Related to Government Officials



No funds may be provided to or spent on behalf of a government official or entity, directly or indirectly, without advance written approval from Colgate’s Global Legal Organization.  This includes any payments, gifts, donations, entertainment, travel, meals, or other items of value. (For additional information, please review the Global Policy on Expenditures Related to Government Officials & Governments.)  Advance approval is not required for official fees supported by government-issued receipts (e.g., permit or license fees).Please note that the term “government official” is widely defined and may include individuals who are employed by any public or state-affiliated institution or organization or who act in an official capacity in any way, whether full-time, part-time or unpaid.  Government officials can be found in every branch and level of government and public life and may include anyone from low-level customs employees, to employees of state-owned media outlets, to high-ranking lawmakers, as well as researchers, professors, teachers, dentists, veterinarians, or other professionals and Key Thought Leaders.  If you are in doubt as to whether an individual could be considered a government official, you should contact the Global Legal Organization.



Commercial Bribery



In addition to prohibiting bribery of government officials, Colgate also prohibits its employees and third parties from engaging in bribery of private parties.  You should not seek to improperly influence the judgment or conduct of any party with whom you might be conducting Company business by offering or providing any payments, gifts or other benefits, or by any other unlawful inducement.

Our Expectations



Colgate’s reputation depends on the conduct of our employees as well as the conduct of those with whom we do business.  It is our goal to ensure that Colgate People and the third parties with whom we work reflect the same high ethical standards and demonstrate a commitment to compliance with all applicable laws.  We further expect our third parties to ensure that their employees and subcontractors understand and comply with this Anti-Bribery Policy.

Failure to comply with this Anti-Bribery Policy or any applicable anti-bribery laws, including but not limited to the FCPA, may result in civil or criminal penalties, as well as termination of the employment or business relationship.



Any questions regarding this policy may be directed to our Global Compliance Legal Specialist: Legal_Compliance@colpal.com

MUTUAL MATERIALS TRANSFER AGREEMENT

THIS MUTUAL MATERIALS TRANSFER AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”), is entered into as of the date of the last signature below (the “Effective Date”), by and between Colgate-Palmolive Company, a Delaware corporation (“Colgate”), with offices at 300 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10022, and [FULL LEGAL ENTITY NAME], a [state/province/country] [corporation/LLC/LP/other type of entity] (“Company”), with offices at [address].  Colgate and Company are referred to herein collectively as the “Parties” and individually as a “Party.” In consideration of the promises and of the mutual agreements and covenants hereinafter set forth and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, and intending to be legally bound, the Parties agree as follows:

Objective.	Each Party may receive or have access to certain Confidential Information (as defined below) of the other Party in connection with the exploration of a business relationship between the Parties involving [description of purpose] (“Purpose”). Colgate may receive from Company [description of materials](“Company Materials”) for evaluation and testing purposes in connection with the Purpose. Company may receive from Colgate [description of materials](“Colgate Materials”)(Company Materials and Colgate Materials collectively “Materials”) for evaluation and testing purposes in connection with the Purpose. 

Definitions.

Definition of Confidential Information.  “Confidential Information” of a Disclosing Party shall mean (a) any information or data, whether technical or nontechnical, whether written (including graphic or electronic) and marked confidential or oral, disclosed by such Party or on such Party’s behalf to the Receiving Party, either directly or indirectly, on or after the Effective Date, and (b) the existence and terms of this Agreement and the fact that discussions or negotiations are taking place between the Parties concerning a possible business relationship. If Confidential Information is disclosed orally, the Disclosing Party shall confirm the confidential nature of such information in writing within 15 days after such oral disclosure. [Alternative definitions of Confidential Information to consider, in light of the needs of the transaction (note that alternative 1 by its nature cannot cover information disclosed before the NDA is signed unless additional language is added to do so expressly):

.    

Confidential Information shall not include information that the Receiving Party demonstrates (a) is publicly available as of the Effective Date or subsequently becomes publicly available through no fault or act of the Receiving Party, (b) is known to the Receiving Party prior to disclosure from the Disclosing Party, (c)  that the Receiving Party received from any third party not under any obligation to the Disclosing Party to keep such information confidential or (d) was independently developed by the Receiving Party without reliance upon or use of the Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party. 

The Company Materials are Confidential Information of the Company and the Colgate Materials are Confidential Information of Colgate.

Definition of Affiliates.  “Affiliate” shall mean an individual, trust, business trust, joint venture, partnership, corporation, association or any other entity which (directly or indirectly) is controlled by, controls, or is under common control with a Party.  For purposes of this definition, the term “control” (including, with correlative meanings, the term “controlled by” and “under common control with”) as used with respect to any Party, shall mean the possession (directly or indirectly) of power to direct or cause the direction of the management or policies of such Party.

Definition of Disclosing Party and Receiving Party.	The Party disclosing such Confidential Information or providing the Materials shall be deemed the “Disclosing Party” and the Party receiving such Confidential Information or the Materials shall be deemed the “Receiving Party.”

Confidentiality.

Obligation of Confidentiality.  The Receiving Party shall (a) maintain any Confidential Information in confidence, (b) take all necessary and reasonable precautions to prevent Confidential Information from being disclosed to any unauthorized third party, and (c) use Confidential Information exclusively for the Purpose.  The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to its directors, officers, employees, advisors or agents and the directors, officers, employees, advisors or agents of its Affiliates (collectively, “Representatives”), each with a need to know such Confidential Information in order to achieve the Purpose; provided that (i) the Receiving Party advises its Representatives of the confidential nature thereof and (ii) such Representatives are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as stringent as those set forth herein. The Receiving Party shall be liable to the Disclosing Party for any failure by any of its Representatives to treat any Confidential Information in the same manner as the Receiving Party is obligated to treat such Confidential Information under the terms of this Agreement.

Trade Secrets. No Disclosing Party shall disclose any “trade secrets” to the Receiving Party pursuant to this Agreement. For purposes of this Agreement “trade secrets” shall have the meaning ascribed to them in the Defend Trade Secrets Act of 2016.

Compelled Disclosures. In the event that the Receiving Party receives a subpoena or other government process that purports to require the production or disclosure of any Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party for use in an action or proceeding, the Receiving Party shall (a) promptly inform the party or entity issuing such subpoena or other government process of the existence of this Agreement, (b) promptly inform the Disclosing Party of the receipt of such subpoena or other government process and (c) not oppose any effort by the Disclosing Party to quash any such subpoena or other government process.  In the event that (x) the Disclosing Party fails to intervene to quash such subpoena or other government process after being given notice and a reasonable opportunity to do so or (y) such intervention fails or is denied by a court of competent jurisdiction, such Confidential Information may be produced but limited to what is strictly necessary, notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary.  In the event that any Confidential Information is ordered produced in an action or proceeding, such Confidential Information shall not lose its confidential status through such use, and the Receiving Party shall take all reasonable and necessary steps to protect the confidentiality of such Confidential Information during such use.

Use of Materials.  The Receiving Party shall not use the other Party’s Materials other than for the Purpose and expressly agrees not to reverse engineer the other Party’s Materials or the components thereof or analyze the Materials or the components thereof in order to determine their material composition. 

Residual Information.  Notwithstanding the confidentiality obligations contained in this Section 3, the Receiving Party may, during and after the term hereof, use in its business any Residual Information.  “Residual Information” means the ideas, know-how and techniques that would be retained in the unaided memory of an ordinary person skilled in the art, not intent on appropriating the proprietary information of the Disclosing Party, as a result of such person’s access to, use, review, evaluation, or testing of the Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party for the Purpose.  Nothing in this Section, however, shall be deemed to grant to the Receiving Party a license under the Disclosing Party’s patents or other intellectual property rights. 

Return of Confidential Information.  At the written request of the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party shall promptly return or destroy (at the sole discretion of the Receiving Party) all Confidential Information in its or its Representatives’ possession, respectively, and shall confirm such return or destruction; provided, however, that the Receiving Party may retain an archival copy or other appropriate record (including electronic backup copies created in the ordinary course) of any such Confidential Information.  Such copies and records may be used exclusively for internal recordkeeping and administrative purposes, to assure compliance with any applicable governmental requirements and for dispute resolution purposes.  In addition, and notwithstanding the foregoing, the Receiving Party shall promptly return all of the other Party’s unused Materials and shall have no right to retain such Materials for any reason.

Right to Disclose Information.  The Disclosing Party hereby represents and warrants that (a) its entry into this Agreement does not violate or constitute a breach of any agreement to which it is otherwise bound, (b) it has the right to disclose to the Receiving Party any Confidential Information disclosed by such Disclosing Party or on such Party’s behalf and (c) to the best of its knowledge, such disclosure does not violate or constitute a breach of any agreement or understanding, written or oral, to which such Party is bound.

Ownership.  

Ownership of Confidential Information. All Confidential Information (including all Materials) disclosed by the Disclosing Party or on its behalf to the Receiving Party or its Representatives pursuant to this Agreement shall be and remain the property of the Disclosing Party.  All data, information, analysis and reports (“Data and Reports”) about Confidential Information that is created or generated by a Receiving Party shall be owned and controlled exclusively by such Receiving Party (which includes without limitation the right to file patent applications on any inventions conceived by such Receiving Party that result from its proper use of Confidential Information hereunder), subject only to its duty hereunder to maintain the confidentiality of any Confidential Information contained in such Data and Reports.

Ownership of Evaluation Documentation.  All information and documentation generated in connection with the evaluation of Materials under this Agreement, including, without limitation, all data, reports, analyses and all documentation related thereto, shall be the sole and exclusive property of Colgate, and are Colgate Confidential Information. [Add the following if the other party requests it or if appropriate under the circumstances] The Receiving Party shall provide a summary of such evaluation documentation to the Disclosing Party promptly after its creation.  

Testing of Materials; Indemnity.  The Receiving Party shall maintain full and complete responsibility for the testing and other use of all Materials received by it, and for compliance with all laws of all governmental bodies with respect thereto, with respect to safety and otherwise.  The Receiving Party shall consult with its own advisors and consultants in determining such compliance, and the Disclosing Party will bear no responsibility with respect thereto. In no event shall the Disclosing Party be liable for any use of its Materials by the Receiving Party, provided that the Disclosing Party has disclosed to the Receiving Party any dangerous or hazardous properties regarding such Materials which are known and confirmed by the Disclosing Party as of the Effective Date or of which the Disclosing Party becomes aware during the term of this Agreement.  The Receiving Party shall indemnify, defend and hold the Disclosing Party, its officers, directors, employees and agents (collectively, the “Indemnitees”), and their respective successors, heirs and assigns, harmless from damages for any loss, claim, injury, liability, cost or expense (collectively, “Losses”) which may arise from (i) the Receiving Party’s testing, handling, storage or other use of the other Party’s Materials and/or (ii) the Receiving Party’s gross negligence or willful misconduct. 

Insurance. Company shall maintain at all times during the Term, and at its sole expense, such policy or policies of insurance, including a general liability, worker’s compensation and employers liability, as are necessary to cover all loss, destruction or damage for which Company has assumed responsibility under the terms of this Agreement, and shall name Colgate as an additional insured with respect to the general liability policy.  Company shall cause its insurance policies to provide a waiver of subrogation in favor of Colgate.  The policies shall be with at least a Standard & Poor’s A+ rated company providing limits of no less than $5,000,000.00 per occurrence.  Such limits can be satisfied with a primary policy or a combination of a primary and excess / umbrella policies.  Company shall promptly furnish upon request certificates of insurance to Colgate evidencing that the insurance required by this paragraph is in full force and effect. [The certificates of insurance required hereunder shall contain a clause which provides that there shall be no reduction, cancellation or expiration of, or other material change to the policy without at least thirty (30) days’ prior written notice to Colgate.

Absence of License. Except for the purpose of fulfilling obligations under this Agreement, nothing in this Agreement, by implication or otherwise, conveys to the Receiving Party any right or license with respect to any intellectual property or Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party.  No right is granted by this Agreement to the Receiving Party to use any registered or unregistered trademark, service mark or trade name of the Disclosing Party.

Freedom of Action.  Company acknowledges that Colgate and its Affiliates are, and will continue to be, in the business of creating, acquiring, developing and improving technology and/or products that are, or may be, similar to, competitive with or a replacement for the Company’s technology and/or products. Subject to Colgate’s obligations under this Agreement, Colgate and its Affiliates are and shall be free to create, acquire, develop or improve (or engage a third party to create, acquire, develop or improve) any technology and/or products, whether or not such technology and/or products are similar to, competitive with or a replacement for the Company’s technology and/or products. Any such technology and/or products, and any intellectual property associated therewith, that is created, acquired, developed or improved by or on behalf of Colgate without reference to the Confidential Information of the Company shall be owned exclusively by Colgate.

No Commitments.  Nothing in this Agreement nor in any previous or contemporaneous communications or understandings, whether oral or written, shall be deemed to provide any commitment of any kind or intent by either Party to enter into any further agreement with the other Party or to disclose any Confidential Information hereunder, and neither Party has acted or shall act in reliance on any potential further agreement.  

Disclaimer.  Neither Party makes any representation or warranty, express or implied, as to the accuracy or completeness of any Confidential Information provided hereunder, all of which shall be provided “as is.”

Limitations of Liability.  EXCEPT FOR THIRD-PARTY CLAIMS SUBJECT TO INDEMNIFICATION PURSUANT TO SECTION 5 AND TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY HAVE ANY LIABILITY TO THE OTHER PARTY, ANY OF THE OTHER PARTY’S AFFILIATES OR ANY THIRD PARTY ARISING OUT OF, RELATED TO OR IN CONNECTION WITH THIS AGREEMENT, REGARDLESS OF THE FORM OF THE ACTION, WHETHER IN CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY, PRODUCT LIABILITY OR OTHERWISE:

FOR INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, INDIRECT, SPECIAL, PUNITIVE OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES OR LIABILITIES OF ANY KIND OR FOR LOSS OF REVENUE OR PROFITS OR LOSS OF BUSINESS; OR

IN AN AGGREGATE AMOUNT IN EXCESS OF $[●].

Governing Law.  This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of State of New York, without giving effect to any choice of law or conflicts of law rules or provisions.

Disputes.   Subject to Section 12.4 below, any dispute between the Parties arising out of, related to or in connection with this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively by invoking the following dispute resolution procedure:

The Parties agree to make a diligent, good faith effort to resolve all disputes amicably if at all possible. To this end, authorized representatives of each Party shall meet within fifteen (15) days after receipt of written notice by either Party at a mutually agreeable time and place to discuss possible resolution of the dispute.

In the event that the Parties are unable to resolve the dispute within fifteen (15) days after their meeting, then either Party may invoke non-binding mediation under the International Institute for Conflict Prevention & Resolution (“CPR”) Mediation Procedure then in effect. Unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties, the Parties will select a single mediator from the CPR Panels of Distinguished Neutrals. The mediation proceeding shall be conducted in New York, New York, or such other location as may be agreed in writing by the Parties. The Parties shall (a) share equally the fees and expenses of the mediator; and (b) bear their own attorneys’ fees and associated costs and expenses. At the request of either Party, the mediator shall enter an appropriate protective order to maintain the confidentiality of information produced or exchanged in the course of the mediation proceedings. The Parties shall use their best efforts to complete the mediation procedure provided for in this Section 12 within no more than sixty (60) days.

After (i) completion of the process described in Section 12.1 and Section 12.2 above or (ii) the non-cooperation of either Party in the completion of the stated procedure, then either Party (in the case of clause (i)) or the cooperating Party (in the case of clause (ii)) may initiate an action in court against the other, but such action may only be brought in a court having jurisdiction pursuant to Section 13 of this Agreement. All applicable statutes of limitation and defenses based upon the passage of time shall be tolled while the process described in Section 12.1 and Section 12.2 above is pending. The Parties shall take such action, if any, required to effectuate such tolling.

Nothing in this Section 12 shall be construed to prevent either Party from seeking injunctive relief against the other Party from any judicial or administrative authority of competent jurisdiction to enjoin such other Party from breaching any provision of this Agreement pending the resolution of a dispute as hereinbefore provided.

Venue.  All disputes arising out of this Agreement (and all amendments and attachments hereto) shall be exclusively resolved in a court of competent jurisdiction in New York County in the State of New York. Each Party expressly consents to the jurisdiction of the state or federal courts in New York County in the State of New York and waives any objections or right as to forum non conveniens, lack of personal jurisdiction or similar grounds. EACH PARTY HEREBY IRREVOCABLY AND UNCONDITIONALLY WAIVES ALL RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION (WHETHER BASED ON CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE) ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, OR THE PERFORMANCE UNDER OR ENFORCEMENT OF THIS AGREEMENT.

Compliance with Laws.  In connection with its performance of this Agreement, Company shall comply with all applicable laws, rules, regulations and treaties, including but not limited to all applicable anti-corruption, competition, environmental, labor, product and ingredient laws, rules, regulations and treaties.  Failure to comply with applicable laws may be deemed a material breach of this Agreement.

Assignment.  This Agreement or any of the Parties’ rights and obligations can only be assigned, transferred or delegated (collectively “to assign” or “assignment”) with the other Party’s express prior written consent; provided that Company’s consent is not necessary if Colgate assigns to any of its Affiliates.  When duly assigned, this Agreement shall be binding on each Party’s successors and assigns.

Entire Agreement; Amendment.  This Agreement supersedes all previous and contemporaneous communications and understandings, whether oral or written, and constitutes the sole and entire agreement between the Parties pertaining to the Confidential Information.  No modification, deletion, addition or waiver of the terms of this Agreement shall be binding on either Party unless made in writing and signed by a duly authorized representative of each Party.

Term; Termination.  

The term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and continue in effect for one (1) year.

This Agreement may be terminated by either Party for any or no reason by providing the other Party with written notice at least thirty (30) days prior to the desired effective date of termination.  

Survival.  The obligations of confidentiality and non-use set forth herein shall apply during the term of this Agreement and survive for a period of five (5) years after the expiration or termination of this Agreement pursuant to Section 18.  All other provisions which by their nature should survive the termination of this Agreement shall survive any such termination.

Headings; Construction.  Headings in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement or of any provision herein.  Each Party has been represented by counsel, or has had the opportunity to be represented by counsel, in connection with this Agreement and, accordingly, any rule of law or any legal doctrine that would require interpretation of any claimed ambiguities in this Agreement against the drafting Party has no application and is expressly waived.

Non-Waiver.  No failure or delay by either Party to exercise any right or remedy hereunder shall operate as a waiver thereof, nor shall a single or partial exercise by either Party of any right or remedy preclude any further exercise thereof or the exercise of any other right or remedy.

Severability.  If any portion of this Agreement is to any extent determined to be illegal, invalid or unenforceable by a court or arbiter of competent jurisdiction, the remainder of this Agreement will not be affected and will remain valid and enforceable.  In addition, the affected portion of this Agreement will remain in effect in all circumstances other than the circumstances that caused the court or arbiter to find that part to be illegal, invalid or unenforceable.

Notices.  Each Party shall deliver all notices required pursuant to Sections 13 and 18 under this Agreement (each, a “Notice”) in writing and in English, referring to this Agreement and addressed to the other Party at its address below or to the last address the receiving Party provided to the other Party in compliance with this Section. The Parties shall deliver any Notice by personal delivery, reputable overnight courier (all fees prepaid), or certified or registered mail (postage prepaid, return receipt requested). A Notice shall be deemed received (a) on the date of personal or courier delivery or (b) if mailed, on the date of receipt or refusal indicated on the return receipt.

Independent Contractors.  The Parties acknowledge that they are engaged in independent business, and this Agreement shall not be deemed to (a) make either Party a partner, joint venturer, agent or other representative of the other Party or (b) grant either Party any right to assume or create any obligation in the name or on behalf of the other Party or to accept legal summons or legal process for the other Party.  Nothing contained herein shall be construed as creating a joint venture, partnership, agency, employment relationship or other enterprise between the Parties and no duties or rights not expressly set forth herein shall be implied.
