GRANT AGREEMENT

This grant AGREEMENT is entered into as of the date of the last signature below (the “Effective Date”) by and between Colgate-Palmolive Company, a Delaware corporation, having its principal offices at 300 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10022 (“Colgate”), and [●], a [●] organized under the laws of [●], having its principal offices at [●] (“Recipient”).  Colgate and Recipient are sometimes hereinafter referred to collectively as the “Parties” and individually as a “Party.”

RECITALS

WHEREAS, Colgate desires to provide a grant to Recipient, as more specifically set forth in this Agreement; and

WHEREAS Colgate and Recipient desire to enter into this Agreement to govern the provision and receipt of such grant.

AGREEMENT

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the promises and the undertakings of the Parties hereinafter set forth, the Parties agree as follows:

DEFINITIONS

“Affiliate” means, with respect to a Person, an individual, trust, business trust, joint venture, partnership, corporation, association or any other entity which (directly or indirectly) is controlled by, controls, or is under common control with a Person.  For purposes of this definition, the term “control” (including, with correlative meanings, the term “controlled by” and “under common control with”) as used with respect to any Person, shall mean the possession (directly or indirectly) of power to direct or cause the direction of the management or policies of such Person.

“Breaching Party” is defined in Section 6.2.1.

“Claims” is defined in Section 5.1.

“Colgate” is defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

 “Effective Date” is defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Governmental Authority” means any legislative, executive or judicial unit of any governmental or quasi-governmental authority or instrumentality (multi-national, national, federal, state, provincial, local or foreign, international or domestic), or any department, agency, board, bureau, commission, official or other regulatory, administrative or judicial authority thereof, including any administrative or regulatory agency or commission, and any court or arbitration tribunal, in each instance having jurisdiction over the subject matter before it.

“Grant Amount” is defined in Section 3.1.

“Indemnity Claim” is defined in Section 5.2.

 “Law” means all supranational, international, national, state and local laws, statutes, regulations, rules, codes or ordinances enacted, adopted, issued or promulgated by any Governmental Authority or common law.

 “Nonbreaching Party” is defined in Section 6.2.1.

“Notice” is defined in Section 7.2.

“Party” and “Parties” are defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Person” means any natural person, corporation, limited liability company, trust, joint venture, association, company, partnership or other entity.

 “Recipient” is defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Representatives” means, for a Party, its directors, officers, employees, advisors or agents and the directors, officers, employees, advisors or agents of its Affiliates.

“Research Project” is defined in Section 2.1.

“Research Project Leader” is defined in Section 2.1.

“Term” is defined in Section 6.1.

“Third Party” means any entity other than Recipient or Colgate or an Affiliate of either Party.

GENERAL OBLIGATIONS

Grant. Recipient shall use the Grant Amount only for the following research project: [•] (“Research Project”). The Research Project shall be led and carried out by [•] who is a full-time faculty member of Recipient (“Research Project Leader”). 

Reports

The Research Project Leader shall provide a progress report to Colgate every six (6) months after the Effective Date until the Research Project has been completed. Such report shall include scientific advances, timeline required to finish the Research Project, percentage of the budget used, challenges, obstacles and any modification(s) of the protocol with the proper justification.

Within thirty (30) days of completion of the Research Project, the Research Project Leader shall provide a final report to Colgate. Such report shall include (i) scientific achievements, results, manuscripts prepared for publication and plans for future grant application, and (ii) a final financial report.

Presentation. At Colgate’s request and subject to a separate agreement between the Parties (“Speaker Agreement”), the Research Project Leader and the Research Project Leader’s mentor at Recipient shall travel to and present the results of the Research Project at Colgate’s facilities in Piscataway, New Jersey (the “Event”).  Subject to Colgate’s travel policy and approval, any travel required by the Research Project Leader and the Research Project Leader’s mentor to attend the Event shall be reimbursed by Colgate as detailed in the Speaker Agreement.

Disclosure.  If Recipient intends to present the results of the Research Project at a non-Colgate venue, Recipient shall advise Colgate in writing at least thirty (30) days before the presentation, which may be via email to the Colgate CARE Program administrator, Zoe Scoulos, at zoe_scoulos@colpal.com, and include an abstract of the presentation and a current progress report.

Publication. Any publication about the Research Project shall carry the following mention: “This research project has been made possible through a grant from Colgate-Palmolive Company”.

GRANT AMOUNT

Grant Amount.  Colgate shall pay to Recipient a grant in the amount of [●] (“Grant Amount”), which shall become due upon the Effective Date.  Such Grant Amount shall be the total amount payable under this Agreement and shall include compensation for all costs, expenses, overhead and fees in connection with this Agreement. 

Payment.  Recipient agrees to establish an account with Colgate’s electronic invoicing provider for the submission and payment of all invoices. Recipient shall submit an invoice electronically and all payments will be made by Colgate to Recipient via a wire transfer. The Grant Amount shall be payable by Colgate within ninety (90) days after receipt of an acceptable invoice from Recipient. Any sales, use, excise, value-added or other taxes or duties and penalties and interest relating thereto shall be the sole responsibility of Recipient.  

GENERAL REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES; LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

General Warranties.  Each Party represents and warrants to the other Party that:

the execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement by such Party have been duly authorized by all necessary action on the part of such Party;

this Agreement, when executed and delivered by such Party in accordance with the provisions hereof, will be a legal, valid and binding obligation of such Party, enforceable against such Party in accordance with its terms, except as such enforceability may be limited by applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, moratorium, reorganization or similar Laws affecting the enforcement of creditors’ rights generally and by general principles of equity; 

such Party’s execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement shall not constitute a violation, breach or default under any contract, instrument, obligation or agreement to which it is a Party or by which it is bound, and will not conflict with or violate any applicable Law of any Governmental Authority having jurisdiction over it or its assets or property; and

such Party shall comply with all applicable Laws in connection with the implementation of the Research Project under this Agreement.

Compliance with Policies.  In connection with the implementation of the Research Project, Recipient shall comply with the generally applicable policies of Colgate provided to Recipient in writing from time to time.  Without limiting the foregoing:

Third Party Code of Conduct. Colgate’s Third Party Code of Conduct is available at https://www.colgatepalmolive.com/en/us/corp/about/governance/third-party-code-of-conduct.  Recipient represents and warrants that it is in compliance with Colgate’s Third Party Code of Conduct and will remain in compliance throughout the Term.  Recipient will not unreasonably withhold agreement to comply with subsequent amendments of Colgate’s Third Party Code of Conduct that are communicated to Recipient from time to time.  Failure to comply with Colgate’s Third Party Code of Conduct may be deemed a material breach of this Agreement. 

Global Anti-Bribery Policy. Recipient shall comply with the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (the “FCPA”), as well as all additional applicable anti-bribery laws, treaties and regulations.  Attached and incorporated by reference to this Agreement as Exhibit A is a copy of Colgate’s Global Anti-Bribery Policy.  Recipient has reviewed the contents of Colgate’s Global Anti-Bribery Policy and shall abide by its terms.  Recipient will not unreasonably withhold agreement to comply with subsequent amendments of Colgate’s Global Anti-Bribery Policy that are communicated to Recipient from time to time.  Failure to comply with Colgate’s Global Anti-Bribery Policy or applicable anti-corruption laws shall be deemed a material and incurable breach of this Agreement.

Recipient’s Maintenance of Insurance.  Recipient shall be responsible for its own insurance coverage, including any claims for personal injury or property damage which might arise while carrying out the Research Project.  Recipient must provide, upon request, valid proof of any required insurance and is required to notify Colgate in writing within five (5) business days of any cancellation or material change to such insurance.

Limitations of Liability.  TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW, IN NO EVENT SHALL COLGATE OWE ANY DAMAGES OR HAVE ANY LIABILITY TO RECIPIENT, THE RESEARCH PROJECT LEADER, ANY OF RECIPIENT’S AFFILIATES OR ANY THIRD PARTY ARISING OUT OF, RELATED TO OR IN CONNECTION WITH THIS AGREEMENT, REGARDLESS OF THE FORM OF THE ACTION, WHETHER IN CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY, PRODUCT LIABILITY OR OTHERWISE: FOR INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, INDIRECT, SPECIAL, PUNITIVE OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES OR LIABILITIES OF ANY KIND OR FOR LOSS OF REVENUE OR PROFITS OR LOSS OF BUSINESS; OR IN AN AGGREGATE AMOUNT IN EXCESS OF THE TOTAL AMOUNTS PAID BY COLGATE TO RECIPIENT PURSUANT TO THIS AGREEMENT.

INDEMNIFICATION

Indemnification by Recipient.  Recipient agrees to defend, indemnify and hold harmless Colgate, Colgate’s Affiliates and their Representatives, from and against any and all losses, liabilities, damages, settlement amounts, and reasonable attorneys’ fees, disbursements and costs (including any reasonable costs of investigation) arising from any actions, suits, threats, allegations, demands or claims brought by any Third Party (collectively, “Claims”), resulting from or relating to (a) the gross negligence, bad faith or intentional or willful misconduct of Recipient, the Research Project Leader or Recipient’s Affiliates or Representatives, (b) breach of any of Recipient’s representations, warranties, covenants or agreements contained herein, and/or(c) violation of Law by Recipient, the Research Project Leader or Recipient’s Affiliates or Representatives in connection with this Agreement.

Indemnification Claims.  Colgate agrees to give Recipient prompt written notice of any matter upon which any indemnified Person intends to base a claim for indemnification (an “Indemnity Claim”) under this Article 5, provided, however, that any delay in providing or failure to provide such notice shall not relieve Recipient of any of its obligations hereunder except to the extent that Recipient is materially prejudiced by such failure.  Recipient shall have the right to participate jointly with the indemnified Person in the indemnified Person’s defense, settlement or other disposition of any Indemnity Claim.  With respect to any Indemnity Claim relating solely to the payment of money damages which could not result in the indemnified Person becoming subject to injunctive or other equitable relief or otherwise adversely affect the business of the indemnified Person in any manner, and as to which Recipient shall have acknowledged in writing the obligation to indemnify the indemnified Person hereunder, Recipient shall have the sole right to defend, settle or otherwise dispose of such Indemnity Claim, on such terms as Recipient, in its sole discretion, shall deem appropriate; provided that Recipient shall provide reasonable evidence of its ability to pay any damages claimed and with respect to any such settlement shall have obtained the written release of the indemnified Person from the Indemnity Claim.  Recipient shall obtain the written consent of the indemnified Person, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, prior to ceasing to defend, settling or otherwise disposing of any Indemnity Claim if as a result thereof the indemnified Person would become subject to injunctive or other equitable relief or the business of the indemnified Person would be adversely affected in any manner.

TERM AND TERMINATION OF AGREEMENT.

Term.  This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and, unless terminated earlier pursuant to this Article, shall continue in force and effect for one (1) year from receipt by University of the Grant Amount. If further time is needed to complete the Research Project, this Agreement may be extended for additional time (not to exceed one year) at no additional cost to Colgate by the mutual agreement of both Parties in writing, which may be via email (the “Term”).

Termination.  This Agreement may be terminated as follows:

Material Breach.  This Agreement may be terminated by either Party (the “Nonbreaching Party”) upon written notice thereof to the other Party (the “Breaching Party”) in the event of a material breach of this Agreement by the Breaching Party which is not cured within sixty (60) days after the receipt by the Breaching Party of written notice from the Nonbreaching Party, specifying in reasonable detail the nature of such breach.  If such breach is not cured within such cure period, this Agreement shall terminate as set forth in the Nonbreaching Party’s notice of breach and in accordance with the terms of this Article; provided, however, that this Agreement shall not be terminated prior to the end of such cure period.

Insolvency.  This Agreement may be terminated by either Party upon sixty (60) days’ prior written notice to the other Party at any time during this Agreement if the other Party: (a) files in any court pursuant to any statute a petition in bankruptcy or insolvency or for reorganization or for an arrangement or for the appointment of a receiver or trustee of the other Party, or of its assets; (b) proposes a written agreement of composition for extension of its debts; (c) is served with an involuntary petition against it, filed in any insolvency proceeding, and such petition shall not be dismissed within sixty (60) days after filing thereof; or (d) makes an assignment for the benefit of its creditors.  The Party affected shall immediately notify the other Party in writing of the occurrence of any of the foregoing events.

Cumulative Remedies.  Except as expressly stated otherwise herein, remedies under this Agreement are cumulative, and nothing in this Agreement shall prevent any Party, in the case of a material breach (after expiration of applicable cure period and notice periods), from terminating this Agreement and seeking to enforce its rights under this Agreement.

Survival.  All provisions under this Agreement which by their terms survive, or by their nature should survive, expiration or any earlier termination of this Agreement shall survive any such expiration or termination, including Article 1, Section 4.4, Article 5, Section 6.3, this Section 6.4, and Article 7.

MISCELLANEOUS

Intellectual Property; Use of Names and Trademarks. Nothing in this Agreement, by implication or otherwise, conveys to Recipient any right or license with respect to any intellectual property of Colgate.  Neither Party nor its Affiliates shall make any oral or written statement or perform any act indicating that the other Party or its Affiliates endorses or approves, or has endorsed or approved, such Party or its products or services.  Nothing contained in this Agreement will be construed as conferring any right to use in advertising, publicity or other promotional activities any name, trade name, trademark, service mark or other designation of a Party (including any contraction, abbreviation or simulation of any of the foregoing) without the prior written approval of such Party.

Notices.  The Parties shall deliver all notices, claims, demands, consents, approvals and other communications under this Agreement (each, a “Notice”) in writing and in English, referring to this Agreement and addressed to the other Party at its address below or to the last address the receiving Party provided to the other Party in compliance with this section.  The Parties shall deliver any Notice by personal delivery, reputable overnight courier (all fees prepaid), certified or registered mail (postage prepaid, return receipt requested) or by email.  A Notice shall be deemed received (i) on the date of personal or courier delivery, (ii) if mailed, on the date of receipt or refusal indicated on the return receipt or (iii) if emailed, upon receipt by the sending Party of an email acknowledgment of receipt by the receiving Party; provided that a “read receipt” or other automatic email response shall not qualify for this purpose.

Entire Agreement; Amendment.  This Agreement and its attachments contain the entire understanding among the Parties and supersede any and all prior agreements, understandings and arrangements whether written or oral among the Parties with respect to the matters contained in this Agreement.  No amendments, changes, modifications or alterations of the terms and conditions of this Agreement shall be binding upon any Party, unless in writing and signed by an authorized Representative of each Party.

Governing Law.  This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of State of New York, without giving effect to any choice of law or conflicts of law rules or provisions. 

Dispute Resolution. Subject to Section 7.5.3 below, any dispute between the Parties arising out of, related to or in connection with this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively by invoking the following dispute resolution procedure:

The Parties agree to make a diligent, good faith effort to resolve all disputes amicably if at all possible. To this end, authorized representatives of each Party shall meet within fifteen (15) days after receipt of written notice by either Party at a mutually agreeable time and place to discuss possible resolution of the dispute.

After (i) completion of the process described in Section 7.5.1 above or (ii) the non-cooperation of either Party in the completion of the stated procedure, then either Party may initiate an action in court against the other, but such action may only be brought in a court having jurisdiction pursuant to Section 7.6 of this Agreement. All applicable statutes of limitation and defenses based upon the passage of time shall be tolled while the process described in Section 7.5.1 above is pending. The Parties shall take such action, if any, required to effectuate such tolling.

Nothing in this Section 7.5 shall be construed to prevent either Party from seeking injunctive relief against the other Party from any judicial or administrative authority of competent jurisdiction to enjoin such other Party from breaching any provision of this Agreement pending the resolution of a dispute as hereinbefore provided.

Venue.  All disputes arising out of this Agreement (and all amendments and attachments hereto) shall be exclusively resolved in a court of competent jurisdiction in the State of New York. Each Party expressly consents to the jurisdiction of the state or federal courts in the State of New York and waives any objections or right as to forum non conveniens, lack of personal jurisdiction or similar grounds. Each Party hereby irrevocably and unconditionally waives all right to trial by jury in any action (whether based on contract, tort or otherwise) arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or its performance under or the enforcement of this Agreement.

Assignment.  This Agreement or any of the Parties’ rights and obligations can only be assigned, transferred or delegated (collectively “to assign” or “assignment”) with the other Party’s express prior written consent; provided that Recipient’s consent is not necessary if Colgate assigns to any of its Affiliates. When duly assigned, this Agreement shall be binding on each Party’s successors and assigns.

Confidentiality. Subject to Section 2.4, Recipient and the Research Project Leader shall keep the existence and the terms of this Agreement confidential. Recipient and the Research Project Leader may disclose the existence and the terms of this Agreement to Recipient’s Representatives only as may be necessary in the ordinary course of carrying out the Research Project. The obligations contained in this Section 7.8 shall survive for five (5) years following the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

Counterparts.  This Agreement may have multiple signature pages signed separately in different locations which, when together, shall be considered one and the same Agreement as of the date the last Party signed, and shall become a binding Agreement when the signed signature pages have been delivered to the other Party.  Each Party is permitted to deliver this Agreement to the other Party by sending a copy of their signed signature pages via facsimile or as an attachment in portable document format (PDF) or other email attachment format, e-signature, to an email addressed to the other Party.

Rules of Construction.  The Parties hereto agree that they have been represented or have had the opportunity to be represented by counsel during the negotiation and execution of this Agreement and, therefore, waive the application of any Law (including any rule of construction) providing that ambiguities in an agreement or other document will be construed against the Party drafting such agreement or document.  Whenever the context hereof shall so require, the singular shall include the plural, the male gender shall include the female gender and neuter, and vice versa.  Whenever the words “include,” “includes” or “including” are used in this Agreement, they shall be deemed to be followed by the words “without limitation” whether or not such words actually appear thereafter.  Whenever the word “or” is used in this Agreement, it shall not be deemed to be exclusive.  Headings in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement or of any provision herein.  This Agreement has been fully negotiated by the Parties and shall not be construed by any Governmental Authority against either Party by virtue of the fact that such Party was the drafting party.

Waiver.  The waiver by any Party hereto of a breach of any provision of this Agreement shall not operate or be construed as a waiver of any subsequent breach.

Severability.  If any portion of this Agreement is to any extent determined to be illegal, invalid or unenforceable by a court or arbiter of competent jurisdiction, the remainder of this Agreement will not be affected and will remain valid and enforceable.  In addition, the affected portion of this Agreement will remain in effect in all circumstances other than the circumstances that caused the court or arbiter to find that part to be illegal, invalid or unenforceable.

Independent Contractors.  Nothing in this Agreement shall operate to or be construed or interpreted as to render the Parties hereto as other than independent contractors, nor shall anything in this Agreement operate or be construed or interpreted as to render any Party, or any of such Party’s Representatives, to be employees, agents, associates, joint ventures or partners of the other Party.

COLGATE-PALMOLIVE COMPANY FCPA AND ANTI-BRIBERY POLICY

GLOBAL ANTI-BRIBERY POLICY







Our Anti-Bribery Commitment



Colgate’s commitment to dealing legally and ethically applies worldwide.  We comply with all applicable anti-bribery laws, including but not limited to the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (“FCPA”), everywhere we do business, and we expect the same of the third parties with whom we work.    While  the  FCPA  prohibits,  among  other  things,  bribery  of  foreign  government officials and entities, other anti-bribery laws, like the UK Bribery Act, prohibit commercial bribery between private individuals and entities.





Colgate people and any third parties acting on our behalf or in connection with our business are prohibited from giving or offering anything of value directly or indirectly to any government official or entity, or to any private individual or entity, in order to improperly obtain or retain any business advantage or to improperly affect any act or decision.





This prohibition includes any facilitating, expediting or “grease” payments made to government officials, either directly or indirectly, in order to expedite any official service or function (for example, small payments made to an official to move Colgate’s application to the front of the line or to shorten the time frame in which services or other actions are provided).  Any official fees supported by government-issued receipts do not qualify as improper payments.



Maintaining Accurate Books and Records



No payment by or on behalf of the Company shall be approved or made if any part of the payment is to be used for an unlawful or improper purpose, or for any purpose other than that described by valid documents supporting the payment.  No false or misleading entries should be made in any books or financial records of the Company for any reason.



Any expenses that an employee or third party incurs on Colgate’s behalf or in connection with our business shall not be reimbursable unless they are lawful and supported by detailed documentation including, for example, valid invoices or receipts.







Expenditures Related to Government Officials



No funds may be provided to or spent on behalf of a government official or entity, directly or indirectly, without advance written approval from Colgate’s Global Legal Organization.  This includes any payments, gifts, donations, entertainment, travel, meals, or other items of value. (For additional information, please review the Global Policy on Expenditures Related to Government Officials & Governments.)  Advance approval is not required for official fees supported by government-issued receipts (e.g., permit or license fees).

Please note that the term “government official” is widely defined and may include individuals who are employed by any public or state-affiliated institution or organization or who act in an official capacity in any way, whether full-time, part-time or unpaid.  Government officials can be found in every branch and level of government and public life and may include anyone from low-level customs employees, to employees of state-owned media outlets, to high-ranking lawmakers, as well as researchers, professors, teachers, dentists, veterinarians, or other professionals and Key Thought Leaders.  If you are in doubt as to whether an individual could be considered a government official, you should contact the Global Legal Organization.



Commercial Bribery



In addition to prohibiting bribery of government officials, Colgate also prohibits its employees and third parties from engaging in bribery of private parties.  You should not seek to improperly influence the judgment or conduct of any party with whom you might be conducting Company business by offering or providing any payments, gifts or other benefits, or by any other unlawful inducement.

Our Expectations



Colgate’s reputation depends on the conduct of our employees as well as the conduct of those with whom we do business.  It is our goal to ensure that Colgate People and the third parties with whom we work reflect the same high ethical standards and demonstrate a commitment to compliance with all applicable laws.  We further expect our third parties to ensure that their employees and subcontractors understand and comply with this Anti-Bribery Policy.

Failure to comply with this Anti-Bribery Policy or any applicable anti-bribery laws, including but not limited to the FCPA, may result in civil or criminal penalties, as well as termination of the employment or business relationship.













Any questions regarding this policy may be directed to our Global Compliance Legal Specialist: Legal_Compliance@colpal.com

CONSULTANT SERVICES AGREEMENT

THIS CONSULTANT SERVICES AGREEMENT is entered into as of the date of the last signature below (the “Effective Date”) by and between Colgate-Palmolive Company, a Delaware corporation, having its principal offices at 300 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10022 (“Colgate”), and [●],  a [state]  [corporate entity type] having its principal offices at (“Consultant”).  COLGATE and Consultant are sometimes hereinafter referred to collectively as the “Parties” and individually as a “Party.”

RECITALS

WHEREAS, COLGATE desires to have Consultant carry out services for COLGATE or its Affiliates, as more specifically set forth in Exhibit A to this Agreement; and

WHEREAS, COLGATE and Consultant desire to enter into this Agreement to govern the provision and receipt of such services.

AGREEMENT

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the premises and the undertakings of the Parties hereinafter set forth, the Parties agree as follows:

DEFINITIONS

“Affiliate” means, with respect to a Person, an individual, trust, business trust, joint venture, partnership, corporation, association or any other entity which (directly or indirectly) is controlled by, controls, or is under common control with a Person.  For purposes of this definition, the term “control” (including, with correlative meanings, the term “controlled by” and “under common control with”) as used with respect to any Person, shall mean the possession (directly or indirectly) of power to direct or cause the direction of the management or policies of such Person.

“Agreement” means this Consultant Services Agreement and all Exhibits hereto, as the same may be amended or modified from time to time in accordance with the terms hereof.

“Background IP” means Intellectual Property under the control of a Party that was developed or acquired by the Party prior to the Effective Date or independently and outside the activities contemplated by this Agreement without reference to or use of the other Party’s Confidential Information or Background IP. For purposes of this definition, a Party “controls” Intellectual Property if it owns or otherwise has the right to license or sublicense such Intellectual Property.

“Breaching Party” is defined in Section 9.2.1.

“Claims” is defined in Section 7.1.

“COLGATE” is defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“COLGATE Confidential Information” means (a) any information or data, whether technical or nontechnical, whether written (including graphic or electronic) and marked confidential or oral, disclosed by COLGATE or its Affiliates or on COLGATE’s behalf to Consultant, either directly or indirectly, on or after the Effective Date [or previously under a Prior Non-Disclosure Agreement], and (b) the existence and terms of this Agreement.  If COLGATE Confidential Information is disclosed orally, COLGATE shall provide a summary and confirm the confidential nature of such information in writing within fifteen (15) days after such oral disclosure.  For the avoidance of doubt, COLGATE Confidential Information shall include Foreground IP, Materials, Deliverables and [●].

“Confidential Information” means COLGATE Confidential Information or Consultant Confidential Information, as the context requires.

“Consultant” is defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Consultant Confidential Information” means (a) any information or data, whether technical or nontechnical, whether written (including graphic or electronic) and marked confidential or oral, disclosed by Consultant or on Consultant’s behalf to COLGATE, either directly or indirectly, on or after the Effective Date [or previously under a Prior Non-Disclosure Agreement], excluding all COLGATE Confidential information, and (b) the existence and terms of this Agreement; provided that Consultant Confidential Information shall not include any Foreground IP.  If Consultant Confidential Information is disclosed orally, Consultant shall provide a summary and confirm the confidential nature of such information in writing within fifteen (15) days after such oral disclosure.

“Deliverables” is defined in Section 2.1.

“Disclosing Party” means the Party disclosing Confidential Information.

“Effective Date” is defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Fees” is defined in Section 3.1.

“Force Majeure” is defined in Section 10.1.

“Foreground IP” means Intellectual Property that is created by the Representatives of  Consultant or the Representatives of COLGATE, individually or jointly, while performing or receiving the Services.

“Governmental Authority” means any legislative, executive or judicial unit of any governmental or quasi-governmental authority or instrumentality (multi-national, national, federal, state, provincial, local or foreign, international or domestic), or any department, agency, board, bureau, commission, official or other regulatory, administrative or judicial authority thereof, including any administrative or regulatory agency or commission, and any court or arbitration tribunal, in each instance having jurisdiction over the subject matter before it.

“Indemnity Claim” is defined in Section 7.2.

“Intellectual Property” means all discoveries, inventions, improvements, developments, procedures, processes, formulations, know-how, trade secrets, formulae, trademarks, service marks, trade dress, designs, logos, packaging, proprietary information, technical information, techniques, works of authorship, drawings, models, manuals and systems, whether or not patentable or copyrightable or otherwise registerable, and all rights and applications or registrations derived or derivable therefrom.

“Law” means all supranational, international, national, state and local laws, statutes, regulations, rules, codes or ordinances enacted, adopted, issued or promulgated by any Governmental Authority or common law.

“Materials” is defined in Section 2.3.

“Nonbreaching Party” is defined in Section 9.2.1.

“Party” and “Parties” are defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Person” means any natural person, corporation, limited liability company, trust, joint venture, association, company, partnership or other entity.

“Prior Non-Disclosure Agreements” mean [●].

“Receiving Party” means the Party receiving Confidential Information.

“Representatives” means, for a Party, its directors, officers, employees, advisors or agents and the directors, officers, employees, advisors or agents of its Affiliates.

“Service Exhibit” is defined in Section 2.1.

“Services” is defined in Section 2.2.

“Term” is defined in Section 9.1.

“Third Party” means any entity other than Consultant or COLGATE or an Affiliate of COLGATE.

GENERAL OBLIGATIONS

Service Exhibit.  Exhibit A hereto (the “Service Exhibit”) sets forth the services and other activities to be conducted by Consultant.  The Service Exhibit identifies: (a) a description of the services to be provided by Consultant; (b) the schedule under which such services are to be performed; (c) the deliverables to be provided by Consultant to COLGATE (the “Deliverables”); (d) COLGATE’s primary contact for receipt of the services; and (e) the Fees (as defined below).

Performance of Services.  Consultant shall, and shall cause its Representatives and permitted subcontractors to, perform all of the services set forth in the Service Exhibit (including the delivery of the Deliverables), together with any services not specifically described in the Service Exhibit but which are inherent in or a necessary part of the services described in the Service Exhibit, or are reasonably required for proper performance of such services (collectively, the “Services”).  Consultant shall be responsible for acquiring all necessary equipment, materials and tools necessary to perform the Services other than the Materials, if any.  [All Deliverables delivered by Consultant are subject to COLGATE’s acceptance, and Consultant shall re-perform and re-deliver any Deliverable that is not accepted by COLGATE.  No payment under this Agreement by COLGATE shall be evidence of the performance of Consultant or the acceptance of any Deliverable.]

Removal of Personnel. Consultant shall maintain staffing levels and continuity of personnel consistent with its obligation to perform the Services.  [Consultant shall not remove or redeploy personnel performing the Services without the prior written permission of Colgate.]  If any Representatives performing the Services are unacceptable to Colgate for any reason, Colgate reserves the right to notify Consultant in which case Consultant shall immediately remove such Representatives from performing the Services hereunder and, if requested by Colgate, provide a qualified replacement.  If Consultant provides replacement Representatives for any reason, Consultant shall not charge Colgate for the number of hours required to train the replacement until such Representatives are familiar with the particular Services, so that such replacement Representatives are capable of performing the Services in accordance with this Agreement. 

Materials.  COLGATE will provide the materials identified in the Service Exhibit, if any (the “Materials”), to Consultant for the performance of the Services.  Consultant shall not use the Materials other than for the performance of the Services and expressly agrees not to analyze, attempt to identify, modify or otherwise reverse engineer the Materials to determine their composition.  Upon the completion of the Services, Consultant shall return all unused Materials to COLGATE, unless otherwise instructed by COLGATE in writing.  The Materials are Confidential Information of COLGATE.

Subcontractors.  Consultant may not subcontract or engage any Third Party to perform any of the Services.

Compliance with Policies While On-Site.  While at the offices or facilities of COLGATE and its Affiliates, Consultant and its Representatives shall comply with all applicable policies and procedures of COLGATE (including security policies and procedures) as provided to Consultant and its Representatives in writing or explained in a formal course on security.

Conflicts.  During the Term and for one (1) year thereafter, Consultant shall not undertake to perform any services or other work that may be adverse to or conflict with Services being provided to COLGATE, including similar work for any of COLGATE’s direct competitors in competing categories, without the prior written consent of COLGATE.

FEES

Fees.  In consideration of Consultant’s performance of the Services, COLGATE shall pay to Consultant the fees as set forth in the Service Exhibit (the “Fees”).  Consultant agrees to establish an account with COLGATE’s electronic invoicing provider for the submission and payment of all invoices.  After the Fees have become due, as set forth in the Service Exhibit, Consultant shall submit an invoice electronically.  All undisputed Fees shall be payable by COLGATE within ninety (90) days after receipt of an acceptable invoice for such Fees from Consultant; provided that Consultant may only issue such an invoice after such Fees have become due pursuant to the Service Exhibit.  All payments will be made by COLGATE to Consultant via a wire transfer.  Any sales, use, excise, value-added or other taxes or duties and penalties and interest relating thereto shall be the sole responsibility of Consultant.

No Other Costs.  Except as otherwise set forth in the Service Exhibit, all direct and indirect costs and expenses (including any travel costs, legal and other advisory fees and other Third-Party costs) in connection with this Agreement incurred by Consultant and its Representatives shall be borne solely by Consultant, and COLGATE shall have no obligation to reimburse Consultant for any such costs or expenses.  In case the Service Exhibit sets forth that specific expenses or costs are to be reimbursed by Colgate, such expenses or costs must be supported by detailed documentation including, for example, valid invoices or receipts.  

Audit.

Consultant shall maintain complete and accurate records of, and supporting documentation for, all Fees billable to and payments made by COLGATE hereunder [in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.]  Consultant shall provide COLGATE with reasonable documentation and other information for each invoice as may be reasonably requested by COLGATE.

COLGATE or its Representatives may audit the books and records of Consultant to verify Fees paid or payable in accordance with this Agreement.  COLGATE’s right to audit Consultant’s books and records for any calendar year shall expire twelve (12) months after the end of such calendar year.  [COLGATE shall pay the costs of the auditors conducting such audit, unless the results of an audit reveal an overpayment of Fees of five percent (5%) or more, in which case, Consultant shall pay the costs of the auditors conducting such audit and COLGATE’s out-of-pocket costs of conducting such audit.  If the audit concludes that an overpayment has occurred during the audited period, such payment shall be remitted by Consultant to COLGATE within thirty (30) days after the date such auditor’s written report identifying the overpayment is delivered to Consultant, together with interest of two percent (2%) per month from the date of overpayment (or the maximum amount of interest permitted by applicable Law if lower).]

INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

Ownership of Deliverables and Data.  All Deliverables (including data, information and work in progress resulting from the conduct of the Services) shall be the exclusive property of COLGATE, shall be considered Confidential Information of COLGATE and shall be subject to COLGATE’s exclusive use, commercial or otherwise.  Consultant hereby assigns, and shall cause its Affiliates and its and their Representatives and permitted subcontractors to assign,  to COLGATE the entire right, title and interest in and to all Deliverables.

Background IP.  All Background IP shall be and remain exclusively the property of the Party that made or acquired such Background IP.  Except as set forth in Article 5, neither Party has any right or license to any of the other Party’s Background IP.

Foreground IP.

Ownership.  COLGATE shall exclusively own all right, title and interest in and to all Foreground IP.  Consultant hereby assigns to COLGATE the entire right, title and interest in and to all Foreground IP.  If Consultant is not permitted by applicable Law to assign, and shall cause its Affiliates and its and their Representatives and subcontractors to assign, any Foreground IP to COLGATE, Consultant hereby grants COLGATE a perpetual, irrevocable, exclusive (even as to Consultant), world-wide, royalty-free, freely-assignable license in all fields to such Foreground IP (including the right to sell and grant sublicenses (through multiple tiers) to such Foreground IP) and agrees not to bring any action, claim or proceeding against COLGATE or any of its sublicensees or assignees for its use or exploitation of such Foreground IP.  COLGATE shall have the exclusive right to prepare and file applications for, prosecute, maintain, defend and assert, at its own costs, the Foreground IP.  Consultant shall reasonably assist and cooperate with COLGATE at COLGATE’s expense in perfecting, maintaining and defending the rights granted to COLGATE in this Section 4.3.1, including the provision of any requested documentation necessary for prosecution or maintenance of patents claiming such Foreground IP, and the execution of any required documents therefor.  Unless obligated by applicable Law, Consultant shall not file any patent applications claiming, or amend any patent applications to claim, any Foreground IP.  If despite the foregoing, Consultant files any patent applications claiming, or amends any patent applications to claim, any Foreground IP, Consultant agrees to assign such patent applications to COLGATE.

Disclosure.  Upon delivery of any Deliverable, Consultant shall provide to COLGATE a written report detailing any Foreground IP developed in connection with or embodied in the Deliverable. GLOBAL ANTI-BRIBERY POLICY





Our Anti-Bribery Commitment



ColgateColgate’s commitment to dealing legally and ethically applies worldwide.  We comply with all applicable anti-bribery laws, including but not limited to the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (“FCPA”), everywhere we do business, and we expect the same of the third parties with whom we  work.    While  the  FCPA  prohibits,  among  other  things,  bribery  of  foreign  government officials and entities, other anti-bribery laws, like the UK Bribery Act, prohibit commercial bribery between private individuals and entities.





Colgate people and any third parties acting on our behalf or in connection with our business are prohibited from giving or offering anything of value directly or indirectly to any government official or entity, or to any private individual or entity, in order to improperly obtain or retain any business advantage or to improperly affect any act or decision.





This prohibition includes any facilitating, expediting or “grease” payments made to government officials, either directly or indirectly, in order to expedite any official service or function (for example, small payments made to an official to move Colgate application to the front of the line or to shorten the time frame in which services or other actions are provided).  Any official fees supported by government-issued receipts do not qualify as improper payments.





Maintaining Accurate Books and Records



No payment by or on behalf of the Company shall be approved or made if any part of the payment is to be used for an unlawful or improper purpose, or for any purpose other than that described by valid documents supporting the payment.  No false or misleading entries should be made in any books or financial records of the Company for any reason.



Any expenses that an employee or third party incurs on Colgate behalf or in connection with our business shall not be reimbursable unless they are lawful and supported by detailed documentation including, for example, valid invoices or receipts.



Expenditures Related to Government Officials



No funds may be provided to or spent on behalf of a government official or entity, directly or indirectly, without advance written approval from Colgate Global Legal Organization.  This includes any payments, gifts, donations, entertainment, travel, meals, or other items of value. (For additional information, please review the Global Policy on Expenditures Related to Government Officials & Governments.)  Advance approval is not required for official fees supported by government-issued receipts (e.g., permit or license fees).

Please note that the term “government official” is widely defined and may include individuals who are employed by any public or state-affiliated institution or organization or who act in an official capacity in any way, whether full-time, part-time or unpaid.  Government officials can be found in every branch and level of government and public life and may include anyone from low-level customs employees, to employees of state-owned media outlets, to high-ranking lawmakers, as well as researchers, professors, teachers, dentists, veterinarians, or other professionals and Key Thought Leaders.  If you are in doubt as to whether an individual could be considered a government official, you should contact the Global Legal Organization.



Commercial Bribery



In addition to prohibiting bribery of government officials, Colgate also prohibits its employees and third parties from engaging in bribery of private parties.  You should not seek to improperly influence the judgment or conduct of any party with whom you might be conducting Company business by offering or providing any payments, gifts or other benefits, or by any other unlawful inducement.



Our Expectations



Colgate reputation depends on the conduct of our employees as well as the conduct of those with whom we do business.  It is our goal to ensure that Colgate People and the third parties with whom we work reflect the same high ethical standards and demonstrate a commitment to compliance with all applicable laws.  We further expect our third parties to ensure that their employees and subcontractors understand and comply with this Anti-Bribery Policy.

Failure to comply with this Anti-Bribery Policy or any applicable anti-bribery laws, including but not limited to the FCPA, may result in civil or criminal penalties, as well as termination of the employment or business relationship.
