RESEARCH AGREEMENT

This RESEARCH AGREEMENT is entered into as of the date of the last signature below (the “Effective Date”) by and between Colgate-Palmolive Company, a Delaware corporation, having its principal offices at 300 Park Avenue, New York, New York  10022 (“Colgate”), and [●], a [●] organized under the laws of [●], having its principal offices at [●] (“Researcher”).  Colgate and Researcher are sometimes hereinafter referred to collectively as the “Parties” and individually as a “Party.”

RECITALS

WHEREAS, Colgate desires to have Researcher carry out a research project for Colgate or its Affiliates, as more specifically set forth in Exhibit A to this Agreement; and

WHEREAS, Colgate and Researcher desire to enter into this Agreement to govern such research project.

AGREEMENT

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the premises and the undertakings of the Parties hereinafter set forth, the Parties agree as follows:

DEFINITIONS

“Affiliate” means, with respect to a Person, an individual, trust, business trust, joint venture, partnership, corporation, association or any other entity which (directly or indirectly) is controlled by, controls, or is under common control with a Person.  For purposes of this definition, the term “control” (including, with correlative meanings, the term “controlled by” and “under common control with”) as used with respect to any Person, shall mean the possession (directly or indirectly) of power to direct or cause the direction of the management or policies of such Person.

“Agreement” means this Research Agreement and all Exhibits hereto, as the same may be amended or modified from time to time in accordance with the terms hereof.

“Background IP” means Intellectual Property under the control of a Party that was developed or acquired by the Party prior to the Effective Date or independently and outside the activities contemplated by this Agreement without reference to or use of the other Party’s Confidential Information or Background IP. For purposes of this definition, a Party “controls” Intellectual Property if it owns or otherwise has the right to license or sublicense such Intellectual Property.

“Breaching Party” is defined in Section 11.2.1.

“Claims” is defined in Section 9.1.

“Colgate” is defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Colgate Confidential Information” means (a) any information or data, whether technical or nontechnical, whether written (including graphic or electronic) and marked confidential or oral, disclosed by Colgate or its Affiliates or on Colgate’s behalf to Provider, disclosed by Colgate or its Affiliates or on Colgate’s behalf to Researcher, either directly or indirectly, on or after the Effective Date [or previously under a Prior Non-Disclosure Agreement], and (b) the existence and terms of this Agreement.  If Colgate Confidential Information is disclosed orally, Colgate shall provide a summary and confirm the confidential nature of such information in writing within fifteen (15) days after such oral disclosure.  For the avoidance of doubt, Colgate Confidential Information shall include Research Project IP, Materials, Deliverables and [●].

“Confidential Information” means Colgate Confidential Information or Researcher Confidential Information, as the context requires.

“Deliverables” is defined in Section 2.1.

“Disclosing Party” means the Party disclosing Confidential Information.

“Effective Date” is defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Fees” is defined in Section 4.1.

“Force Majeure” is defined in Section 12.1.

“Governmental Authority” means any legislative, executive or judicial unit of any governmental or quasi-governmental authority or instrumentality (multi-national, national, federal, state, provincial, local or foreign, international or domestic), or any department, agency, board, bureau, commission, official or other regulatory, administrative or judicial authority thereof, including any administrative or regulatory agency or commission, and any court or arbitration tribunal, in each instance having jurisdiction over the subject matter before it.

“Indemnity Claim” is defined in Section 9.2.

“Intellectual Property” means all discoveries, inventions, improvements, developments, procedures, processes, formulations, know-how, trade secrets, formulae, trademarks, service marks, trade dress, designs, logos, packaging, proprietary information, technical information, techniques, works of authorship, drawings, models, manuals and systems, whether or not patentable or copyrightable or otherwise registerable, and all rights and applications or registrations derived or derivable therefrom.

“Law” means all supranational, international, national, state and local laws, statutes, regulations, rules, codes or ordinances enacted, adopted, issued or promulgated by any Governmental Authority or common law.

“Materials” is defined in Section 2.4. 

“Nonbreaching Party” is defined in Section 11.2.1.

“Notice” is defined in Section 12.2. 

“Party” and “Parties” are defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Person” means any natural person, corporation, limited liability company, trust, joint venture, association, company, partnership or other entity.

“Prior Non-Disclosure Agreements” mean [●].

“Project Description” is defined in Section 2.1.

“Publications” is defined in Section 6.1.

“Receiving Party” means the Party receiving Confidential Information.

“Representatives” means, for a Party, its directors, officers, employees. advisors or agents and the directors, officers, employees, advisors or agents of its Affiliates.

“Research Project” is defined in Section 2.1.

“Research Project IP” mean Intellectual Property that is created by the Representatives of either or both Parties while performing the Research Project under this Agreement.

“Research Project Manager” is defined in Section 3.1.

“Research Steps” is defined in Section 2.1.

“Researcher” is defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Researcher Confidential Information” means (a) any information or data, whether technical or nontechnical, whether written (including graphic or electronic) and marked confidential or oral, disclosed by Colgate or its Affiliates or on Colgate’s behalf to Provider, disclosed by Researcher or its Affiliates or on Researcher’s behalf to Colgate, either directly or indirectly, on or after the Effective Date[ or previously under a Prior Non-Disclosure Agreement], excluding all Colgate Confidential Information, and (b) the existence and terms of this Agreement; provided that Researcher Confidential Information shall not include any Research Project IP.  If Researcher Confidential Information is disclosed orally, Researcher shall provide a summary and confirm the confidential nature of such information in writing within fifteen (15) days after such oral disclosure.

“Term” is defined in Section 11.1.

“Third Party” means any entity other than Researcher or Colgate or an Affiliate of either Party.

GENERAL OBLIGATIONS

Research Project.  Exhibit A hereto (the “Project Description”) sets forth the research and other activities to be conducted by Researcher (the “Research Project”).  The Project Description identifies: (a) the general description of the Research Project; (b) the scope of work to be undertaken by Researcher; (c) the schedule under which such scope of work is to be completed; (d) the principal steps for carrying out the Research Project (the “Research Steps”); (e) the deliverables to be provided by Researcher to Colgate (the “Deliverables”); (f) milestones; (g) the Fees (as defined below); and (h) the approved expenses.

Performance of Obligations.  Researcher shall, and shall cause its Representatives and permitted subcontractors to, perform all of the tasks and obligations set forth in the Project Description (including the performance of the Research Steps and delivery of the Deliverables), together with any tasks and obligations not specifically described in the Project Description but which are inherent in or a necessary part of the tasks and obligations described in the Project Description, or are reasonably required for proper performance of such tasks and obligations.  Researcher shall be responsible for acquiring all necessary equipment, materials and tools necessary to conduct the Research Project other than the Materials, if any.  Researcher shall complete each milestone set forth in the Project Description within the period specified in the Project Description for such milestone.  [All Deliverables delivered by Researcher are subject to Colgate’s acceptance, and Researcher shall re-perform and re-deliver any Deliverable that is not accepted by Colgate.  No payment under this Agreement by Colgate shall be evidence of the performance of Researcher or the acceptance of any Deliverable. 

Removal of Personnel.  Researcher shall maintain staffing levels and continuity of personnel consistent with its obligation to perform the Research Project.  Researcher shall not remove or redeploy personnel performing the Research Project without the prior written permission of Colgate.  If any Representatives performing the Research Project are unacceptable to Colgate for any reason, Colgate reserves the right to notify Researcher in which case Researcher shall immediately remove such Representatives from performing the Research Project hereunder and, if requested by Colgate, provide a qualified replacement.  If Researcher provides replacement Representatives for any reason, Researcher shall not charge Colgate for the number of hours required to train the replacement until such Representatives are familiar with the particular Research Project, so that such replacement Representatives are capable of performing the Research Project in accordance with this Agreement.

Materials.  Colgate will provide the materials identified in the Project Description, if any (the “Materials”), to Researcher for the performance of the Research Project.  Researcher shall not use the Materials other than for the performance of the Research Project and expressly agrees not to analyze, attempt to identify, modify or otherwise reverse engineer the Materials to determine their composition.  Upon the completion of the Research Project, Researcher shall return all unused Materials to Colgate, unless otherwise instructed by Colgate in writing.  The Materials are Confidential Information of Colgate.

Subcontractors.  Researcher may not subcontract or engage any Third Party to perform any of its tasks or obligations hereunder, or consult with any Third Party regarding such tasks and obligations, unless: (a) Colgate provides written approval in advance; and (b) such Third Party enters into an agreement having commercial, Intellectual Property and confidentiality terms that are approved in writing by Colgate.  No such subcontracting shall relieve Researcher of its obligations under this Agreement and Researcher shall be responsible for the actions and inactions of all of its permitted subcontractors as if such actions and inactions were committed by Researcher. 

Exclusivity.  During the Term and for [●] year(s) thereafter, Researcher shall not (and shall cause its Affiliates not to), itself or in collaboration with or pursuant to a contract or agreement with or for the benefit of any Third Party, engage in, undertake or otherwise pursue, a research, development or commercialization project which may be adverse to or conflict with the Research Project or is identical or similar to the Research Project, including similar work for any of Colgate’s direct competitors in competing categories, without the prior written consent of Colgate.

MANAGEMENT OF THE RESEARCH PROJECT

Research Project Managers.  Each Party hereby appoints the Research Project manager for such Party set forth in Exhibit B (each, a “Research Project Manager”) to act as the primary contact for such Party in connection with matters related to the Research Project.  Either Party may replace its Research Project Manager at any time by providing written notice to the other Party.  Researcher’s Research Project Manager shall keep Colgate’s Research Project Manager apprised of the status of the Research Project and of the various Research Steps at all times.  The Research Project Managers will meet at least [●], or more frequently as agreed by the Research Project Managers, and such meetings may be held by videoconference or telephone conference.

Compliance with Policies While On-Site.  While at the offices or facilities of Colgate and its Affiliates, Researcher and its Representatives shall comply with all applicable policies and procedures of Colgate (including security policies and procedures) as provided to Researcher and its Representatives in writing or explained in a formal course on security.

FEES

Fees.  In consideration of Researcher’s performance of the Research Project, Colgate shall pay to Researcher the fees as set forth in the Project Description (the “Fees”).  Researcher agrees to establish an account with Colgate’s electronic invoicing provider for the submission and payment of all invoices.  After the Fees have become due, as set forth in the Project Description, Researcher shall submit an invoice electronically.  All undisputed Fees shall be payable by Colgate within ninety (90) days after Colgate’s receipt of an acceptable invoice for such Fees from Researcher; provided that Researcher may only issue such an invoice after such Fees have become due pursuant to the Project Description.  All payments will be made by Colgate to Researcher via a wire transfer.  Any sales, use, excise, value-added or other taxes or duties and penalties and interest relating thereto shall be the sole responsibility of Researcher. 

No Other Costs.  Except as otherwise set forth in the Project Description, all direct and indirect costs and expenses (including any travel costs, legal and other advisory fees and other Third-Party costs) in connection with this Agreement incurred by Researcher or its Representatives shall be borne solely by Researcher, and Colgate shall have no obligation to reimburse Researcher for any such costs or expenses. 

Audit. 

Researcher shall maintain complete and accurate records of, and supporting documentation for, all Fees billable to and payments made by Colgate hereunder in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.  Researcher shall provide Colgate with reasonable documentation and other information for each invoice as may be reasonably requested by Colgate.  

Colgate or its Representatives may audit the books and records of Researcher to verify Fees paid or payable in accordance with this Agreement.  Colgate’s right to audit Researcher’s books and records for any calendar year shall expire twelve (12) months after the end of such calendar year.  [Colgate shall pay the costs of the auditors conducting such audit, unless the results of an audit reveal an overpayment of Fees of five percent (5%) or more, in which case, Researcher shall pay the costs of the auditors conducting such audit and Colgate’s out-of-pocket costs of conducting such audit.  If the audit concludes that an overpayment has occurred during the audited period, such payment shall be remitted by Researcher to Colgate within thirty (30) days after the date such auditor’s written report identifying the overpayment is delivered to Researcher, together with interest of two percent (2%) per month from the date of overpayment (or the maximum amount of interest permitted by applicable law if lower).

INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

Ownership of Deliverables and Data.  All Deliverables (including data, information and work in progress resulting from the conduct of the Research Project) shall be the exclusive property of Colgate, shall be considered Colgate Confidential Information and shall be subject to Colgate’s exclusive use, commercial or otherwise.  Researcher hereby assigns, and shall cause its Affiliates and its and their Representatives and subcontractors to assign, to Colgate the entire right, title and interest in and to all Deliverables.

Background IP.  All Background IP shall be and remain exclusively the property of the Party that made or acquired such Background IP.  Except as set forth in Article 7, neither Party has any right or license to any of the other Party’s Background IP.

Research Project IP.

Ownership.  Colgate shall exclusively own all right, title and interest in and to all Research Project IP.  Researcher hereby assigns, and shall cause its Affiliates and its and their Representatives and subcontractors to assign, to Colgate the entire right, title and interest in and to all Research Project IP.  If Researcher is not permitted by applicable Law to assign any Research Project IP to Colgate, Researcher hereby grants Colgate a perpetual, irrevocable, exclusive (even as to Researcher), world-wide, royalty-free, freely-assignable license in all fields to such Research Project IP (including the right to sell and grant sublicenses (through multiple tiers) to such Research Project IP) and agrees not to bring any action, claim or proceeding against Colgate or any of its sublicensees or assignees for its use or exploitation of such Research Project IP.  Colgate shall have the exclusive right to prepare and file applications for, prosecute, maintain, defend and assert, at its own costs, the Research Project IP.  Researcher shall reasonably assist and cooperate with Colgate at Colgate’s expense in perfecting, maintaining and defending the rights granted to Colgate in this Section 5.3.1, including the provision of any requested documentation necessary for prosecution or maintenance of patents claiming such Research Project IP, and the execution of any required documents therefor.  Unless obligated by applicable Law, Researcher shall not file any patent applications claiming, or amend any patent applications to claim, any Research Project IP. If despite the foregoing, Researcher files any patent applications claiming, or amends any patent applications to claim, any Research Project IP, Researcher agrees to assign such patent applications to Colgate.

Disclosure.  Upon delivery of any Deliverable, Researcher shall provide to Colgate a written report detailing any Research Project IP developed in connection with or embodied in the Deliverable.  Researcher shall include in its written report a reasonable level of detail regarding the applicable Research Project IP and shall provide such additional information on the Research Project IP as is reasonably requested by Colgate.

Enforcement.  Colgate shall have the exclusive right to bring and control any claim, action or proceeding related to the infringement, misappropriation or other violation of any Research Project IP, and shall retain all damages, recoveries and other amounts awarded in connection therewith.  Researcher shall reasonably assist and cooperate with Colgate in bringing a claim, action or proceeding pursuant to this Section 5.3.3, at Colgate’s expense, including the provision or execution of any requested documentation.  Researcher acknowledges that it may be a necessary party to any claim, action or proceeding brought by Colgate arising from enforcement of any Research Project IP and, if necessary, Researcher shall participate in such claim, action or proceeding, at Colgate’s request.

Use of Names and Trademarks.  Neither Party nor its Affiliates shall make any oral or written statement or perform any act indicating that the other Party or its Affiliates endorses or approves, or has endorsed or approved, such Party or its products or services.  Nothing contained in this Agreement will be construed as conferring any right to use in advertising, publicity or other promotional activities any name, trade name, trademark, service mark or other designation of a Party (including any contraction, abbreviation or simulation of any of the foregoing) without the prior written approval of such Party.

PUBLICATIONS

Publications.  Any proposed electronic, oral, or written disclosure, including, but not limited to, abstracts, manuscripts, presentations and publications, by Researcher referring to the Research Project (“Publications”) shall be submitted by Researcher to Colgate for review and approval ninety (90) days prior to submission for publication.  No Publication shall be undertaken without such approval.  Colgate may withhold approval at Colgate’s sole discretion.  It is understood and agreed that all Publications which Researcher publishes with Colgate’s permission based on information obtained from the Research Project may, at Colgate’s sole discretion, carry a statement that the Research Project was supported by Colgate-Palmolive Company.

LICENSES

License to Researcher Background IP and Confidential Information.  Researcher, on behalf of itself and its Affiliates, grants to Colgate and Colgate’s Affiliates a non-exclusive, royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide license to practice and otherwise fully exploit all Researcher Background IP and Researcher Confidential Information, including to manufacture, have manufactured, use, import, sell or offer for sale any product or service or practice any method, in any and all fields to the extent incorporated into, or otherwise necessary or useful to exploit, any Research Project IP or Deliverable.  For the avoidance of doubt, expiration or termination of this Agreement shall not terminate or limit Colgate’s rights under this Section 7.1.

No Other Licenses or Rights.  Except as expressly set forth herein, nothing in this Agreement grants, by implication, estoppel or otherwise, a Party any license or right to any of the other Party’s Intellectual Property or Confidential Information.

GENERAL REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES; LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

General Warranties.  Each Party represents and warrants to the other Party that:

[the execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement by such Party have been duly authorized by all necessary action on the part of such Party;]

this Agreement, when executed and delivered by such Party in accordance with the provisions hereof, will be a legal, valid and binding obligation of such Party, enforceable against such Party in accordance with its terms, except as such enforceability may be limited by applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, moratorium, reorganization or similar Laws affecting the enforcement of creditors’ rights generally and by general principles of equity; and

such Party’s execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement shall not constitute a violation, breach or default under any contract, instrument, obligation or agreement to which it is a Party or by which it is bound, and will not conflict with or violate any applicable Law of any Governmental Authority having jurisdiction over it or its assets or property.

Compliance With Law.  Researcher represents, warrants and covenants that it shall comply with all applicable Laws in connection with its performance of its tasks and obligations under this Agreement.

Performance.  Researcher represents, warrants and covenants that:

it shall devoteall necessary time, attention, effort and resources to the performance of the Research Project and the delivery of the Deliverables so as to meet its obligations set forth in this Agreement;

it shall perform the Research Project, deliver the Deliverables and otherwise perform its obligations set forth in this Agreement in a diligent, careful, thorough, workmanlike and professional manner; and

[it and its personnel have] and shall have the skills, knowledge, qualifications and experience necessary to perform and manage the performance of the Research Project, deliver the Deliverables and otherwise perform its obligations set forth in this Agreement.

Compliance with Policies.  In connection with the performance of Researcher’s tasks and obligations pursuant to this Agreement, Researcher shall comply with the generally applicable policies of Colgate provided to Researcher in writing from time to time.  Without limiting the foregoing:

Supplier Code of Conduct.  Researcher represents and warrants that it is in compliance with Colgate’s Supplier Code of Conduct as of the Effective Date and shall remain in compliance throughout the term of this Agreement with Colgate’s Supplier Code of Conduct and any subsequent amendments thereto in the form (a) provided by Colgate to Researcher throughout the term of this Agreement or (b) updated throughout the term of this Agreement at https://www.colgatepalmolive.com/en/us/corp/about/governance/third-party-code-of-conduct, including the requirement of strict compliance with the letter and spirit of applicable environmental laws and regulations and the public policies they represent.

Global Anti-Bribery Policy. Attached to this Agreement as Exhibit C is a copy of Colgate’s Global Anti-Bribery Policy.  Researcher represents and warrants that it has reviewed the contents of Colgate’s Global Anti-Bribery Policy and agrees that it shall abide by the terms of such policy and any subsequent amendments thereto in the form provided by Colgate to Researcher throughout the Term.

Researcher’s Maintenance of Insurance.  Researcher shall maintain at all times during the Term, and at its sole expense, such policy or policies of insurance, including a general liability, worker’s compensation and employers liability, as are necessary to cover all loss, destruction or damage for which Researcher has assumed responsibility under the terms of this Agreement, and shall name Colgate as an additional insured with respect to such insurance.  Researcher shall cause its insurance policies to provide a waiver of subrogation in favor of Colgate.  The policies shall be with at least a Standard & Poor’s A+ rated company providing limits of no less than $5,000,000.00 per occurrence.  Such limits can be satisfied with a primary policy or a combination of a primary and excess / umbrella policies.  Researcher shall promptly furnish upon request certificates of insurance to Colgate evidencing that the insurance required by this paragraph is in full force and effect. [The certificates of insurance required hereunder shall contain a clause which provides that there shall be no reduction, cancellation or expiration of, or other material change to the policy without at least thirty (30) days’ prior written notice to Colgate.] 

Disclaimer of Warranties.  OTHER THAN AS SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 8, ALL WARRANTIES, BOTH EXPRESS AND IMPLIED, ARE EXPRESSLY DISCLAIMED BY BOTH PARTIES, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. WITHOUT LIMITING THE FOREGOING, NEITHER PARTY REPRESENTS, WARRANTS OR GUARANTEES THAT ANY PARTICULAR OUTCOME OR RESULT, INCLUDING DEVELOPMENT OF A PRODUCT FOR COMMERCIALIZATION, WILL ARISE FROM THE RESEARCH ACTIVITIES CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THIS AGREEMENT.

Limitations of Liability.  TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW, IN NO EVENT SHALL COLGATE HAVE ANY DAMAGES OR LIABILITY TO RESEARCHER, ANY OF RESEARCHER’S AFFILIATES OR ANY THIRD PARTY ARISING OUT OF, RELATED TO OR IN CONNECTION WITH THIS AGREEMENT, REGARDLESS OF THE FORM OF THE ACTION, WHETHER IN CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY, PRODUCT LIABILITY OR OTHERWISE:

FOR INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, INDIRECT, SPECIAL, PUNITIVE OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES OR LIABILITIES OF ANY KIND OR FOR LOSS OF REVENUE OR PROFITS OR LOSS OF BUSINESS; OR

IN AN AGGREGATE AMOUNT IN EXCESS OF THE GREATER OF $[●] OR [TWO TIMES] THE TOTAL AMOUNTS PAID BY COLGATE TO RESEARCHER PURSUANT TO THIS AGREEMENT.

INDEMNIFICATION

Indemnification by Researcher.  Researcher agrees to defend, indemnify and hold harmless Colgate, Colgate’s Affiliates and their Representatives, from and against any and all losses, liabilities, damages, actions, suits, demands or claims brought by any Third Party (including amounts paid in settlement, reasonable costs of investigation and reasonable attorneys’ fees and disbursements) (collectively, “Claims”), arising out of or resulting from [(a) the negligence, gross negligence, bad faith or intentional or willful misconduct of Researcher or its Affiliates, Representatives or permitted subcontractors], (b) breach of any of Researcher's representations, warranties, covenants or agreements contained herein, (c) violation of Law by Researcher or its Affiliates, Representatives or permitted subcontractors in connection with Researcher’s performance under this Agreement, and (d) the actual or alleged infringement, misappropriation or violation of a Third Party’s Intellectual Property by (1) Colgate’s use, practice or other exploitation of (i) Researcher’s Background IP in accordance with the terms hereof or (ii) any of the Deliverables or (2) Researcher’s and its Affiliates’, Representatives’ and permitted subcontractors’ performance under this Agreement.

Indemnification Claims.  Colgate agrees to give Researcher prompt written notice of any matter upon which any indemnified Person intends to base a claim for indemnification (an “Indemnity Claim”) under this Article 9, provided, however, that any delay in providing or failure to provide such notice shall not relieve Researcher of any of its obligations hereunder except to the extent that Researcher is materially prejudiced by such failure.  Researcher shall have the right to participate jointly with the indemnified Person in the indemnified Person’s defense, settlement or other disposition of any Indemnity Claim.  With respect to any Indemnity Claim relating solely to the payment of money damages which could not result in the indemnified Person becoming subject to injunctive or other equitable relief or otherwise adversely affect the business of the indemnified Person in any manner, and as to which Researcher shall have acknowledged in writing the obligation to indemnify the indemnified Person hereunder, Researcher shall have the sole right to defend, settle or otherwise dispose of such Indemnity Claim, on such terms as Researcher, in its sole discretion, shall deem appropriate; provided that Researcher shall provide reasonable evidence of its ability to pay any damages claimed and with respect to any such settlement shall have obtained the written release of the indemnified Person from the Indemnity Claim.  Researcher shall obtain the written consent of the indemnified Person, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, prior to ceasing to defend, settling or otherwise disposing of any Indemnity Claim if as a result thereof the indemnified Person would become subject to injunctive or other equitable relief or the business of the indemnified Person would be adversely affected in any manner.

CONFIDENTIALITY AND NON-USE

Obligations of Confidentiality.  The Receiving Party shall (a) maintain any Confidential Information in confidence; (b) take all necessary and reasonable precautions to prevent Confidential Information from being disclosed to any unauthorized third party, which shall include open artificial intelligence platforms (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini), and (c) use Confidential Information exclusively for performing any task or obligations described in the Project Description or otherwise in accordance with any licenses granted hereunder, as applicable.  The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to its Representatives and permitted subcontractors, each with a need to know such Confidential Information in order to perform any task or obligations described in the Project Description or otherwise in accordance with any licenses granted hereunder; provided that (i) the Receiving Party advises its Representatives and permitted subcontractors of the confidential nature thereof and (ii) such Representatives and permitted subcontractors are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as stringent as those set forth herein  (for subcontractors, the confidentiality terms must be approved in writing by Colgate, as set forth in Section 2.4).  The Receiving Party shall be liable to the Disclosing Party for any failure by any of its Representatives or permitted subcontractors to comply with this Article 10 with respect to the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information in the same manner as the Receiving Party is obligated to treat such Confidential Information under the terms of this Agreement.

Exclusions.  Confidential Information shall not include information that the Receiving Party demonstrates:

is in the public domain as of the Effective Date, or subsequently enters the public domain through no fault or act of the Receiving Party;

is known to the Receiving Party prior to disclosure from the Disclosing Party[; provided that such information was not acquired from the Disclosing Party under one of the Prior Non-Disclosure Agreements if such information is still to be treated as confidential under such Prior Non-Disclosure Agreement;]

that the Receiving Party received from any third party not under any obligation to the Disclosing Party to keep such information confidential; and

was independently developed by the Receiving Party without reliance upon or use of the Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party.

Compelled and Mandatory Disclosures.

In the event that the Receiving Party receives a subpoena or other government process that purports to require the production of any Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party for use in an action or proceeding or for any purpose other than for performing any task or obligations described in the Project Description or in connection with any licenses granted hereunder, the Receiving Party shall (a) promptly inform the party or entity issuing such subpoena or other government process of the existence of this Agreement, (b) promptly inform the Disclosing Party of the receipt of such subpoena or other government process and (c) not oppose any effort by the Disclosing Party to quash any such subpoena or other government process.  In the event that (x) the Disclosing Party fails to intervene to quash such subpoena or other government process after being given notice and a reasonable opportunity to do so or (y) such intervention fails or is denied by a court of competent jurisdiction, such Confidential Information may be produced but limited to what is strictly necessary, notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary.

In the event that the Receiving Party believes it is required by applicable Law or stock exchange rules to disclose any part of the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information, the Receiving Party shall: (a) promptly advise the Disclosing Party of each such requirement in writing and identify the documents so required thereby, so that the Disclosing Party may seek an appropriate protective order or other remedy or waive compliance by the Receiving Party with the provisions of this Agreement; and (b) consult with the Disclosing Party on the advisability of taking legally available steps to resist or narrow the scope of such requirement.  If, in the absence of such a protective order or such a waiver by the Disclosing Party of the provisions of this Agreement, the Receiving Party is nonetheless required by mandatory applicable Law to disclose any part of the Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information, the Receiving Party may disclose such Confidential Information without liability under this Agreement, except that the Receiving Party shall furnish only that portion of the Confidential Information which is legally required.

In the event that any Confidential Information is produced or disclosed pursuant to this Section 10.3.3, such Confidential Information shall not lose its confidential status through such use, and the Receiving Party shall take all reasonable and necessary steps to protect the confidentiality of such Confidential Information during such use.

Terms of Agreement.  Subject to Section 10.2 and Section 10.3, neither Party shall, without the prior written consent of the other Party, disclose in any manner to any Third Party the existence and the terms and conditions of this Agreement.

Trade Secrets.  No Disclosing Party shall disclose any “trade secrets” to the Receiving Party pursuant to this Agreement, unless: (a) such Confidential Information is clearly marked as a “trade secret” of the Disclosing Party and (b) the Receiving Party has separately agreed in writing to the receipt of such “trade secret.”  In connection with the disclosure of any “trade secret,” the Disclosing Party may also condition such disclosure on additional confidentiality obligations and disclosure limitations that must be agreed upon in writing by the Parties, such as limitation of disclosure to a defined group of individual Representatives of the Receiving Party.

Survival.  The mutual obligations of confidentiality and non-use under this Article 10 shall survive the expiration and earlier termination of this Agreement for a period of [two (2) years] after its expiration or earlier termination.

TERM AND TERMINATION OF AGREEMENT.

Term.  This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and, unless terminated earlier pursuant to this Article, shall continue in force and effect until the [earlier/later] of [●]or completion by both Parties of all tasks and obligations set forth the Project Description (the “Term”).

Termination.  This Agreement may be terminated as follows: 

Material Breach.  This Agreement (in its entirety) may be terminated by either Party (the “Nonbreaching Party”) upon written notice thereof to the other Party (the “Breaching Party”) in the event of a material breach of this Agreement by the Breaching Party which is not cured within sixty (60) days after the receipt by the Breaching Party of written notice from the Nonbreaching Party, specifying in reasonable detail the nature of such breach.  If such breach is not cured within such cure period, this Agreement shall terminate as set forth in the Nonbreaching Party’s notice of breach and in accordance with the terms of this Article; provided, however, that this Agreement shall not be terminated prior to the end of such cure period.  

Insolvency.  This Agreement may be terminated by either Party upon sixty (60) days’ prior written notice to the other Party at any time during this Agreement if the other Party: (a) files in any court pursuant to any statute a petition in bankruptcy or insolvency or for reorganization or for an arrangement or for the appointment of a receiver or trustee of the other Party, or of its assets; (b) proposes a written agreement of composition for extension of its debts; (c) is served with an involuntary petition against it, filed in any insolvency proceeding, and such petition shall not be dismissed within sixty (60) days after filing thereof; or (d) makes an assignment for the benefit of its creditors.  The Party affected shall immediately notify the other Party in writing of the occurrence of any of the foregoing events.

For Convenience.  This Agreement may be terminated by Colgate for any or no reason by providing Researcher with written notice at least thirty (30) days prior to the desired effective date of termination.  If Colgate elects to terminate this Agreement pursuant to this Section 11.2.3, Researcher shall be entitled to receive Fees for the Research Steps performed until the termination date of this Agreement but Colgate shall have no other liability to Researcher as a result of such termination of this Agreement.

Cumulative Remedies.  Except as expressly stated otherwise herein, remedies under this Agreement are cumulative, and nothing in this Agreement shall prevent any Party, in the case of a material breach (after expiration of applicable cure period and notice periods), from terminating this Agreement and seeking to enforce its rights under this Agreement.

Consequences of Termination.  Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement:

each Party shall either (at the sole discretion of such Party) deliver to the other Party or destroy all Confidential Information and original technical data and technology supplied by the other Party pursuant to this Agreement to such Party; provided, however, that each Party may retain an archival copy or other appropriate record (including electronic backup copies created in the ordinary course) of any such Confidential Information.  Such copies and records may be used exclusively for internal recordkeeping and administrative purposes, to assure compliance with any applicable Governmental Authority requirements and for dispute resolution purposes;

Researcher shall, in accordance with such Colgate’s instructions, deliver to Colgate: (i) all materials, products or equipment of Colgate previously provided to Researcher in connection with the Research Project, including the Materials pursuant to this Agreement; and (ii) all Deliverables (including Deliverables in progress) developed under this Agreement; and

If either Party terminates prior to the expiration of the Term (other than by Colgate for Researcher’s breach), Colgate shall, within sixty (60) days after the effective date of termination, pay Researcher the Fees associated with Research Steps completed by Researcher under this Agreement prior to either Party providing the other with notice of termination.  All Fees advanced by Colgate to Researcher and not earned by Researcher under this Agreement shall be reimbursed by Researcher to Colgate within sixty (60) days after the effective date of termination.

Survival.  All provisions under this Agreement which by their terms survive, or by their nature should survive, expiration or any earlier termination of this Agreement shall survive any such expiration or termination, including Article 1, Section 4.3, Article 5, Article 6, Section 7.1, Section 8.7, Article 9, Article 10, Section 11.4, this Section 11.5 and Article 12.

MISCELLANEOUS

Force Majeure.  No liability shall result to Colgate or Researcher from any delay in performance or from non-performance caused by acts of God, fire, flood, explosion, war, action or request of governmental authority, or any other unforeseeable circumstances of a similar nature beyond the reasonable control of the Party affected; provided that the delayed or nonperforming Party (i) promptly notifies the other Party of the existence of such cause and its probable duration and (ii) makes all reasonable efforts to prevent, limit and remove the effects of such cause (“Force Majeure”).  [In the event of a Force Majeure that continues for thirty (30) days or more, Colgate may terminate this Agreement immediately upon notice as per Section 12.2 to Researcher.] 

Notices.  The Parties shall deliver all notices, claims, demands, consents, approvals and other communications under this Agreement (each, a “Notice”) in writing and in English, referring to this Agreement and addressed to the other Party at its address below or to the last address the receiving Party provided to the other Party in compliance with this section.  The Parties shall deliver any Notice by personal delivery, reputable overnight courier (all fees prepaid), certified or registered mail (postage prepaid, return receipt requested) or by email.  A Notice shall be deemed received (i) on the date of personal or courier delivery, (ii) if mailed, on the date of receipt or refusal indicated on the return receipt or (iii) if emailed, upon receipt by the sending Party of an email acknowledgment of receipt by the receiving Party; provided that a “read receipt” or other automatic email response shall not qualify for this purpose.

This Agreement and its attachments contain the entire understanding among the Parties and supersede any and all prior agreements, understandings and arrangements whether written or oral among the Parties with respect to the matters contained in this Agreement.  No amendments, changes, modifications or alterations of the terms and conditions of this Agreement shall be binding upon any Party, unless in writing and signed by an authorized Representative of each Party.

Governing Law.  This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of State of New York, without giving effect to any choice of law or conflicts of law rules or provisions.

Dispute Resolution.  Subject to Section 12.5.4 below, any dispute between the Parties arising out of, related to or in connection with this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively by invoking the following dispute resolution procedures:

  The Parties agree to make a diligent, good faith effort to resolve all disputes amicably if at all possible. To this end, authorized representatives of each Party shall meet within fifteen (15) days after receipt of written notice by either Party at a mutually agreeable time and place to discuss possible resolution of the dispute.

  In the event that the Parties are unable to resolve the dispute within fifteen (15) days after their meeting, then either Party may invoke non-binding mediation under the International Institute for Conflict Prevention & Resolution (“CPR”) Mediation Procedure then in effect . Unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties, the Parties will select a single mediator from the CPR Panels of Distinguished Neutrals. The mediation proceeding shall be conducted in New York, New York, or such other location as may be agreed in writing by the Parties. The Parties shall (a) share equally the fees and expenses of the mediator; and (b) bear their own attorneys’ fees and associated costs and expenses. At the request of either Party, the mediator shall enter an appropriate protective order to maintain the confidentiality of information produced or exchanged in the course of the mediation proceedings. The Parties shall use their best efforts to complete the mediation procedure provided for in this Section 12.5 within no more than sixty (60) days.

  After (i) completion of the process described in Section 12.5.1 and Section 12.5.2 above or (ii) the non-cooperation of either Party in the completion of the stated procedure, then either Party (in the case of clause (i)) or the cooperating Party (in the case of clause (ii)) may initiate an action in court against the other, but such action may only be brought in a court having jurisdiction pursuant to Section 12.6 of this Agreement. All applicable statutes of limitation and defenses based upon the passage of time shall be tolled while the process described in Section 12.5.1 and Section 12.5.2 above is pending. The Parties shall take such action, if any, required to effectuate such tolling.

  Nothing in this Section 12.5 shall be construed to prevent either Party from seeking injunctive relief against the other Party from any judicial or administrative authority of competent jurisdiction to enjoin such other Party from breaching any provision of this Agreement pending the resolution of a dispute as hereinbefore provided.

Venue.  All disputes arising out of this Agreement (and all amendments and attachments hereto) shall be exclusively resolved in a court of competent jurisdiction in the State of New York. Each Party expressly consents to the jurisdiction of the state or federal courts in the State of New York and waives any objections or right as to forum non conveniens, lack of personal jurisdiction or similar grounds. Each Party hereby irrevocably and unconditionally waives all right to trial by jury in any action (whether based on contract, tort or otherwise) arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or its performance under or the enforcement of this Agreement.

Assignment.  This Agreement or any of the Parties’ rights and obligations can only be assigned, transferred or delegated (collectively “to assign” or “assignment”) with the other Party’s express prior written consent; provided that Researcher’s consent is not necessary if Colgate assigns to any of its Affiliates. When duly assigned, this Agreement shall be binding on each Party’s successors and assigns.

Time of the Essence.  Time is of the essence in the performance of this Agreement.

Counterparts. Each Party is permitted to deliver this Agreement to the other Party by sending a copy of their signed signature pages via facsimile or as an attachment in portable document format (PDF) or other email attachment format, e-signature, to an email addressed to the other Party.

Rules of Construction. Severability.  If any portion of this Agreement is to any extent determined to be illegal, invalid or unenforceable by a court or arbiter of competent jurisdiction, the remainder of this Agreement will not be affected and will remain valid and enforceable.  In addition, the affected portion of this Agreement will remain in effect in all circumstances other than the circumstances that caused the court or arbiter to find that part to be illegal, invalid or unenforceable.

GLOBAL ANTI-BRIBERY POLICY







Our Anti-Bribery Commitment



Colgate’s commitment to dealing legally and ethically applies worldwide.  We comply with all applicable anti-bribery laws, including but not limited to the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (“FCPA”), everywhere we do business, and we expect the same of the third parties with whom we  work.    While  the  FCPA  prohibits,  among  other  things,  bribery  of  foreign  government officials and entities, other anti-bribery laws, like the UK Bribery Act, prohibit commercial bribery between private individuals and entities.





Colgate people and any third parties acting on our behalf or in connection with our business are prohibited from giving or offering anything of value directly or indirectly to any government official or entity, or to any private individual or entity, in order to improperly obtain or retain any business advantage or to improperly affect any act or decision.





This prohibition includes any facilitating, expediting or “grease” payments made to government officials, either directly or indirectly, in order to expedite any official service or function (for example, small payments made to an official to move Colgate’s application to the front of the line or to shorten the time frame in which services or other actions are provided).  Any official fees supported by government-issued receipts do not qualify as improper payments.



Maintaining Accurate Books and Records



No payment by or on behalf of the Company shall be approved or made if any part of the payment is to be used for an unlawful or improper purpose, or for any purpose other than that described by valid documents supporting the payment.  No false or misleading entries should be made in any books or financial records of the Company for any reason.



Any expenses that an employee or third party incurs on Colgate’s behalf or in connection with our business shall not be reimbursable unless they are lawful and supported by detailed documentation including, for example, valid invoices or receipts.



Expenditures Related to Government Officials



No funds may be provided to or spent on behalf of a government official or entity, directly or indirectly, without advance written approval from Colgate’s Global Legal Organization.  This includes any payments, gifts, donations, entertainment, travel, meals, or other items of value. (For additional information, please review the Global Policy on Expenditures Related to Government Officials & Governments.)  Advance approval is not required for official fees supported by government-issued receipts (e.g., permit or license fees).



Please note that the term “government official” is widely defined and may include individuals who are employed by any public or state-affiliated institution or organization or who act in an official capacity in any way, whether full-time, part-time or unpaid.  Government officials can be found in every branch and level of government and public life and may include anyone from low-level customs employees, to employees of state-owned media outlets, to high-ranking lawmakers, as well as researchers, professors, teachers, dentists, veterinarians, or other professionals and Key Thought Leaders.  If you are in doubt as to whether an individual could be considered a government official, you should contact the Global Legal Organization.



Commercial Bribery



In addition to prohibiting bribery of government officials, Colgate also prohibits its employees and third parties from engaging in bribery of private parties.  You should not seek to improperly influence the judgment or conduct of any party with whom you might be conducting Company business by offering or providing any payments, gifts or other benefits, or by any other unlawful inducement.

Our Expectations



Colgate’s reputation depends on the conduct of our employees as well as the conduct of those with whom we do business.  It is our goal to ensure that Colgate People and the third parties with whom we work reflect the same high ethical standards and demonstrate a commitment to compliance with all applicable laws.  We further expect our third parties to ensure that their employees and subcontractors understand and comply with this Anti-Bribery Policy.

Failure to comply with this Anti-Bribery Policy or any applicable anti-bribery laws, including but not limited to the FCPA, may result in civil or criminal penalties, as well as termination of the employment or business relationship.













Any questions regarding this policy may be directed to our Global Compliance Legal Specialist: Legal_Compliance@colpal.com

JOINT DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT

This JOINT DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT is entered into as of the date of the last signature below (the “Effective Date”) by and between Colgate-Palmolive Company, a Delaware corporation, having its principal offices at 300 Park Avenue, New York, New York  10022 (“Colgate”), and [●], a [●] organized under the laws of [●], having its principal offices at [●] (“Company”).  Colgate and Company are sometimes hereinafter referred to collectively as the “Parties” and individually as a “Party.”

RECITALS

WHEREAS, Colgate and Company desire to collaborate to [●] (the “Purpose”); and

WHEREAS, Colgate and Company desire to enter into this Agreement to govern research and development activities related to, and the protection of confidential information and other proprietary materials, information and intellectual property developed during, such collaboration.

AGREEMENT

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the premises and the undertakings of the Parties hereinafter set forth, the Parties agree as follows:

DEFINITIONS

“Affiliate” means, with respect to a Person, an individual, trust, business trust, joint venture, partnership, corporation, association or any other entity which (directly or indirectly) is controlled by, controls, or is under common control with a Person.  For purposes of this definition, the term “control” (including, with correlative meanings, the term “controlled by” and “under common control with”) as used with respect to any Person, shall mean the possession (directly or indirectly) of power to direct or cause the direction of the management or policies of such Person.

“Agreement” means, as described in the preamble, this Joint Development Agreement.

“Background IP” means Intellectual Property under the control of a Party that was developed or acquired (other than from the other Party) by the Party prior to the Effective Date or independently and outside the activities contemplated by this Agreement without reference to or use of the other Party’s Confidential Information or Background IP. For purposes of this definition, a Party “controls” Intellectual Property if it owns or otherwise has the right to license or sublicense such Intellectual Property.

“Breaching Party” is defined in Section 11.2.1.

“Change of Control” means: (a) the acquisition of ownership, directly or indirectly, beneficially or of record, by any Person or group (within the meaning of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and the rules of the Securities and Exchange Commission thereunder as in effect on the date hereof), of Equity Interests representing more than fifteen percent (15%) of the aggregate ordinary voting power represented by the issued and outstanding Equity Interests of Company; (b) occupation of a majority of the seats (other than vacant seats) on the board of directors of Company by Persons who were neither (i) nominated by the board of directors of Company nor (ii) appointed by directors so nominated; (c) the acquisition of direct or indirect Control of Company by any Person or group; or (d) the transfer or assignment by Company of all or substantially all of its assets, or its rights or obligations under this Agreement, to another Person.

“Claims” is defined in Section 9.1.

“Colgate” is defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Colgate Confidential Information” means (a) any information or data, whether technical or nontechnical, whether written (including graphic or electronic) and marked confidential or oral, disclosed by Colgate or its Affiliates or on Colgate’s behalf to Company, either directly or indirectly, on or after the Effective Date [or previously under a Prior Non-Disclosure Agreement], and (b) the existence and terms of this Agreement.  If Colgate Confidential Information is disclosed orally, Colgate shall provide a summary and confirm the confidential nature of such information in writing within fifteen (15) days after such oral disclosure.  For the avoidance of doubt, Colgate Confidential Information shall include Materials, Deliverables and [●].

“Colgate Program Developments” means Program Developments that are based exclusively on Colgate Background IP or created exclusively by the Representatives of Colgate (without reference to any Company Background IP or Company Program Development).

“Commercially Reasonable Best Efforts” means, for each Party, efforts and resources comparable to those that would be employed by such Party to develop a product exclusively-owned by such Party that would have similar market potential at a similar stage in the product life cycle as the applicable product, [but in any event, no less than dedicating its highest level of skill and care to the Program.]

“Company” is defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Company Confidential Information” means (a) any information or data, whether technical or nontechnical, whether written (including graphic or electronic) and marked confidential or oral, disclosed by Company or its Affiliates or on Company’s behalf to Colgate, either directly or indirectly, on or after the Effective Date [or previously under a Prior Non-Disclosure Agreement], excluding all Colgate Confidential Information, and (b) the existence and terms of this Agreement.  If Company Confidential Information is disclosed orally, Company shall provide a summary and confirm the confidential nature of such information in writing within fifteen (15) days after such oral disclosure.

“Company Program Developments” mean Program Developments that are based exclusively on Company Background IP or created exclusively by the Representatives of Company (without reference to any Colgate Background IP or Colgate Program Development).

“Confidential Information” means Colgate Confidential Information or Company Confidential Information, as the context requires.

[“Company Market” means [●].]

[“Competitor” means any direct or indirect competitor of Colgate or its Affiliates, or any Affiliate of such a competitor.]

“Control” means the possession, directly or indirectly, of the power to direct or cause the direction of the management or policies of a Person, whether through the ability to exercise voting power, by contract or otherwise.  “Controlled” and “Controlling” shall have correlative meanings.

“Deliverables” is defined in Section 2.1.

“Development Plan” is defined in Section 2.1.

“Disclosing Party” means the Party disclosing Confidential Information.

“Effective Date” is defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Equity Interests” means shares of capital stock, partnership interests, membership interests in a limited liability company, beneficial interests in a trust or other equity ownership interests in a Person, and any warrants, options or other rights entitling the holder thereof to purchase or acquire any such equity interest.

“Force Majeure” is defined in Section 12.1.

“Governmental Authority” means any legislative, executive or judicial unit of any governmental or quasi-governmental authority or instrumentality (multi-national, national, federal, state, provincial, local or foreign, international or domestic), or any department, agency, board, bureau, commission, official or other regulatory, administrative or judicial authority thereof, including any administrative or regulatory agency or commission, and any court or arbitration tribunal, in each instance having jurisdiction over the subject matter before it.

“Indemnity Claim” is defined in Section 9.3.

“Intellectual Property” means all discoveries, inventions, improvements, developments, procedures, processes, formulations, know-how, trade secrets, formulae, trademarks, service marks, trade dress, designs, logos, packaging, proprietary information, technical information, techniques, works of authorship, drawings, models, manuals and systems, whether or not patentable or copyrightable or otherwise registerable, and all rights and applications or registrations derived or derivable therefrom.

“Joint Program Developments” mean Program Developments that are neither Colgate Program Developments nor Company Program Developments.

“Law” means all supranational, international, national, state and local laws, statutes, regulations, rules, codes or ordinances enacted, adopted, issued or promulgated by any Governmental Authority or common law.

“Material” means, for either Party, any tangible material, device, product or prototype.

“Milestone” shall mean an event or achievement associated with a specific date or outcome as set forth in Section 2.2.

“Nonbreaching Party” is defined in Section 11.2.1.

“Notice” is defined in Section 12.2.

“Oversight Committee” is defined in Section 3.1.1.

 “Party” and “Parties” are defined in the preamble to this Agreement.

“Person” means any natural person, corporation, limited liability company, trust, joint venture, association, company, partnership or other entity.

“Prior Non-Disclosure Agreements” mean [●].

“Program” means, collectively, the activities to be undertaken by the Parties pursuant to the Development Plan.

“Program Developments” mean Intellectual Property that is created by the Representatives of either or both Parties while performing work under this Agreement.

“Purpose” is defined in the recitals.

“Receiving Party” means the Party receiving Confidential Information.

“Representatives” means, for a Party, its directors, officers, employees, advisors or agents and the directors, officers, employees, advisors or agents of its Affiliates.

[“Rules” is defined in Section 12.5.2.]

“Target Product” means [●].

“Term” is defined in Section 11.1.

“Third Party” means any entity other than Company or Colgate or an Affiliate of either Party.

[“Trigger Event” means the occurrence of any of the following events: (a) Company’s termination of this Agreement pursuant to Section 11.2.3; (b) Company experiencing a Change of Control prior to the termination or expiration of this Agreement; or (c) Company materially breaching or otherwise being unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement, including under Section 12.1 (Force Majeure) of this Agreement, prior to the termination or expiration of this Agreement.]

GENERAL OBLIGATIONS

Development Plan.  All work and performance under this Agreement for joint development of the Target Product will be described in the development plan that (a) identifies the scope of work to be undertaken by each Party, (b) further describes the Target Product to be developed, (c) identifies the budget and payment obligations, (d) describes the deliverables (the “Deliverables”), (e) describes the schedule under which development is to be completed and the Deliverables to be provided and (f) specifies the minimum staffing (including percentage of effort) and project management to be provided by each Party (the “Development Plan”).  The Development Plan is set forth on Exhibit A.

Milestones.  The following table identifies the Milestones, the success criteria for each Milestone, the results of meeting the success criteria and the consequences, if any, for failure to meet the success criteria:

Performance of Obligations.  Each Party shall use its Commercially Reasonable Best Efforts to, and cause its Affiliates, Representatives and permitted subcontractors to, perform all of the tasks and obligations assigned to it under this Agreement, together with any tasks and obligations not specifically described in this Agreement but which are inherent in or a necessary part of the tasks and obligations described in this Agreement, or are reasonably required for proper performance of such tasks and obligations.

Subcontractors.  Neither Party may subcontract or engage any Third Party to perform any of its tasks or obligations hereunder, or consult with any Third Party regarding such tasks and obligations, unless: (a) the other Party provides written approval in advance; and (b) such Third Party enters into an agreement having commercial, Intellectual Property and confidentiality terms that are approved in writing by both Parties.  No such subcontracting shall relieve either Party of its obligations under this Agreement and each Party shall be responsible for the actions and inactions of all of its permitted subcontractors as if such actions and inactions were committed by such Party.

Exclusivity.   During the Term and for [●] years thereafter, Company shall not (and shall cause its Affiliates not to), itself or in collaboration or pursuant to a contract or agreement with or for the benefit of any Third Party, engage in, undertake or otherwise pursue the discovery, research, development, supply, sale, offer for sale or commercialization of any product that competes, directly or indirectly, with the Target Product.

MANAGEMENT OF THE PROGRAM

Oversight Committee.

Establishment.  The Parties shall establish an oversight committee (the “Oversight Committee”) to oversee and manage the Program and to discuss operational issues and disputes.  The Oversight Committee will be composed of two (2) members with one representative appointed by each of Company and Colgate.  Both representatives will be employees of either Company or Colgate, as the case may be.  Either Party may replace its representative at any time by providing written notice to the other Party.

Responsibilities.  The Oversight Committee shall perform the following functions: 

coordinate and carry out, or cause the applicable Party’s Representatives and permitted subcontractors to carry out, the activities of the Parties hereunder to ensure timely implementation of this Agreement;

review the Milestones and confirm that the Parties are meeting all technical, commercial and financial requirements of this Agreement; 

settle operational disputes and disagreements; provided, however, that if the Oversight Committee is unable to settle any such disputes or disagreements, the dispute resolution procedure set forth in Section 12.5 below shall be invoked;

discuss the regulatory classification of the Target Products and other products that are the subject of the Agreement; 

discuss regulatory responsibilities, if any, related to this Agreement; 

discuss the possible allocation of costs and expenses under this Agreement; and 

perform such other functions as are appropriate to further the Purpose as determined by the Parties. 

Meetings.  The Oversight Committee will meet at least [●], or more frequently as agreed by the Oversight Committee.  The sites of the meetings shall alternate between the principal offices of the Parties unless otherwise agreed.  By mutual agreement of the Parties, meetings of the Oversight Committee may be held by videoconference or telephone conference.

On-Site Participation by Employees.  While at the offices or facilities of a Party, the other Party’s Representatives shall have access to such areas as are reasonably related to the implementation of the Development Plan, such as laboratories and designated office space, as well as food-service and public areas or as otherwise authorized by such Party, and shall comply with all applicable policies and procedures of such Party (including security policies and procedures) as provided to such other Party’s Representatives in writing.

COSTS AND EXPENSES

Internal Costs.  Except as otherwise set forth in the Development Plan, all direct and indirect costs and expenses (including any travel costs, legal and other advisory fees) in connection with this Agreement incurred by a Party or its Representatives shall be borne solely by such Party, and the other Party shall have no obligation to reimburse such Party for any such costs or expenses.  In case the Development Plan sets forth that specific expenses or costs will be repaid by a Party to the other Party, such expenses or costs must be supported by detailed documentation including, for example, valid invoices or receipts.  

Third-Party Costs.  Unless otherwise set forth in the Development Plan, if, subject to Section 2.4, any Party engages any Third Party to perform any obligations related to this Agreement or otherwise purchases any products or services from a Third Party in connection with this Agreement, all payments to such Third Party shall be borne solely by such engaging or purchasing Party, and the other Party shall have no obligation to reimburse such Party for any such payments.

COMMERCIALIZATION

If Colgate desires to commercialize any Target Product [or any other product developed pursuant to this Agreement], the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to enter into a definitive agreement setting forth the terms and conditions upon which Colgate may so commercialize such Target Product [or such product].

INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

Background IP.  All Background IP shall be and remain exclusively the property of the Party that made or acquired such Background IP.  Except as set forth in Article 7, neither Party has any right or license to any of the other Party’s Background IP.

Program Developments.

Colgate Program Developments.  Colgate shall exclusively own all right, title and interest in and to all Colgate Program Developments.  Company hereby assigns, and shall cause its Affiliates and its and their Representatives and contractors to assign, to Colgate the entire right, title and interest in and to all Colgate Program Developments.  If Company is not permitted by applicable Law to assign a Colgate Program Development to Colgate, Company hereby grants Colgate a perpetual, irrevocable, exclusive (even as to Company), world-wide, royalty-free, freely-assignable license in all fields to such Colgate Program Development (including the right to sell and grant sublicenses to such Colgate Program Development) and agrees not to bring any action, claim or proceeding against Colgate or any of its sublicensees or assignees for its use or exploitation of such Colgate Program Development.  Subject to Section 6.2.5, Colgate shall have the exclusive right to prepare applications for, prosecute, maintain and defend, at its own costs, the Colgate Program Developments.  Company shall reasonably assist and cooperate with Colgate at Colgate’s expense in perfecting, maintaining and defending the rights granted to Colgate in this Section 6.2.1, including the provision of any requested documentation necessary for prosecution or maintenance of patents claiming such Colgate Program Developments, and the execution of any required documents therefor. While  the  FCPA  prohibits,  among  other  things,  bribery  of  foreign  government officials and entities, other anti-bribery laws, like the UK Bribery Act, prohibit commercial bribery between private individuals and entities.





Colgate people and any third parties acting on our behalf or in connection with our business are prohibited from giving or offering anything of value directly or indirectly to any government official or entity, or to any private individual or entity, in order to improperly obtain or retain any business advantage or to improperly affect any act or decision.





This prohibition includes any facilitating, expediting or “grease” payments made to government officials, either directly or indirectly, in order to expedite any official service or function (for example, small payments made to an official to move Colgate’s application to the front of the line or to shorten the time frame in which services or other actions are provided).  Any official fees supported by government-issued receipts do not qualify as improper payments.



Maintaining Accurate Books and Records



No payment by or on behalf of the Company shall be approved or made if any part of the payment is to be used for an unlawful or improper purpose, or for any purpose other than that described by valid documents supporting the payment.  No false or misleading entries should be made in any books or financial records of the Company for any reason.



Any expenses that an employee or third party incurs on Colgate’s behalf or in connection with our business shall not be reimbursable unless they are lawful and supported by detailed documentation including, for example, valid invoices or receipts.



Expenditures Related to Government Officials



No funds may be provided to or spent on behalf of a government official or entity, directly or indirectly, without advance written approval from Colgate’s Global Legal Organization.  This includes any payments, gifts, donations, entertainment, travel, meals, or other items of value. (For additional information, please review the Global Policy on Expenditures Related to Government Officials & Governments.)  Advance approval is not required for official fees supported by government-issued receipts (e.g., permit or license fees).



Please note that the term “government official” is widely defined and may include individuals who are employed by any public or state-affiliated institution or organization or who act in an official capacity in any way, whether full-time, part-time or unpaid.  Government officials can be found in every branch and level of government and public life and may include anyone from low-level customs employees, to employees of state-owned media outlets, to high-ranking lawmakers, as well as researchers, professors, teachers, dentists, veterinarians, or other professionals and Key Thought Leaders.  If you are in doubt as to whether an individual could be considered a government official, you should contact the Global Legal Organization.



Commercial Bribery



In addition to prohibiting bribery of government officials, Colgate also prohibits its employees and third parties from engaging in bribery of private parties.  You should not seek to improperly influence the judgment or conduct of any party with whom you might be conducting Company business by offering or providing any payments, gifts or other benefits, or by any other unlawful inducement.



Our Expectations



Colgate’s reputation depends on the conduct of our employees as well as the conduct of those with whom we do business.  It is our goal to ensure that Colgate People and the third parties with whom we work reflect the same high ethical standards and demonstrate a commitment to compliance with all applicable laws.  We further expect our third parties to ensure that their employees and subcontractors understand and comply with this Anti-Bribery Policy.

Failure to comply with this Anti-Bribery Policy or any applicable anti-bribery laws, including but not limited to the FCPA, may result in civil or criminal penalties, as well as termination of the employment or business relationship.













Any questions regarding this policy may be directed to our Global Compliance Legal Specialist: Legal_Compliance@colpal.com
